Water in Your Fort Myers Home Right Now? Do This First
Make it safe. If water is near outlets, cords, a light fixture or a sagging ceiling, switch off that circuit at the breaker and keep people and pets out. Never stand in water to reach the electrical panel.
Stop the source. Close the valve behind the toilet, sink or washer, or shut the main valve, usually near the meter or where the line enters the house, often in the garage. For an AC leak, turn the system off at the thermostat.
Photograph everything. Take photos and video of the water, the source, wet walls, ceilings, floors and damaged belongings before anything is moved or thrown out.
Move what you can. Lift rugs, electronics, papers, photos and boxes off wet floors, and set furniture legs on foil, plastic lids or wood blocks.
Let air move. If it is safe and the water is clean, open interior doors and run the AC to pull humidity out. Keep the AC off if sewage or floodwater is involved.
Start drying the same day. Wet drywall, carpet pad and baseboards rarely dry on their own in Fort Myers humidity, and mold can begin growing within 24 to 48 hours.
What not to do
Don't use a household vacuum on standing water.
Don't turn on ceiling fans or lights in a room with a wet or bulging ceiling.
Don't walk through sewage or floodwater without boots and gloves.
Don't throw away damaged items before they are photographed.
Don't paint over a water stain until you know the wall behind it is dry.
Need every step? Use the first-hour water damage checklist .

What Kind of Water Damage Is in Your Fort Myers Home?
Pick what matches what you are seeing. Each page explains the usual cause, what gets dried or removed and what to ask your insurer.
AC leaking from the air handler or through the ceiling
A clogged condensate drain line is one of the most common causes of indoor water damage in Southwest Florida. The AC tech clears the line, but the wet drywall, insulation and flooring around it still need drying. See AC leak water damage .
Water dripping from the ceiling or a stain that keeps spreading
Usually an attic air handler, a roof leak after a storm or a bathroom above. Turn off power to that room before you look closer. See ceiling leak water damage .
Water coming in from the condo above
In Florida condos, responsibility is split between the association and the unit owners. Photograph your unit before anything is removed and notify the association in writing. See condo water damage .
Sewage or a drain backing up
Toilet, tub and floor-drain backups are Category 3 water. Carpet, pad and drywall it touches usually have to be removed, not dried. See sewage backup cleanup.
Sewer smell or slow drains in an older home
Many Lee County homes built before about 1975 have cast iron drain lines that crack and corrode under the slab. See cast iron pipe water damage .
Burst pipe or split supply line
Braided toilet, sink and ice maker lines can fail without warning and keep running until someone shuts the valve. See burst pipe water damage .
Water heater leaking in the garage or closet
Older tanks rust through at the bottom and soak the garage, the laundry room or the hallway carpet. See water heater leak cleanup .
Dishwasher, washer, fridge or ice maker leak
Appliance leaks often run slowly under cabinets and flooring for days before anyone sees them. See appliance leak water damage .
Warm spots on the floor, wet baseboards or a jump in the water bill
These are common signs of a leak under the slab. A plumber finds and repairs the pipe; the floors and walls around it still need drying. See slab leak water damage .
Came back to a wet or musty seasonal home
A failed AC, a leaking water heater or a split supply line can run for weeks while nobody is home. See water damage in vacant homes .
Soft or wet floor in a mobile home
Particle board subfloors and belly wrap hold water out of sight, so manufactured homes need a different drying approach than a slab house. See mobile home water damage .
Floodwater or storm surge
Rising water is Category 3. It usually means flood cuts in the drywall and a claim under a separate flood policy. See flood and storm cleanup.
Wet floors or swollen kitchen cabinets
Laminate and vinyl plank trap water underneath, and particle board cabinet bases swell fast. Some can be saved if they are dried early. See water damaged floors and water damaged kitchen cabinets .

Signs of Hidden Water Damage in Fort Myers Slab Homes
Water rarely stays where you first see it. On a slab home it spreads sideways under flooring and behind baseboards. Watch for these signs, especially after an AC leak or a storm:
Baseboards that are swollen, pulling away from the wall or soft at the bottom.
Grout lines that stay dark long after mopping, or tiles that sound hollow when tapped.
Laminate or vinyl plank that is cupping, lifting at the seams or feels spongy.
Paint that bubbles or peels, or drywall that feels cool and soft to the touch.
A musty smell that gets stronger when the AC runs or the house is closed up.
Brown rings or spots on the ceiling near the air handler, a bathroom or an outside wall.
Interior doors that suddenly stick, or carpet that feels damp near a wall.
A water bill that is higher than usual with no change in how you use water.
If you notice two or more of these, the water has probably traveled further than it looks. Moisture meters and a thermal camera show exactly where it went.
Services
How Fort Myers Homes Are Built, and Why It Changes the Drying
Most homes in Fort Myers are not built like homes up north. Block walls, slabs, condo stacks and manufactured homes each hide water in a different place, so each one is dried a different way.
How the home is built Where the water hides How it gets dried
Concrete block walls with stucco Interior drywall usually sits on wood furring strips over the block, so water wicks into the gap behind the drywall and stays against the block Baseboards come off and the bottom of the wall is opened so air reaches the cavity; block and furring strips are read separately
Slab-on-grade with tile or vinyl plank Water runs under the flooring along the slab and shows up rooms away from the leak The whole slab is moisture-mapped; tile usually stays in place, plank often comes up
Wood-frame second floors and additions Water drops through the ceiling and runs down inside wall cavities Ceilings and walls are opened only where readings show water
Condo mid-rises and towers A leak in one unit travels down plumbing and AC chases into the units below Units above and below are checked, and the association is brought in early
Manufactured homes Particle board subfloor soaks up water, and water pools inside the belly wrap The belly is opened and dried from below; soft subfloor is replaced
This is why two leaks of the same size can take very different drying plans. The readings, not the look of the room, decide what stays and what goes.

How Water Damage Restoration Works in Fort Myers, Step by Step
1 You call and describe what you see
Tell us where the water came from, which rooms are affected and whether it is clean water, a drain backup or floodwater. We walk you through making the area safe and confirm timing with you before anyone heads out.
2 Inspection and moisture mapping
Moisture meters and thermal imaging trace how far the water traveled behind baseboards, under tile and up inside walls. The readings are recorded and become the starting point for the drying plan.
3 Water removal
Standing water is extracted, and soaked carpet pad and anything that cannot be saved are removed. With contaminated water, affected materials come out under containment.
4 Drying and daily monitoring
Dehumidifiers and air movers run around the clock. Moisture readings are taken and logged as the job goes on, and equipment is adjusted until materials reach normal dry readings, not just until surfaces feel dry.
5 Cleaning, records and repair planning
Affected areas are cleaned and treated, and you get the photos and moisture logs. Then you decide who rebuilds the drywall, baseboards, flooring and cabinets.
Most clean-water jobs take about 3 to 5 days to dry. Concrete slabs, hardwood, tile on slab and sewage jobs usually take longer.

What Fort Myers Homes Can Dry in Place and What Has to Go
Whether a material can be saved depends on the type of water, how long it sat and what the material is made of. This is the general rule of thumb:
Material Clean water, caught early Sewage or floodwater
Drywall Often dried in place if it is not swollen or crumbling Usually cut out above the wet line (a flood cut)
Baseboards Often removed carefully so the wall behind can dry, then reused Usually replaced
Carpet Sometimes dried and cleaned Removed
Carpet pad Usually replaced because it soaks up water like a sponge Removed
Tile on slab Usually dried in place; the slab under it takes time Cleaned and sanitized; grout may need attention
Laminate and vinyl plank Often has to be lifted so water underneath can dry Removed
Hardwood Can sometimes be dried with specialty mats if started early Usually removed
Cabinets Toe kicks pulled so the base can dry; swollen particle board is replaced Lower cabinets usually removed
Insulation Wet batt insulation is usually replaced Removed
Speed is the biggest factor you control. The sooner drying starts, the more of your home stays in place.

Clean Water, Gray Water or Sewage in Your Fort Myers Home?
The water category decides what can be saved, how the work is done and how careful you need to be around it.
Category What it means Fort Myers examples What usually happens
1, Clean Water from a clean source Supply line, water heater, AC condensate, rain before it touches the ground Often dried in place if handled quickly
2, Gray Some contamination Washing machine, dishwasher, toilet overflow without waste Carpet pad and some drywall usually removed; antimicrobial applied
3, Black Heavy contamination Sewage backup, cracked cast iron drain, floodwater, storm surge Porous materials removed; protective gear; children and pets kept away
Clean water does not stay clean. After a day or two in contact with flooring, dust and building materials it can become Category 2, which is one more reason not to wait.

Sewer Backup in Fort Myers: Your Line or the Utility's?
When sewage comes up through a tub or floor drain, the first question is where the blockage is. That decides who clears it.
The lateral is yours. The pipe that runs from your house to the sewer main is generally the property owner's to clear and repair, including roots and grease buildup.
The main is the utility's. The main in the street belongs to the City of Fort Myers or Lee County Utilities, depending on your address.
Check the neighbors. If homes on both sides are backing up too, the problem is probably the main. Call your utility first.
Check the cleanout. The cleanout is a capped pipe in the yard near the house. If it is full of sewage, the blockage is past it, toward the street. If it is empty, the clog is inside the house plumbing. Let a plumber open it if you are not sure; a cleanout under pressure can spray.
Stop using water. No flushing, showers, laundry or dishwasher until the line is cleared. Every gallon you send down comes back up somewhere.
Services
Why Water Damage Spreads Faster in Fort Myers and Lee County
Humidity. Fort Myers air stays humid most of the year, so wet materials barely dry on their own and mold gets ideal conditions.
The AC almost never stops. Months of constant cooling produce a lot of condensate, and every clogged drain line is a chance for it to overflow into a closet, ceiling or hallway.
Slab-on-grade construction. Water spreads under tile, vinyl plank and baseboards instead of draining away, so the wet area is usually bigger than it looks.
Aging drain lines. Older homes in parts of Fort Myers and Cape Coral still have cast iron drains that crack under the slab.

Water Damage Through the Year in Fort Myers
The calls change with the seasons here. Knowing what each part of the year brings tells you what to check.
Time of year What Fort Myers homes see most What to check
Winter and spring (dry season) Seasonal residents come back to leaks that ran while the house was empty; water heaters and supply lines fail Walk the house before unpacking: ceilings, the AC closet, under every sink and the water heater pan
Summer rainy season (about June to September) Afternoon downpours, roof and window leaks, and AC units running hardest with clogged drain lines The AC drain line and float switch, ceiling stains near the air handler, windows on the storm side of the house
Hurricane season (June 1 to November 30) Storm surge, wind-driven rain through stucco and windows, and power loss that stops the AC and pumps A flood policy in place, photos of the home before a storm, and a plan to shut off water and power

Rebuilding in a Fort Myers Flood Zone: The 50% Rule
If your home or business sits in a FEMA flood zone that starts with A or V, there is one more step before the rebuild. Building departments in Lee County check repair permits against the "50% rule", also called substantial damage.
What it means. If the repairs needed to bring the building back to its pre-damage condition add up to 50% or more of the building's market value, the building has to be brought into full compliance with current flood rules, which can mean raising it.
Any kind of damage counts. Lee County applies the rule to damage of any origin, so wind, fire and large leaks count, not only floodwater.
Your own work counts. The rule applies even if you do the work yourself or others donate the labor and materials.
Repairs add up. Lee County evaluates repair permits from the same damage event together, not one at a time.
An elevation certificate can settle it. A building that already meets current flood rules can be repaired without the 50% limit, and Lee County may already have the certificate on file.
Who decides. The building department that issues your permit (the City of Fort Myers, Lee County or your town) makes the call. Ask them before you plan the rebuild.
The photos, moisture logs and written scope from the water damage job become part of the paper trail for both the permit and any claim, so keep them together.
Services
Do You Need a Restoration Company in Fort Myers, or Can You Handle It Yourself?
Not every leak needs professional equipment. You can usually handle it yourself if:
A small amount of clean water landed on tile or another hard surface and was wiped up within minutes.
Nothing soaked into carpet, walls, cabinets or the floor underneath.
There is no musty smell over the next few days.
It is time to call for help if:
Water got under flooring, behind baseboards or into drywall or cabinets.
A ceiling is stained, wet or sagging.
The water came from a toilet, drain, sewer line or flood.
More than one room is affected, or you are not sure where the water came from.
The house sat closed up with water in it for a day or more.
Someone in the home has asthma, allergies or a weakened immune system.
If you are not sure, call 239-356-3708 and describe what you see. If fans and a wet vac will handle it, we will tell you that.

Condo Water Damage in Fort Myers: Who Handles What
Water from the unit above is one of the most common condo calls in Fort Myers, and it involves more people than a house leak. Take these steps in order:
1 Stop the source. Knock on the unit above. If no one is home, call the association or building manager to shut off the water to that unit.
2 Photograph before cleanup. Take photos and video of the ceiling, walls, floors and anything damaged in your unit.
3 Notify the association in writing. Note the date, the time and where the water came in.
4 Call your HO-6 insurer or agent. Under Florida Statute 718.111(11), the association's master policy generally covers the building as originally installed, while floor, wall and ceiling coverings, built-in cabinets and countertops, appliances, water heaters and electrical fixtures inside your unit are generally the unit owner's to insure.
5 Dry every affected unit. Water often reaches the unit below yours and the walls shared with neighbors. Drying only one unit leaves wet material behind the shared walls.
Services
Water Damage in Fort Myers Businesses and Vacation Rentals
A business or a rental has two problems at once: the water, and the days the space can't be used.
Businesses. Restaurants, medical and dental offices, retail stores and warehouses get drying plans built around opening hours, with equipment placed so parts of the space can stay open where it is safe.
Vacation rentals. A leak found at checkout means guests arriving in a day or two. You get photos and moisture readings you can share with the owner, the property manager and the insurer, plus a clear answer on when the unit can be booked again.
Property managers. One call covers the unit with the leak and the units around it, with readings for each so nothing gets missed behind shared walls.
Services
Water Damage and Insurance in Fort Myers: What Florida Homeowners Should Know
This is general information, not advice about your policy. Many policies cover water damage that is sudden and accidental, like a burst supply line or an AC overflow. Every policy is different, so read yours and talk to your agent or insurer.
Sudden vs. gradual. Damage from long-term seepage or a leak that went on for months is often excluded. Report the date you found the damage truthfully.
Flood is separate. Rising water and storm surge are covered by a flood policy (NFIP or private), not standard homeowners coverage. NFIP policies generally have a 30-day waiting period, so buy before hurricane season, not during it.
Condos split coverage. Florida Statute 718.111(11) divides responsibility between the association's master policy and the unit owner's HO-6 policy.
Assignment of benefits is gone. For policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, Florida no longer allows post-loss assignment of benefits, so the agreement for the work stays between you and the company you hire.
Deadlines apply. You generally have one year from the date of loss to give your insurer notice of a new claim, and insurers generally must pay or deny within 60 days of notice.
Mold is limited. Mold coverage is often capped, and Florida has its own rules for who can perform mold assessment and remediation.
Prevent further damage. Most policies expect you to take reasonable steps to stop the damage from getting worse, so start drying and keep your receipts.
Check for a water damage cap. Some Florida policies limit plumbing-leak water damage to a fixed amount per loss through a limited water damage endorsement. Look for it on your declarations page or ask your agent.
More detail: how insurance handles water damage in Florida .

How to Prevent the Next Leak in Your Fort Myers Home
Most of the water damage we see in Lee County starts with something small that could have been caught early.
AC drain line. Have the condensate line cleared at every AC service, and make sure the unit has a float switch that shuts it off when the drain pan fills.
Supply lines. Check the braided lines under sinks and toilets and behind the washer and fridge. Replace any that bulge, rust or kink.
Water heater. Look for rust or moisture at the base. Tank water heaters usually wear out somewhere around 8 to 12 years.
Leak sensors and shut-off valves. Small sensors under sinks, the water heater and the AC closet send an alert to your phone. An automatic shut-off valve closes the main when it senses a leak.
Before you leave for the season. Shut off the main water valve and the water heater, leave the AC on to control humidity, and have someone walk the house regularly while you are away.
Before hurricane season. Photograph every room and your belongings, find your main shut-off valve, and check that your flood coverage is in place.

Questions Fort Myers Homeowners Ask
Who do I call first when water is coming into my house?
Stop the water at the fixture or main shut-off first. Then call 239-356-3708 to remove the water and dry the structure, a plumber to repair the pipe or fixture, and your insurer or agent to report the damage.
What does water damage restoration include?
Everything from the first call to a dry, clean structure: emergency water removal, moisture mapping with meters and a thermal camera, structural drying with daily readings, cleaning and antimicrobial treatment where needed, and photos and moisture logs for your records and your insurer. The rebuild of drywall, flooring and cabinets comes after, and who does it is your choice.
Should I turn off my AC after a leak?
If the AC itself is leaking, yes, turn it off at the thermostat until the drain line is cleared. If the leak came from somewhere else and the water is clean, running the AC helps pull moisture out of the air. After sewage or floodwater, keep it off so contaminated air is not spread through the ducts.
How long does it take to dry out a house after a leak?
Most clean-water jobs take about 3 to 5 days with dehumidifiers and air movers running around the clock. Concrete slabs, hardwood and sewage jobs take longer. A house is dry when moisture readings are back to normal, not when surfaces feel dry.
How can I tell if my walls are still wet inside?
You often can't by touch alone. Drywall can feel dry on the surface while the bottom few inches and the framing behind it are still wet. A moisture meter or a thermal camera is the reliable way to check.
How do I choose a water damage company in Fort Myers?
Ask whether the technicians are IICRC-trained, whether they take moisture readings and share the logs, and whether you get a written scope before any work beyond emergency water removal. A good company photographs the damage before anything is torn out and leaves the choice of repair contractor with you. Be wary of anyone who asks you to sign over your insurance benefits: for Florida policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, post-loss assignment of benefits isn't allowed.
What causes most water damage in Fort Myers homes?
Clogged AC condensate lines are one of the most common causes, followed by split supply lines under sinks and toilets, failing water heaters, roof and window leaks in summer storms, appliance leaks and, in older homes, cracked cast iron drains under the slab.
What should I do with wet carpet?
Pull it back from the wall if you can and get air under it. Carpet pad soaks up water and is usually replaced. Carpet touched by sewage or floodwater should be removed, not dried.
Do I have to use the company my insurer recommends?
Usually not. You can generally choose your own restoration company unless your policy includes a managed repair program you agreed to. Check your policy before you sign anything.
Does the 50% rule apply to my Fort Myers home?
Only if the building is in a flood zone that starts with A or V. Your building department compares the repair total with the building's market value when you apply for permits.
How fast can someone get to my Fort Myers home?
The call is answered 24/7, and you're told the timing before anyone heads out. Arrival depends on where you are in Lee County, the time of day and how many calls are coming in, which climbs after a big storm. While you wait, you get clear steps to make the area safe and keep the damage from spreading.
Do you handle condos, mobile homes and businesses?
Yes. Condos and townhomes, manufactured homes, vacation rentals, seasonal homes and businesses each hide water in different places, so each one gets a drying plan built around how it is put together.
What should I do before leaving my Fort Myers home for the summer?
Shut off the main water valve and the water heater, leave the AC running to control humidity, and have someone walk the house regularly while you're away. A leak in an empty home can run for weeks before anyone sees it.
Is there 24-hour water damage help near me in Fort Myers?
Yes. 239-356-3708 is answered 24/7, including nights, weekends and holidays, for Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Lehigh Acres, North Fort Myers, Fort Myers Beach, Estero and Bonita Springs.

Key facts about water removal in Fort Myers
Extraction removes the liquid water. Structural drying removes the water that has already soaked into drywall, slab, baseboards and cabinets.
Clean water can turn into contaminated Category 2 water within about 24 to 48 hours, and mold can start growing in the same window in Florida humidity.
Most Lee County homes sit on concrete slabs, so water spreads sideways under flooring instead of draining away.
Water from a toilet, drain or flood is Category 3 and is handled with protective gear and removal of porous materials.

Water Spreading in Your Fort Myers Home Right Now? Do This First
Cut the power. Switch off the breaker to any room where water reaches outlets, cords or appliances. Never stand in water to reach the panel.
Stop the source. Close the valve behind the toilet, sink or washer, or shut the main valve, usually where the line enters the house, often in the garage. For an AC overflow, turn the system off at the thermostat.
Photograph everything. Take photos and video of the water, the source and every wet room before anything is moved.
Lift what you can. Get rugs, electronics, papers, photos and small furniture out of the water. Put furniture legs on foil or plastic lids.
Skip the household vacuum. It isn't built for water and can shock you.
Stay out of dirty water. If the water came from a toilet, a drain or outside, keep out of it and keep children and pets away.

What to Have Ready When You Call for Water Removal in Fort Myers
A two-minute call gets the right equipment to the right door. Have these answers ready:
Where the water is coming from, and whether it is stopped.
Which rooms and floors are wet, and roughly when it started.
Whether the water is clean, from a toilet or drain, or from outside.
Whether the power is off in the wet rooms.
The gate code or guard house instructions if you live in a gated community.
For a condo: the building manager's or association's number, and the unit above or below yours.
Pets in the home, and where the crew can park close to the door.
If you don't know some of it, call anyway. Every call to 239-356-3708 is answered 24/7.

What Happens During Emergency Water Removal in Fort Myers?
Emergency water removal follows the same order on almost every job: make it safe, find the water, take it out, remove what can't be saved and set up drying.
1 Safety and source check
The water source is confirmed stopped, power to wet areas is confirmed off and the water category is identified: clean (Category 1), gray (Category 2) or black (Category 3).
2 Moisture mapping
Moisture meters and a thermal imaging camera show how far the water traveled under tile and vinyl plank, behind baseboards, under cabinets and up into the bottom of the drywall. The wet area is almost always bigger than the puddle.
3 Water extraction
Truck-mounted or portable extractors pull standing water and the water held in carpet. Weighted extraction tools press out water that a wand alone leaves behind in carpet and pad. Submersible pumps handle deep water in garages or after storms.
4 Removal of what can't be saved
Soaked carpet pad, swollen particle board, wet insulation and anything touched by sewage are usually removed, photographed and listed for your records and your insurer.
5 Drying setup
Dehumidifiers and air movers are placed and the first moisture readings are logged. From here the job becomes structural drying, which runs until the materials reach normal dry readings.
Services
How Fast Does Water Need to Come Out of a Fort Myers Home?
The sooner, the better. Every hour water sits, it wicks higher into drywall and deeper under flooring, and more material has to be removed later.
Time since the leak What is happening inside the house
First few hours Water runs under baseboards and flooring; drywall starts wicking water upward
24 to 48 hours Clean water can become Category 2; mold can begin in Florida humidity; odors start
2 to 7 days Particle board and MDF swell for good; laminate and vinyl plank cup or lift; a musty smell sets in
Weeks Mold behind walls and under flooring becomes likely; framing and subfloors can be affected
A floor can look dry while the slab and the bottom of the walls are still wet. That is why measured readings matter more than how a surface feels.
Services
What Equipment Is Used for Water Extraction in Fort Myers Homes?
Truck-mounted extractors: the strongest suction, used for large areas and deep carpet in single-family homes.
Portable extractors: for condos, upper floors, gated communities and tight spaces a truck hose can't reach.
Submersible pumps: for deep standing water in garages, lanais or ground floors after heavy rain.
Weighted extraction tools: press water out of carpet and pad.
Moisture meters and thermal cameras: find water you can't see behind walls and under floors.
Dehumidifiers and air movers: start pulling moisture out of the air and the structure once the liquid water is gone.
The more water extraction removes, the shorter the drying stage and the less tear-out the house needs.

What You Get After Water Removal in Fort Myers
The paperwork from the first visit matters as much as the extraction. It shows your insurer, your adjuster and, in a flood zone, your building department exactly what happened and why.
Photos of every wet room before anything is moved, and again after extraction.
A moisture map showing where readings were taken and how wet each spot was.
A list of materials removed, such as carpet pad, baseboards or the bottom of the drywall, with photos taken before they leave the house.
A list of belongings that were moved, stored or set aside for disposal.
The first drying readings and the equipment placed in each room.
A written scope before any work beyond emergency water removal.
Keep these together. They answer most of the questions that come later about the claim and the repairs.

Can You Remove the Water Yourself With a Shop Vac in Fort Myers?
Sometimes. A wet vac, towels and fans can handle a small clean-water spill on tile that you caught right away. It usually isn't enough when:
The water sat for more than a few hours or reached more than one room.
It ran under tile, vinyl plank, laminate, cabinets or baseboards.
The water came from a toilet, a drain, a sewer line or floodwater.
Drywall feels soft, paint is bubbling or baseboards are swelling.
You notice a musty smell a day or two later.
The water you can see is rarely the problem. The water inside walls and under flooring is what turns into swelling and mold later.

It depends on the water category, how long the water sat and the material. As a general rule:
Material Clean water, caught early Sewage or floodwater

What Happens to Furniture and Belongings During Water Removal in Fort Myers?
Contents are handled alongside the water, not after it. On most jobs:
Furniture is lifted onto blocks or foil tabs, or moved to a dry room, so the legs don't wick water or stain the carpet.
The most fragile things move first. Rugs, boxes, papers, photos and electronics are moved before anything else, because they are the most likely to be ruined by sitting water.
Everything is photographed and listed before anything is thrown away, so your insurer can see what was damaged. Keep a sample of the carpet and pad if your adjuster hasn't seen them.
Pack-outs for bigger jobs. When several rooms are affected or repairs will take weeks, contents may be boxed, listed and stored off-site, then brought back once the rooms are rebuilt.
Sewage and floodwater change the rules. Porous items such as mattresses, upholstered furniture and stuffed toys usually can't be made safe and are listed for disposal; hard items can often be cleaned and disinfected.
Wet papers and photos can sometimes be saved by freezing them until they can be dried properly. Don't pull apart stuck photos while they are wet.
Ask what will be moved, stored or thrown out before it happens, and keep your own list.

Where the water came from decides how it is handled. These are the calls that come in most often across Lee County:
Where the water came from Water category What the first visit usually involves Read more
Split supply line under a sink, toilet or ice maker Category 1 if caught early Extraction, baseboards checked, cabinet toe kicks pulled Burst pipe water damage

Water Removal in Fort Myers Block Homes, Condos, Garages and Lanais
Concrete block homes
Drywall in most Fort Myers homes is fastened to wood furring strips over concrete block. Water that gets behind the baseboard sits in that gap, against the block, where an extractor can't reach it. Pulling the baseboard and checking the cavity with a meter is part of the first visit.
Tile on slab
Tile usually stays, but water works its way under loose or hollow-sounding tiles and into the grout. Extraction takes what is on top; the slab underneath is dried and checked with readings over the following days.
Condos
Upper-floor units usually need portable equipment, and the water may already be in the unit below. Tell building management right away so a shared riser or the unit above can be shut off, and photograph both units.
Garages
Water heaters and washers often sit in the garage. Water on a garage slab runs under the door into the house and soaks the bottom of the shared wall and anything stored on the floor.
Lanais and sliding doors
During heavy summer storms, wind-driven rain can push under sliders and lanai thresholds into living areas. Rainwater that touched the ground outside is treated as contaminated.
Mobile and manufactured homes
Water runs under the floor into the belly wrap and particle board subfloor, where it can't be seen. See mobile home water damage .
Services
Water Removal After a Storm or Flood in Lee County
After hurricanes and heavy rain, many Lee County homes have rising water at floor level and roof leaks overhead at the same time. Floodwater and storm surge are Category 3, so removal comes with flood cuts, disinfection and drying.
Wait until officials say it is safe to go back in.
Keep the power off if water reached outlets or the electrical panel.
Never run a generator inside the house, in the garage or near open windows.
Photograph everything, inside and out, before you start.
Keep children and pets out of rooms that took in floodwater.
Services
Saltwater Storm Surge: Why Water Removal Is Different Near the Gulf
Storm surge in Lee County is salt or brackish water pushed in from the Gulf, up the Caloosahatchee and into the back bays. Homes on Fort Myers Beach, along the river and on Cape Coral canals are the most exposed. Surge does more than wet the house:
Mud and silt come with it. Surge leaves a layer of mud that has to be shoveled and washed out before extraction can finish.
Salt stays behind. Salt left in drywall, wood and insulation keeps pulling moisture from humid air, so porous materials the surge touched are usually removed rather than dried.
Surfaces get washed, not just dried. Studs, block walls and the slab are cleaned and rinsed to take off salt and silt before drying starts.
Metal corrodes fast. Outlets, wiring, the electrical panel, AC equipment and appliances that sat in saltwater corrode quickly. Have a qualified electrician check them before the power goes back on.
If surge reached your home, photograph the water line on the walls before anything is cut out. It shows your flood insurer and your building department how high the water rose.
Services
Will Insurance Pay for Water Removal in Fort Myers?
This is general information, not advice about your policy. Water removal is often covered when the water came from something sudden and accidental, like a burst line or a failed appliance. Most policies also expect you to take reasonable steps to stop further damage, so starting water removal quickly usually helps rather than hurts. Rising water and storm surge need a separate flood policy. Every policy is different, so check yours. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .

Questions About Emergency Water Removal in Fort Myers
What is emergency water removal?
It is the first stage of water damage restoration: standing water is extracted, soaked materials that can't be saved are removed, moisture is mapped and drying equipment is set so the structure can dry.
How long does water extraction take?
Extraction for one or two rooms usually takes a few hours. Drying the structure afterward usually takes about 3 to 5 days for clean water, longer for slabs, hardwood and contaminated water.
Is water removal the same as water mitigation?
Water removal is the first part of mitigation. Mitigation is the whole job of stopping further damage: extracting water, removing what can't be saved and drying the structure.
Can water removal start before the plumber fixes the leak?
Yes, as long as the water is shut off. Close the valve at the fixture or the main, and extraction can start while you wait for the plumber to repair the pipe.
Does water removal get the water inside the walls?
Not by itself. Extraction pulls the liquid water off floors and out of carpet. Water already inside drywall, behind baseboards and in the slab comes out during structural drying, sometimes with small openings at the bottom of the wall so air can reach it.
Why does my floor feel dry when the meter says it is wet?
Tile and vinyl plank dry on top long before the slab underneath does. A moisture meter reads what is inside the material, which is why drying runs until the readings are normal, not until the surface feels dry.
Can you remove water from a garage or lanai?
Yes. Garage slabs often sit lower than the house, so water from a water heater, washer or storm runoff tends to pool there first. Standing water is extracted, stored boxes are lifted and checked, and the drywall on the wall shared with the house is read with a moisture meter, because water wicks into it from the garage side. On a screened lanai, water is pushed off the slab away from the house so it doesn't run back under the sliding doors.
Will my carpet be saved?
Carpet soaked by clean water and extracted quickly can often be dried in place, but the pad is usually replaced. Carpet touched by sewage or floodwater has to be removed.
Do I need to leave the house during water extraction?
Usually not for a clean-water leak. Extraction is loud for a few hours and the drying equipment runs day and night after that, but most families stay. Leave the affected rooms if the water is sewage or floodwater, or if a ceiling is sagging. See what to do about a leaking ceiling .
Can you get water out from under tile or vinyl plank?
Tile set on a concrete slab usually stays in place: water is pulled from the surface and grout lines, and the slab dries underneath with dehumidifiers over the following days. Floating vinyl plank and laminate trap water beneath them, so they often have to be lifted for the water and the slab under them to dry. Moisture readings decide which boards come up.
Can I run my AC during water removal?
Yes, if the leak was clean water and the AC isn't the source. The AC helps pull humidity out of the air. Keep it off if the water was sewage or floodwater, or if the AC is the thing leaking.
Is storm surge water harder to clean up than pipe water?
Yes. Surge is Category 3 and usually salt or brackish, so porous materials it touched are removed, surfaces are washed to take off salt and silt, and electrical parts are checked before the power returns.
Do you need my gate code or condo manager's number?
It helps. In gated communities and condo buildings, having the gate code and the manager's number ready saves time at the door and lets a shared water line be shut off quickly.
Is there emergency water extraction near me in Cape Coral or Lehigh Acres?
Yes. Emergency water removal covers Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Fort Myers Beach , Estero and Bonita Springs . Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7.

Water Mitigation and Structural Drying in Fort Myers, FL
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
Structural drying is the part of water mitigation that removes moisture from building materials after the standing water is gone. Dehumidifiers pull water out of the air, air movers push dry air across wet surfaces, and moisture meters track progress every day. Most clean-water jobs dry in about 3 to 5 days; slabs, hardwood and long-running leaks take longer.

Water Mitigation vs. Restoration in Fort Myers: What's the Difference?
Water mitigation stops the damage from getting worse. Restoration puts the house back together. Mitigation starts the same day; repairs come after the structure is confirmed dry.
Stage Water mitigation Restoration
Goal Stop further damage Rebuild what was damaged
Work Water removal, tear-out of what can't be saved, drying, antimicrobial treatment Drywall, baseboards, paint, flooring, cabinets
When Same day, then drying (about 3 to 5 days for most clean-water jobs) After moisture readings are back to normal
Services
How Structural Drying Works in Fort Myers Homes
The steps below follow the IICRC S500, the industry standard for water damage restoration that defines water categories, drying classes and what "dry" means.
1 Map the moisture
Moisture meters and a thermal camera show exactly which walls, floors and cabinets are wet. Dry areas of the same house are measured too; they become the target the wet materials must reach.
2 Remove what can't dry
Wet carpet pad, soaked insulation, swollen particle board and anything touched by sewage come out. Standing water is extracted first through emergency water removal.
3 Set the equipment
Low-grain refrigerant (LGR) dehumidifiers pull water vapor out of the air. Air movers blow across wet walls and floors so moisture evaporates faster. Desiccant dehumidifiers are used for dense materials like concrete and hardwood, and in tight spaces where refrigerant units struggle.
4 Open up hidden spaces
Baseboards may come off and small holes are drilled behind them so dry air reaches inside the wall cavity. Cabinet toe kicks come off so air can move under the cabinets. Wet vinyl plank or laminate may be lifted so the slab can breathe.
5 Measure every day
Moisture readings and indoor humidity are checked and logged as the job goes on, and equipment is moved as areas dry. The logs show what was wet, how wet, and when it reached dry.
6 Confirm it's dry
Drying is finished when wet materials match the dry readings of the same materials elsewhere in the house. Only then do drywall, baseboards and flooring go back.
Services
Why Drying Takes Longer in Fort Myers Homes
Humid outdoor air. Southwest Florida air holds a lot of moisture most of the year, so open windows slow drying down instead of speeding it up.
Concrete slabs. Most Lee County homes are slab-on-grade. Concrete soaks up water and releases it slowly, and tile, vinyl plank and laminate trap it underneath.
Concrete block walls. Many homes have block exterior walls with drywall over furring strips, which can hold moisture in the gap behind the drywall.
Slow, hidden leaks. AC condensate overflows and supply-line drips often run for days before anyone notices, so more material is wet when drying starts.
Seasonal homes. A leak in a closed-up home can soak a house for weeks. See water damage in vacant homes .
Services
Drying Fort Myers Block Homes, Ceilings, Condos and Mobile Homes
Concrete block walls
Drywall on the outside walls of most Fort Myers homes sits on wood furring strips over block, often with foil-faced insulation board in the gap. That layer slows drying from the room side, so the cavity is opened at the bottom and dried directly, and the furring strips are read separately from the drywall.
Tile on a slab
Tile that is still bonded can usually stay, and the slab dries through the grout lines. Tiles that sound hollow or have popped loose are lifted so the concrete under them can release its water.
Ceilings under an attic air handler
When an attic AC unit overflows, wet blown insulation sits on the ceiling drywall and keeps it wet from above. The wet insulation is removed, and a sagging ceiling is taken down before it falls. Turn off power to that room and stay out from under a bulging ceiling. See ceiling leak water damage .
Condos
Water crosses into the unit below and into walls shared with neighbors. Drying has to cover every affected unit, and the association is kept in the loop so access to each unit is lined up. See condo water damage .
Mobile and manufactured homes
Water collects in the belly wrap under the floor and soaks the particle board subfloor. The belly is opened and dried from below, and soft subfloor is replaced. See mobile home water damage .
Services
Why Box Fans and a Home Dehumidifier Aren't Enough in Fort Myers Humidity
They can help with a small surface spill. After a real leak they fall short because:
They can't push air inside walls, under tile or behind cabinets.
A household dehumidifier removes a small fraction of the water a commercial LGR unit pulls from the air each day.
Without moisture readings, nobody knows when the wall or slab is actually dry, so drywall gets closed up wet.
Moving damp air around in Florida humidity can spread moisture into dry rooms.

How Long Structural Drying Takes in Fort Myers
Most clean-water jobs dry in about 3 to 5 days. Dense materials and contaminated water take longer.
What got wet Typical drying time
Drywall and carpet, clean water, caught early About 3 to 5 days
Tile or vinyl plank on a concrete slab Often more than 5 days; flooring may need lifting
Hardwood or engineered wood Longer; specialty drying mats may be used
Plaster or concrete block Longer; often needs desiccant drying

Drying Classes 1 to 4: How Equipment Is Sized in Fort Myers Homes
Under the IICRC S500, drying equipment is sized by how much water got into the structure and how hard the materials are to dry:
Class What it looks like
Class 1 Small area; little water absorbed
Class 2 A whole room; water wicked up walls and into carpet and pad
Class 3 Water came from above; ceilings, walls, insulation and floors soaked
Class 4 Dense materials like hardwood, concrete or plaster are wet; needs longer, specialty drying
A higher class means more equipment and more days. Water category (clean, gray or black) is a separate measure of contamination. See clean, gray and black water explained on the homepage.
Services
What "Dry" Means: How Fort Myers Drying Jobs Are Measured
Every material has its own target. The target is set by measuring the same material in a dry part of your house, not by a number someone guesses.
Material How it's checked It's dry when
Drywall Moisture meter at the bottom of the wall, compared with dry drywall in another room Readings match the dry drywall
Wood framing and furring strips Meter readings through the opened cavity Readings match dry framing elsewhere in the house
Concrete slab Meter readings across the slab, plus a moisture test before new flooring Readings match the dry slab, and the test meets the flooring maker's limit
Cabinets Readings at the base and toe kick area Readings match dry cabinets or millwork
Hardwood Readings across several boards Readings match unaffected boards
Indoor air Humidity readings in each drying area Humidity stays low and steady while equipment runs

Does Wet Drywall Have to Be Cut Out in Fort Myers Homes?
Not always. Drywall wet with clean water and dried quickly can often stay. It is usually cut out when:
The water was sewage, floodwater or another Category 3 source.
The insulation behind it is soaked.
It sat wet long enough to soften, swell, crumble or grow mold.
When drywall is removed, a straight flood cut is made above the highest wet point, often about 2 or 4 feet up the wall, so the repair is clean and the framing can dry.
Services
How Slabs, Floors and Cabinets Are Dried in Fort Myers
Concrete slabs dry slowly. Vinyl plank or laminate on top usually has to be lifted so the concrete can release moisture. Tile that is still bonded can often stay while the slab dries through the grout.
Hardwood may be dried in place with drying mats if work starts early; cupped or buckled boards usually come out.
Cabinets are dried by removing toe kicks and pushing dry air underneath. Swollen particle board bases are replaced.
More detail: water damaged floors and water damaged kitchen cabinets .

Living With Drying Equipment in Your Fort Myers Home
Drying works only while the equipment runs, so a few days of noise and warm air are part of the job.
Leave it running day and night. Turning it off lets humidity climb back and adds days to the job.
Keep the AC on. Dehumidifiers release warm, dry air, so rooms feel warmer than usual. The AC keeps the house comfortable and helps hold humidity down.
Keep doors and windows closed unless you are told otherwise. Plastic sheeting may close off the wet area so the dehumidifiers work on a smaller space.
Mind the power. Each dehumidifier and air mover draws real power. Keep them on their own circuits, never share an extension cord with other appliances, and call if a breaker trips.
Don't move or turn the fans. Each air mover is aimed at a wet spot on purpose.
Keep kids and pets clear of cords, hoses and fan intakes.
Services
Before Repairs Start: Your Fort Myers Drying Checklist
Once a wall is closed or new flooring goes down, any water left inside is sealed in. Check these before anything is rebuilt:
Final readings in every room on the log match the dry standard.
The slab has been tested before new flooring, and the test meets the flooring maker's limit.
The inside of every opened wall has been photographed before it is closed.
Wet insulation has been replaced, not put back.
Antimicrobial has been applied wherever gray water or sewage touched.
The house has no musty smell with the doors closed and the AC running.
You have the final drying log and photos.
If the home is in a flood zone, you have checked the 50% rule with your building department before planning the rebuild.

Daily moisture logs, photos and equipment records show what was wet, how wet it was and when it was dry. Services
Questions About Water Mitigation and Drying in Fort Myers
What is structural drying?
Structural drying is the process of removing moisture from walls, floors, ceilings and cabinets after a leak, using dehumidifiers, air movers and moisture readings until materials are back to normal dry levels.
How do you know the house is dry?
Wet materials are measured against dry materials of the same type in an unaffected part of the house. When they match, drying is finished. Touch and smell are not reliable.
Will I get mold?
Mold can begin within 24 to 48 hours in humid conditions, which is why drying should start the same day. If mold has already grown, bring in a qualified Florida mold remediation company to remove it.
Does antimicrobial spray replace drying?
No. Antimicrobial treats surfaces touched by gray water or sewage; it does not dry anything. Mold is prevented by getting the materials dry.
Why are there holes drilled behind my baseboards?
The small holes let dry air into the wall cavity, so the inside of the wall can dry without cutting out the drywall. They are covered when the baseboards go back on.
Why is the house so warm during drying?
Dehumidifiers release warm, dry air as they pull water out. Keep the AC running; the warm, dry air is what helps materials give up their water.
Should I open the windows to help it dry?
Usually not in Fort Myers. Humid outdoor air slows drying. Keep the house closed and the AC running unless you are told otherwise.
Can I stay home during drying?
Usually yes after a clean-water leak. Expect noise and warm air around the equipment. Rooms affected by sewage or floodwater should stay closed off.
Can new flooring go down as soon as the walls are dry?
Not until the slab is tested. Concrete holds water longer than walls do, and most flooring makers set a moisture limit the slab has to meet before installation.
What if the power is out after a storm?
Drying needs steady power. Until it is back, remove wet carpet pad, baseboards and anything soaked so the rest can start drying, and keep any generator outside, away from doors and windows.
Do I need professional drying if the leak was small?
If the water stayed on a hard surface and was wiped up right away, probably not. If it reached under flooring, into walls or under cabinets, the hidden moisture usually needs commercial equipment and readings.
Why does my house smell musty after a leak was fixed?
A musty smell usually means something is still wet, often the bottom of a wall, the slab under flooring or insulation above a ceiling. Have moisture readings taken before anything is painted or closed up.
Is structural drying available in Cape Coral, Lehigh Acres and Estero?
Yes. Structural drying covers Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Fort Myers Beach , Estero and Bonita Springs . Call 239-356-3708 any hour.

The area is contained, sewage is extracted, porous materials it touched (carpet, pad, drywall below the wet line, insulation) are removed, hard surfaces are cleaned and disinfected, and the structure is dried. Sewage can carry bacteria, viruses and parasites. Keep children, pets, older adults and anyone with a weak immune system away.
Stop using all water. Every flush, shower or load of laundry can come back up at the lowest drain.
Porous materials touched by sewage are removed, not dried. Tile, concrete and framing are cleaned, disinfected and dried.
Many older Lee County homes have cast iron drain lines that crack under the slab and cause repeat backups.

Stop using water. No flushing, showers, laundry, dishwasher or sinks.
Close it off. Keep people and pets out of the affected area and shut the doors.
Cut the power at the breaker if sewage reaches outlets, cords or appliances.
Turn off the AC and fans that could move air from the affected area into the rest of the house.
Don't vacuum or mop it with household equipment; that spreads the contamination.
Photograph everything, then call a plumber to clear the line and a cleanup crew for the house.

Is Sewage Water Dangerous? Staying Safe in a Fort Myers Backup
Yes. Sewage is Category 3, or black water, the most contaminated type of water damage. It can carry bacteria, viruses and parasites, and it soaks into anything porous it touches. Skin contact, splashes and dirty hands are the main risks, which is why cleanup is done in gloves, boots, eye protection and respirators.
Until the area is cleaned:
Keep children, pets, older adults, pregnant women and anyone with a weak immune system or breathing problems out of the area.
Wash your hands with soap and clean water after touching anything from the affected rooms, and don't eat or drink there.
Cover any cuts before you go near it. If a cut or scrape touches sewage and turns red, swollen or painful, see a doctor.
Wash clothes that got splashed separately from the rest of the laundry, in hot water.
Don't mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners; the fumes are dangerous. Bleach also can't make soaked carpet, pad or drywall safe again.
Services
Why Sewage Backs Up in Fort Myers Homes
Main line clogs. Wipes, grease and roots block the line between the house and the street, so waste comes up at the lowest fixture, usually a shower or tub.
Cast iron drains. Many homes built before about 1975 have cast iron drain lines that corrode, scale and crack under the slab.
Heavy rain and storm surge. Overloaded sewer systems and flooded ground can push water back into homes during storms.
Lift station trouble. Flat Lee County relies on lift stations to pump sewage. When one loses power or fails during a storm, the lowest homes and ground-floor units on that line can back up.
Septic problems. Homes on septic can back up when the tank or drain field fails or floods, which is more common in parts of Lehigh Acres and North Fort Myers .
Septic-to-sewer conversions. New sewer connections in parts of Lee County, including Cape Coral's utility expansion areas, can expose old drain problems.
Toilet overflows. A clogged toilet that overflows with waste is Category 3. A clean-bowl overflow is usually Category 2.
Services
Signs Your Fort Myers Main Sewer Line Is Backing Up
Water comes up in the tub or shower when you flush the toilet.
Several drains are slow at the same time, not just one sink.
Gurgling sounds from drains or the toilet.
Sewer smell in bathrooms or near floor drains.
Water or waste around the cleanout pipe outside the house.
One slow drain is usually a local clog. Several at once usually points to the main line.

Whether your home is on a sewer line or a septic tank changes the signs, the cause and who you call first.
On city or county sewer On septic
Common signs Water comes up in the tub or shower when you flush; several drains slow at once Slow drains everywhere, gurgling, soggy ground or a sewage smell over the drain field

Who Is Responsible for the Sewer Line in Fort Myers?
As a general rule, the lateral line from your house to the public sewer connection is the property owner's responsibility, and the main in the street belongs to the utility. Rules differ between the City of Fort Myers, Lee County Utilities, Cape Coral, Bonita Springs and other providers, so ask your utility if the blockage might be on their side. If several homes on your street are backing up at once, call the utility right away.
Finding your cleanout. The cleanout is a capped pipe, usually 3 or 4 inches across, near the house or near the property line. On many Fort Myers homes it is hidden by landscaping or mulch. Knowing where it is lets a plumber reach the line fast, and sewage around it is a sign the blockage is past your house.

How Sewage Cleanup Works in Fort Myers Homes
1 Containment
Plastic barriers and closed doors keep contamination from spreading to clean rooms. Air filtration may be set up to keep odors and particles inside the work area.
2 Protective gear
Work is done in gloves, boots, eye protection and respirators.
3 Extraction
Sewage and contaminated water are pumped and extracted. See emergency water removal .
4 Removal of contaminated porous materials
Carpet, pad, drywall below the wet line, insulation and swollen particle board vanities are bagged and removed. Drywall is cut in a straight line above the highest wet point, often about 2 or 4 feet up the wall.
5 Cleaning and disinfection
Hard surfaces like tile, concrete and wood framing are cleaned first, then treated with an antimicrobial. Disinfectant works only on a surface that has already been cleaned.
6 Drying
Dehumidifiers and air movers dry the slab and framing, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
7 Rebuild
Once materials are clean and read dry, drywall, baseboards, vanities and flooring are replaced.
Services

After Cleanup: How to Know Your Fort Myers Home Is Safe Again
Before the rooms go back into use, check that:
Every porous material the sewage touched is gone, including the drywall and insulation below the wet line.
Hard surfaces have been cleaned and then disinfected, not just sprayed.
Moisture readings in the slab and framing are back to normal.
There is no sewage smell with the doors closed. A smell that lingers means something contaminated is still in place.
A plumber has cleared the line and confirmed it drains, ideally with a camera inspection that shows what caused the backup.
If the AC ran while sewage was in the house, the air handler and nearby ducts have been checked.
You have photos, the list of removed items and the drying log.

Sewage Backups in Fort Myers Condos and Multi-Unit Buildings
In condo buildings, a blockage in a shared drain stack can push sewage into lower units, often the ground floor. Report it to building management immediately so everyone stops using water. Who pays depends on where the blockage was and your condo documents: a shared line is often the association's responsibility, while a line serving only your unit is often yours.

Sewage After Storms and Flooding in Lee County
After hurricanes and heavy rain, floodwater and sewer overflows often mix. Treat any water that came in from outside, or up through the drains during a storm, as Category 3.
Power outages can stop lift stations, so avoid flushing and running water until power is back in your area.
A flooded septic drain field can't take water until the ground drains; keep water use to a minimum.
Keep children out of standing water in yards and streets after a storm.

Does Insurance Cover Sewage Backup in Florida?
This is general information, not advice about your policy. It depends on the cause and your policy:
Sewer or drain backup is often excluded unless your policy has a water backup endorsement. Check your declarations page.
A sudden pipe break inside the home is often covered for the resulting damage, even when the pipe itself is not.
Cast iron drains that wore out over time are often treated as wear and tear for the pipe, while some resulting damage may still be covered.
Flood and storm surge need a separate flood policy.
Additional living expenses may apply if a covered loss makes the home unlivable.

How to Prevent Another Sewage Backup in Your Fort Myers Home
Don't flush wipes, even ones labeled flushable, and keep grease out of the kitchen sink.
Have the main line camera-inspected if you have repeat clogs or an older home with cast iron drains.
Ask a plumber whether a backwater valve makes sense for your home.
Know where your outdoor cleanout is, and keep it clear of mulch and plants.
If you are on septic, keep up with pumping and inspections, and keep cars and heavy equipment off the drain field.

Questions About Sewage Backup Cleanup in Fort Myers
What is sewage backup cleanup?
It is the removal of black water from a home: containment, extraction, removal of contaminated porous materials, cleaning and disinfection of hard surfaces, and drying of the structure.
Can I clean up sewage myself?
A small clean-bowl overflow on tile can be cleaned with gloves and disinfectant. Real sewage on carpet, drywall or more than one room should be handled by a professional crew, because contaminated porous materials must be removed, not wiped.
Is a toilet overflow without waste still sewage?
Not quite. A clean-bowl overflow is usually Category 2. It still needs pad and some drywall removed and an antimicrobial applied, but it is not handled like a sewage backup unless it sat for a day or more.
Can I just use bleach on it?
Bleach can help on hard, already-cleaned surfaces, but it can't make soaked carpet, pad, drywall or insulation safe. Those have to come out. Never mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners.
Why does sewage come up in my shower when I flush?
The main drain line is usually blocked. Water from the toilet can't get past the blockage, so it rises at the lowest drain, often the shower or tub. Stop using water and call a plumber.
How long does sewage cleanup take?
Removal and disinfection usually take one to two days for a bathroom or one room. Drying the slab and framing takes several more days before rebuilding starts.
Is it safe to stay home after a sewage backup?
Not always, but keep the affected area sealed off and stay out of it. If the only bathroom is affected, or someone in the home is vulnerable, staying elsewhere is safer.
Should I run the AC after a sewage backup?
Keep it off until the affected area is closed off, so contaminated air isn't pulled through the system. If it ran during the backup, have the air handler and nearby ducts checked.
Will the smell go away?
Yes, once contaminated materials are removed and surfaces are disinfected and dried. A smell that lingers usually means something contaminated is still in place.
When can I use the toilet again?
Only after a plumber has cleared the line and confirmed it drains properly.
Who pays for a sewage backup in a condo?
It depends on where the blockage was and your condo documents. A shared line is often the association's responsibility; a line serving only your unit is often yours.
My home is on septic. Is the cleanup different?
The cleanup inside the house is the same: Category 3 rules apply. The difference is the cause. A septic company has to pump and inspect the tank and drain field before you use water again.
Who does emergency sewage cleanup in Fort Myers at night?
Call 239-356-3708 . The line is answered 24/7 for sewage backups in Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres, North Fort Myers, Fort Myers Beach , Estero and Bonita Springs .

Key facts about AC leaks in Fort Myers
Your AC pulls water out of the air as it cools. In humid Southwest Florida that is a lot of water every day, and it all has to leave through a small PVC drain line.
Attic air handlers leak into ceilings; closet units leak into floors, baseboards and the next room; condo units often leak into the unit below.

Check the ceiling. If it sags or bulges, keep everyone out from underneath it.

What You See vs. What's Wrong: Reading an AC Leak in Fort Myers
What the leak looks like usually tells you where it started.
What you see Most likely cause What to do
Water around the air handler only while the AC runs, and a full pan Clogged condensate drain line AC off, call the HVAC company to clear the line
The AC shut itself off and the pan is full The float switch did its job; the drain line is still clogged Leave it off until the line is cleared
Water dripping from a pipe over a window or under the eave The primary drain line is clogged and water is leaving through the backup line Call the HVAC company now, before the backup fails too
Ice on the copper lines or the coil, then a flood when it melts Frozen evaporator coil from a dirty filter or low refrigerant AC off, change the filter, call the HVAC company
Drips from ceiling vents but the pan is dry Sweating ducts or vents in a hot, humid attic HVAC company to check duct insulation and seal leaks

Why Is My AC Leaking Water Inside My Fort Myers Home?
Your air conditioner removes moisture as it cools. That water collects on the evaporator coil, drips into a drain pan and leaves the house through a condensate drain line. When any part of that path fails, the water ends up in your home instead. The most common causes:
Clogged condensate drain line. Algae, slime and dust build up inside the line. This is the most common reason AC units leak indoors in Florida.
Full, rusted or cracked drain pan. Older metal pans rust through; plastic pans crack.
Failed float switch. This safety switch should shut the AC off when the pan fills. If it is missing, stuck or wired wrong, the pan overflows.
Frozen evaporator coil. A dirty filter or low refrigerant can freeze the coil. When it thaws, more water comes off than the pan can handle.
Disconnected or sagging drain line. A joint pulls apart in the attic or wall and drips onto drywall.
Condensate pump failure. Units that pump water out, common in condos and interior closets, leak when the pump stops.
Sweating ducts and vents. Cold supply ducts in a hot, humid attic collect condensation that drips through ceiling vents.
Services
The Backup Drain and Float Switch in Fort Myers AC Systems
Florida's mechanical code calls for a backup wherever an AC overflow could damage the building, such as an attic or a closet over finished floors. That backup is usually one of these:
A secondary drain pan under the air handler, with its own drain line. In many Fort Myers homes that line ends over a window or under the eave, so dripping water there is a warning sign.
A float switch in the pan or drain line that shuts the AC off when water rises.
If your AC has neither, or the float switch has never been tested, ask your HVAC company to check it at the next service. It is a small part that prevents a large ceiling repair.
Services
Signs of AC Water Damage in Fort Myers Homes
AC leaks are often slow and can run for days before anyone sees water, especially with attic units. Watch for:
Brown or yellow stains on the ceiling near the air handler or a supply vent.
Bubbling paint or soft drywall in the hallway beside the AC closet.
Swollen or stained baseboards next to the air handler.
Damp carpet near the closet, or vinyl plank lifting at the edges.
A musty smell when the AC runs.
Rust on the bottom of the air handler cabinet, or a pan that is always wet.
The AC shutting off on its own, which can mean the float switch tripped.
Services
Where AC Leak Water Goes in Fort Myers Homes and Condos
Where your air handler sits decides where the damage ends up.
Air handler location Common in Where the water goes
Attic Single-family homes in Fort Myers, Cape Coral and Lehigh Acres Insulation first, then the ceiling drywall below, often a hallway or bedroom
Interior closet Many slab homes and condos Closet floor, baseboards, the shared wall with the next room, carpet or vinyl plank
Garage Older single-family homes Garage slab, the wall shared with the house, stored items
Condo utility closet Condos in Fort Myers, Estero and Bonita Springs Your floor and the ceiling of the unit below
Blown-in and batt insulation can soak up a lot of water before it reaches the drywall. That is why an attic leak may show only a small stain while the insulation above is soaked. In a condo, an AC leak often reaches the unit below and brings in the association and your neighbor's insurer. See condo water damage .
Services
AC Repair vs. Water Damage Restoration in Fort Myers: Who Fixes What?
An HVAC technician fixes the cause: clears the drain line, replaces the pan, installs or resets the float switch, or repairs a frozen coil. That stops new water.
They don't dry your house. Water already in the ceiling, walls, insulation and floor stays there unless it is measured and dried. Water damage restoration covers the rest:
Moisture mapping with meters and a thermal camera to find every wet area, including inside walls and above the ceiling.
Removing what can't be dried, such as soaked insulation, sagging drywall and swollen baseboards.
Drying with dehumidifiers and air movers, with readings logged daily.
Photos and moisture logs for your records and your insurer.
The best order is the HVAC company first to stop the water, then drying the same day. If the HVAC company can't come until tomorrow, drying can still start as long as the AC stays off.
Services
How AC Leak Damage Is Dried and Repaired in Fort Myers
Ceiling: a small stain from a short leak can often be dried in place. A sagging, soft or stained-through ceiling is usually cut out and replaced, and wet insulation above it is removed.
Walls: drywall next to an air handler closet often wicks water up from the floor. It can usually be dried in place if caught early; if it stayed wet for days, the bottom of the wall may be cut out.
Floors: tile on slab usually stays and is dried. Luxury vinyl plank often has to be lifted because it traps water on the concrete. Carpet pad near the closet is usually replaced. See water damaged floors .
Closet: the air handler platform, closet baseboards and any particle board nearby are checked for swelling.
Attic insulation: wet blown-in insulation is pulled back or removed so the ceiling drywall can dry from above, then replaced once the ceiling reads dry.
Most clean-water AC leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days once drying starts. Leaks that ran for weeks take longer and usually mean more tear-out.
Services
Is AC Condensate Water Clean in a Fort Myers Home?
AC condensate is usually treated as Category 1, clean water, when it is caught quickly. But the drain pan and line can hold algae and bacteria, and water that sits for a day or two in Fort Myers humidity can become Category 2. If the leak ran for days, plan on antimicrobial treatment and more material removal.
Services
Condo AC Leaks in Fort Myers: When Your Unit Floods the One Below
In many Fort Myers, Estero and Bonita Springs condos, each owner's AC sits in a utility closet right above a neighbor's ceiling. When it overflows:
1 Shut your AC off and tell building management right away.
2 Knock on the unit below and ask the owner to check their ceiling and walls.
3 Photograph both units before anything is removed.
4 Notify your HO-6 insurer. In most condos, the AC that serves only your unit is the unit owner's to maintain, so an overflow from your system often starts with your policy. Check your condo documents for the exact rules.
5 Dry both units. Drying only the unit with the AC leaves wet drywall and insulation in the ceiling below.
Services
Does Insurance Cover AC Leak Water Damage in Florida?
This is general information, not advice about your policy. It depends on how the leak happened. Florida policies usually separate sudden damage from slow, long-term leaks:
Often covered: water damage from a sudden overflow, such as a drain line that clogs and spills, a pan that cracks or a coil that thaws all at once.
Often excluded: damage from a leak that ran for weeks, which insurers may treat as gradual seepage or lack of maintenance.
Usually not covered: repairing the AC unit itself. The policy typically addresses the resulting water damage, not the equipment.
Mold coverage is often capped.
Report the date you found the leak truthfully, photograph everything and keep the HVAC technician's invoice, since it shows the cause. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Services
How to Stop AC Leaks in Your Fort Myers Home
Service the drain line. Have the condensate line flushed and checked at least once a year; many Florida homeowners do it twice because algae grows fast here. Ask your HVAC company whether a vinegar flush between visits suits your system.
Change the filter on schedule. A clogged filter can freeze the coil.
Test the float switch. Make sure a working float switch is installed and that it actually shuts the system off.
Check the secondary pan. Attic units should sit over a secondary drain pan that is clean, dry and not rusted.
Look once a month. Open the air handler closet and check for water in the pan or rust on the cabinet.
Watch the backup line. If water drips from the pipe over a window or under the eave, call the HVAC company the same day.
Add a leak sensor. A small sensor in the pan or closet sends an alert to your phone when water appears.
Plan for the season. If you leave for the summer, have someone check the AC regularly. See water damage in vacant homes .
Services
Questions About AC Leak Water Damage in Fort Myers
Why is my AC leaking water inside?
Most often because the condensate drain line is clogged, so water backs up and overflows the drain pan. Other causes include a cracked pan, a failed float switch, a frozen coil or a disconnected drain line.
Can I keep running my AC if it's leaking?
No. Turn it off until the cause is fixed. Running it keeps producing water that ends up in your ceiling or walls.
Why is water dripping from a pipe over my window?
That pipe is usually the end of your AC's backup drain line. Water there means the main drain line is clogged and the backup is doing its job. Call the HVAC company before the backup clogs too.
My AC shut off by itself and the pan is full. What happened?
The float switch tripped, which means it worked. The drain line is still clogged, so leave the AC off until it is cleared, then check the ceiling and floor near the unit for water that got out before the switch tripped.
Is a small ceiling stain from the AC an emergency?
Not always, but it means water has already soaked through insulation and drywall. Have it checked within a day or two, because hidden moisture in Florida humidity can lead to mold within 24 to 48 hours.
Will the HVAC company fix my ceiling?
Usually not. HVAC companies fix the air conditioner. Drying and repairing the ceiling, walls and floor is water damage restoration work.
How long does it take to dry after an AC leak?
Most clean-water AC leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days with dehumidifiers and air movers. Longer leaks and wet slabs take more time.
How often should the AC drain line be cleaned in Fort Myers?
Have it cleared at every AC service, which in Fort Myers usually means at least once a year and often twice, because the system runs most of the year. Between visits, many HVAC companies suggest pouring a cup of white vinegar into the drain line's access port every few months to slow algae growth. Ask your HVAC company what suits your system.
Why does my AC closet smell musty?
A musty smell usually means water has been sitting in the pan, the closet floor or the wall behind the unit. Check for a wet pan or rust, and have the area measured for hidden moisture.
Who pays when my condo AC leaks into the unit below?
It depends on your condo documents and where the leak started. In most condos the AC serving only your unit is the owner's responsibility, so the claim often starts with your HO-6 policy. Tell building management and your insurer right away.
Who fixes AC water damage in Cape Coral or Lehigh Acres?
After the HVAC technician fixes the unit, call 239-356-3708 to dry the ceiling, walls and floor. AC leak drying covers Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Fort Myers Beach , Estero and Bonita Springs , answered 24/7.

Water Coming Through Your Fort Myers Ceiling? Do This Right Now
Get people and pets out from under it. Wet drywall is heavy and can fall without warning.
Turn off power at the breaker for any room where water drips from a light fixture, ceiling fan or smoke detector. Don't touch a wet switch.
Stop the source if you can. If your AC is in the attic, switch it off at the thermostat. If a bathroom above is leaking, shut off its water. If rain is coming in, focus on catching the water.
Catch the water with buckets, towels and plastic sheeting, and move furniture, rugs and electronics out of the way.
Don't push on a bulge or stand under it. If a bubble keeps growing and you must relieve it, stand to the side, make one small hole at the lowest point with a long screwdriver and let it drain into a bucket.

Is a Sagging Ceiling in Your Fort Myers Home About to Fall?
A flat stain is a warning; a sag or bubble is an emergency. Drywall is gypsum held together by paper. Once it is soaked it loses strength, and the weight of the water pulls it away from the screws. Treat it as dangerous if you see:
A bulge or bubble in the ceiling or the paint.
Cracks or a sagging line along a drywall seam.
Screw heads popping through the surface.
Water dripping from more than one spot.
A ceiling that feels soft when gently pressed from a ladder at the edge.
A sagging section almost always has to be cut out and replaced once the area is dry.

Hallway or near the AC return Attic air handler overflow or a clogged condensate drain line Is the AC drain pan full? Did the AC shut off on its own? HVAC company
Around a ceiling vent Sweating ducts or a loose duct connection in a hot, humid attic Is the vent wet even on dry days? HVAC company
Near an exterior wall, after rain Roof leak, flashing, a soffit or a window above Does it get worse during storms? Roofer
Under a bathroom (two-story homes and condos) Toilet wax ring, shower pan, tub drain or supply line above Does it drip after someone showers or flushes? Plumber
Under a laundry room or kitchen above Washer hose, dishwasher or ice maker line upstairs Is there water on the floor above? Plumber or appliance tech
Anywhere in a condo The unit above, or a shared line or roof Ask the neighbor and building management right away The neighbor or the association
Garage ceiling Water heater, AC or plumbing above the garage, or the roof Check the appliance area above Plumber, HVAC company or roofer
If your AC is in the attic and the stain is near it, read AC leak water damage.
