Why Is My Fort Myers Ceiling Leaking When It Isn't Raining?
Most often it is the AC: a clogged condensate drain line or sweating ducts in the attic. In two-story homes and condos it can be a bathroom, laundry or kitchen above. Some homes also have water lines running through the attic, where a pinhole leak shows up as a ceiling stain.

Roof Leaks in Fort Myers: Tile, Shingle and Flat Roofs
The roof over your ceiling decides where rain gets in.
Roof type Where it usually leaks Good to know
Concrete or clay tile Worn underlayment, cracked or slipped tiles, valleys and roof vents The tiles shed most of the rain; the underlayment beneath them is what keeps it out, so a tile roof can leak with no broken tiles in sight
Asphalt shingle Lifted or missing shingles after wind, flashing where the roof meets a wall, pipe boots Damage often shows only after the next heavy rain
Flat or low-slope (lanai roofs, porch additions, many condos) Seams, clogged drains and scuppers, standing water Water spreads across the roof before it finds a way in, so the stain can be far from the leak
Metal Loose fasteners, seams and flashing at walls Fasteners can back out over years of heat
After a storm, have a roofer put a tarp on as soon as it is safe. Never go on a wet roof yourself. See flood and storm cleanup .

Why Ceiling Leaks Are So Common in Fort Myers Homes
Attic air handlers. Many Southwest Florida homes have the air handler in the attic, where a clogged condensate line overflows straight onto the ceiling.
Humid attics. Hot, humid attic air makes cold ducts sweat and drip through ceiling vents.
Afternoon storms and hurricanes. Wind-driven rain gets past flashing, vents and soffits, especially after storms that loosen shingles or tiles.
Two-story homes and condos. Bathrooms and laundry rooms above living spaces send leaks straight down.
Plumbing in the attic. A supply line in the attic leaks directly onto the ceiling.
Services
Why a Ceiling Stain in a Fort Myers Home Is More Than a Paint Problem
By the time a stain shows, water has already soaked through the insulation above and the drywall itself. In Florida humidity that moisture rarely dries on its own, and left alone it leads to:
Mold on the back of the drywall and in the insulation, which can begin within 24 to 48 hours.
Stains that bleed back through fresh paint.
Sagging and eventual collapse.
Rot in ceiling joists or roof decking if the leak keeps going.
The kind of insulation above the ceiling changes what happens next:
Attic insulation What water does to it What usually happens
Blown-in cellulose Soaks up water, packs down and gets heavy on the drywall Removed and replaced
Blown-in or batt fiberglass Holds water against the drywall and loses its fluff Usually removed and replaced
Radiant barrier on the roof deck Not a water problem itself, but can hide a roof leak above it Checked for stains on the decking
Services
Should You Go Into the Attic in a Fort Myers Home?
Only if it is safe. Fort Myers attics get very hot, and a misstep goes straight through the ceiling.
Never go above a ceiling that is sagging, soft or dripping.
Step only on the joists or a walkboard, never on the drywall between them.
Go early in the morning, bring a flashlight and keep someone at the bottom of the ladder.
Look for a full AC drain pan, a wet duct, a dripping pipe or daylight through the roof deck. Don't try to fix anything up there.
If you're not sure, leave it to the HVAC company, plumber or roofer, and to the moisture mapping that follows.
Services
How a Wet Ceiling Is Dried or Replaced in Fort Myers
1 Find and stop the source
An HVAC technician, plumber or roofer fixes the cause. A tarp goes on the roof if rain is still getting in.
2 Measure the moisture
A moisture meter and thermal camera show how far the water spread across the ceiling and down the walls, which is usually wider than the stain.
3 Decide what stays
A small, recent, clean-water stain can often be dried in place. A ceiling that sagged, stayed wet for days or has wet insulation above it is usually opened up.
4 Remove wet insulation and damaged drywall
Soaked insulation is bagged out and the wet section of ceiling is cut back to sound drywall.
5 Dry the framing and attic space
Dehumidifiers and air movers run until the joists and remaining drywall read dry. See how structural drying works .
6 Repair
New insulation, new drywall, tape, texture and paint. Knockdown and other textures common in Fort Myers homes are matched to the rest of the ceiling so the patch doesn't show.
Water often runs along joists and down the inside of walls, so the walls below the stain are checked too. If water reached the floor, emergency water removal comes first.
Services
Popcorn Ceilings in Older Fort Myers Homes
Many older homes in Fort Myers and Cape Coral have textured "popcorn" ceilings. Some textures applied before the mid-1980s contain asbestos. Before a wet popcorn ceiling is scraped or cut, have a sample tested, and don't sand or scrape it yourself.

Does Insurance Cover a Leaking Ceiling in Florida?
This is general information, not advice about your policy. It depends on what caused the leak:
Sudden leaks from a burst supply line, an appliance or an AC overflow are often covered for the resulting damage. See burst pipe water damage .
Roof leaks after a storm may be covered when wind damaged the roof. Hurricane claims usually carry a separate hurricane deductible.
Roof leaks from age or wear are often excluded.
Slow leaks that ran for weeks are often treated as gradual damage.
Leaks from the unit above in a condo involve your HO-6 policy, the neighbor's policy and the association.
Photograph the ceiling before anything is removed, keep the repair invoices that show the cause and report the date you found the leak truthfully. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .

How to Prevent Ceiling Leaks in Your Fort Myers Home
Have the AC condensate line cleared at every service and the float switch tested.
Have the roof checked after any big storm, even if nothing looks wrong from the ground.
Keep gutters, scuppers and flat-roof drains clear before the summer rainy season.
In two-story homes and condos, recaulk showers and tubs and replace old washer hoses upstairs.
Glance at the ceilings near the air handler and bathrooms once a month for new stains.

Questions About Ceiling Leaks in Fort Myers
What should I do if water is leaking through my ceiling?
Keep people out from under it, turn off power to wet fixtures at the breaker, stop the source if you can, catch the water and photograph everything. Then have the ceiling measured for moisture.
Should I poke a hole in a ceiling bubble?
Only if it keeps growing and you can do it safely: stand to the side, make one small hole at the lowest point and drain it into a bucket. If the ceiling is sagging across a wide area, keep everyone out of the room instead.
Is water dripping from a light fixture dangerous?
Yes. Turn off that circuit at the breaker, don't touch the switch and keep clear. Have an electrician check the fixture and box before you turn the power back on.
What if water dripped from a smoke detector?
Turn off that circuit and have the detector checked or replaced. Don't count on a smoke detector that got wet.
Why does my ceiling leak only when rain comes from one direction?
Wind-driven rain is getting past flashing, a soffit, a vent or a window on that side of the house. Tell the roofer which direction the storm came from; it narrows the search.
Can my tile roof leak if no tiles are broken?
Yes. On a tile roof the underlayment beneath the tiles keeps the water out. When it wears out, rain gets through even with every tile in place.
Can I just paint over a ceiling water stain?
Only after the leak is fixed and the drywall and insulation are confirmed dry with a moisture meter. Paint over wet drywall traps moisture, and the stain usually comes back.
How long does a wet ceiling take to dry?
A small clean-water area often dries in about 3 to 5 days with drying equipment. If insulation or a large section of drywall has to come out, repairs add time after drying.
Who fixes the ceiling after the leak is repaired?
The plumber, roofer or HVAC company fixes the source. Drying the ceiling, removing wet insulation and replacing drywall is water damage restoration work.
Can a ceiling leak cause mold?
Yes. Wet insulation and the back of the drywall can grow mold within 24 to 48 hours in humid conditions, often before anything shows on the painted side.
Who can help with a leaking ceiling tonight in Fort Myers or Cape Coral?
Call 239-356-3708 . The line is answered 24/7 for ceiling leaks in Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Fort Myers Beach , Estero and Bonita Springs .

Water Leaking From the Condo Above in Fort Myers? First-Hour Steps
Knock on the door above or beside you. The owner or tenant may not know. Ask them to shut off the fixture or the unit's water valve.
Call building management or the association if no one answers. Many buildings can shut off a unit's water or the riser in an emergency.
Cut power at your breaker to any room where water drips from a light, fan or smoke detector.
Catch and move: buckets, towels and plastic under the drip; furniture, electronics and rugs out of the way.
Photograph and video everything: ceiling, walls, floor, the source if you can see it and damaged belongings. Write down the time you found it.
Collect names: the owner above, their insurer if they will share it, and the management company contact.
Report the loss to your HO-6 insurer and start drying the same day.

Why Condo Leaks in Fort Myers Are Different From House Leaks
In a single-family home, a leak is your problem and your policy. In a condo, responsibility depends on where the water came from, what it damaged and what your declaration says. Water also travels: a washer hose that bursts on the fourth floor can wet the third, second and first floors through ceilings and wall cavities. That is why buildings in Fort Myers, Estero, Bonita Springs and Fort Myers Beach often have several units drying at once after a single failure.
Services
How Water Travels in Fort Myers Condo Buildings
The way your building is put together decides which neighbors get wet.
Building type How the water moves What gets checked
Two- and three-story garden-style condos (common in gated communities) Straight down through wood-framed floors into the ceiling below The unit below, the shared walls and the ceiling cavity between floors
Mid-rise and high-rise towers (along the river, on the beach, in Estero and Bonita Springs) Concrete floors slow it down, so water runs along the slab to pipe chases, AC closets and wall bottoms, then drops Units stacked below the same kitchen, bath and AC closet, often several floors down
Townhomes and villas Sideways through the shared wall, plus down if there is a second floor Both sides of the shared wall and the floor below
Kitchens sit over kitchens and bathrooms over bathrooms in most buildings, so the unit directly below the source is checked first, then the one below that.
Services
What Causes Most Condo Leaks in Southwest Florida
AC condensate overflows from a clogged drain line or failed condensate pump in an interior closet.
Washing machine hoses and stacked washer-dryer units. See appliance leak water damage .
Water heaters in utility closets, often directly above someone else's ceiling. See water heater leak cleanup .
Toilet supply lines, wax rings and shower pans that fail slowly.
Dishwasher and ice maker lines in the kitchen above.
Shared risers and pipes in the walls that serve more than one unit.
Roofs, windows, balconies and exterior walls, especially during storms.
Shared drain stacks that back up into the lowest units. See sewage backup cleanup .
Services
Who Pays for a Condo Leak in Fort Myers? What Florida Law Says
Florida Statute 718.111(11) sets the default. The association's policy generally covers the building as originally installed: the structure and common elements such as the roof, exterior walls, shared pipes and original drywall.
The unit owner is generally responsible for items inside the unit, including:
Floor, wall and ceiling coverings (tile, carpet, wood, paint, wallpaper)
Electrical fixtures, appliances, water heaters and water filters
Built-in cabinets and countertops
Window treatments
Personal property, plus any upgrades or improvements
Most owners insure these with an HO-6 policy.
When another owner caused it: if the leak came from a neighbor's unit, for example a washer hose or toilet line they failed to maintain, that owner or their insurer may be responsible for some of the damage. That usually depends on the cause and on negligence, and it is often settled between the insurers.
Leak source Who is usually involved
Roof, exterior wall, window frame or balcony Association
Shared riser or pipe serving several units Association
Pipe, fixture or appliance serving only the unit above Owner above and their insurer
Your own appliance, water heater or AC You and your HO-6 insurer
Shared drain line backup Association, depending on where the blockage was
This is general information, not legal advice. Ask management for the declaration, and talk with your insurer or a Florida attorney for disputes.
Services
Who Should Start the Cleanup in a Fort Myers Condo?
Start drying right away, whoever ends up paying. Most policies expect owners to take reasonable steps to prevent further damage, and waiting while parties argue lets drywall, cabinets and flooring swell and grow mold.
In many buildings the association sends its own restoration vendor when several units or common elements are wet. You can usually still bring in a company for your own unit's finishes and belongings, but coordinate with management so two crews aren't working against each other. Ask:
Who is drying the common elements and the shared walls?
Who is responsible for my unit's flooring, cabinets and contents?
Will moisture readings and photos be shared with me and my insurer?
Services
Can the Association Get Into a Fort Myers Condo to Stop a Leak?
Usually, yes. Florida Statute 718.111(5) gives the association a right of access to each unit when it is needed for maintenance or repair of the common elements, or to prevent damage to the common elements or to another unit. That is how management can shut off water in a unit when the owner is away.
Make sure management has a key or entry code for your unit, especially if you leave for the season.
Give management a current phone number for you and anyone who checks the unit while you're gone.
Your declaration and building rules set the details, such as notice and who may enter.

How Condo Water Damage Is Dried in Fort Myers
1 Stop the source and check every affected unit
Moisture meters and a thermal camera trace the water from the source unit down through ceilings and walls.
2 Remove standing water
Water on floors and in carpet is extracted. See emergency water removal .
3 Open what can't dry
Sagging ceiling drywall, soaked insulation and swollen cabinet bases are removed and photographed.
4 Dry each unit
Dehumidifiers and air movers run in every wet unit, with readings logged for each one. See structural drying .
5 Document for every insurer
Each unit's photos, readings and removed materials are recorded separately, because each owner's claim is separate.
Condo drying often needs access to the unit above even if it isn't wet, to reach the source or the space between floors. Ask management to arrange access early.

Interior finishes the association doesn't insure: flooring, cabinets, countertops, fixtures, paint.
Personal property: furniture, clothing, electronics.
Loss of use if you have to stay elsewhere during repairs, depending on your policy.
Loss assessment coverage, if you have it, can help when the association charges owners for a deductible or uninsured loss.

Condo Leaks in Seasonal Fort Myers Buildings
Many condos in Estero, Bonita Springs and on Fort Myers Beach sit empty for months. A leak above an empty unit can run for weeks. Before you leave for the season:
Shut off your unit's water at the main valve, and turn off the water heater.
Leave the AC on and set to control humidity.

Questions About Condo Water Damage in Fort Myers
Who pays for water damage from the condo above me in Florida?
It depends on the source. Damage to the building structure or shared pipes is generally the association's; damage to your unit's finishes is generally yours under your HO-6 policy. If the owner above caused the leak, their insurer may be responsible for some of the damage. Your declaration and the insurers decide the details.
Should I call my insurance or the association first?
Call the unit above and building management first to stop the water. Then report the loss to your HO-6 insurer and start drying.
Can the association enter my unit to stop a leak?
Usually, yes. Florida law gives the association a right of access to units when needed to prevent damage to the common elements or to another unit. Keep a key or code on file with management.
Can I use my own restoration company in a condo?
Usually yes for your unit's interior, but coordinate with the association, especially when it has sent its own vendor for common elements or several units.
My unit is below and the upstairs owner isn't home. What now?
Call building management or the association. Many buildings can shut off a unit's water or the riser in an emergency. Keep documenting while you wait.
I rent my condo. Who do I call?
Tell your landlord and building management right away, then photograph your belongings. The owner's HO-6 and the association handle the building; your renters policy, if you have one, covers your belongings.
Does the association have to pay for my flooring and cabinets?
Generally no. Under Florida's condo law, floor coverings and built-in cabinets are usually the unit owner's to insure, unless your declaration says otherwise.
How long does condo drying take?
Most clean-water condo leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days per unit. Several units, sewage or wet concrete take longer.
What if the leak keeps coming back?
Repeat leaks from a common element, such as a roof, riser or association-maintained line, should be reported to the association in writing each time, with dates and photos.

Cast Iron Pipe Water Damage in Fort Myers and Cape Coral
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
Cast iron drain pipes, common in Florida homes built before about 1975, corrode from the inside, crack and leak wastewater under the slab or into walls. A plumber confirms it with a camera and repairs or lines the pipe; restoration removes contaminated flooring and drywall, disinfects and dries the slab and walls.
Cast iron leaks in Lee County
Details
Phone 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7
Homes most at risk Fort Myers and Cape Coral homes built before about 1975, plus some from the 1970s and 1980s
Water category Category 3, because the pipe carries wastewater
How it's confirmed A plumber's camera inspection through the cleanout
Who does what The plumber repairs or lines the pipe; restoration removes contaminated materials, disinfects and dries
Insurance in short The pipe is often treated as wear and tear; some resulting damage and tear-out may be covered
Key facts about cast iron drains in Lee County
A leaking drain line leaks wastewater, so the damage is Category 3 (black water), not clean water.
Signs include slow drains, repeat clogs, sewer odor, cracked or hollow tile and damp baseboards near bathrooms.
Cape Coral's septic-to-sewer conversions and older Fort Myers neighborhoods are where these failures show up most.
Insurance often treats the pipe as wear and tear, while some resulting damage or tear-out may be covered depending on the policy.

Sewer Smell, Backups or Damp Tile in Your Fort Myers Home? Do This First
Stop using water in the house: no flushing, showers, laundry or dishwasher until a plumber checks the line.
Keep people and pets away from any area where wastewater is on the floor or the smell is strong.
Cut power at the breaker if wastewater reaches outlets or appliances.
Don't mop or vacuum it with household tools.
Photograph the backup, wet floors, cracked tile and stained baseboards.
Call a plumber for a camera inspection and a cleanup crew for the house.
More steps: the first-hour water damage checklist .

Services
Why Cast Iron Pipes Fail in Fort Myers and Cape Coral
Cast iron was the standard material for home drain and sewer lines for decades. It corrodes from the inside as wastewater, sewer gases and minerals eat at the pipe wall, and the bottom of the pipe thins until it cracks or rots through. Florida's moisture-rich conditions are widely blamed for speeding up that corrosion. When it fails, drain water leaks into the soil under the slab or into the wall cavity, often for months before anyone notices.
In Cape Coral, many homes from the 1970s and 1980s, especially in the older southeast and southwest Cape, still have original cast iron sewer lines. Older Fort Myers neighborhoods have many homes from the same era. Cape Coral's ongoing utility expansion is also connecting older homes from septic to city sewer, and new connections can expose drain-line problems that went unnoticed for years.
Services
Signs of Cast Iron Pipe Failure in Fort Myers Homes
Slow drains in more than one fixture, especially showers and tubs on the lowest level.
Clogs that come back soon after a plumber clears them.
Sewer smell in a bathroom or near a floor drain, often worse after heavy rain.
Sewage or gray water backing up into a tub, shower or floor drain.
Cracked, loose or hollow-sounding tile, especially in bathrooms.
Damp or stained baseboards and swollen door frames near bathrooms.
Water stains on flooring with no visible leak above.
Mold or a musty smell low on walls next to bathrooms or the kitchen.
Roaches or other pests around drains, which can mean an opening in the line.
Rust-colored flakes in what the plumber clears from the line.
If your home was built before about 1975 and you notice two or more of these, have the line checked.
Services
How to Tell If Your Fort Myers or Cape Coral Home Has Cast Iron Pipes
Check the year built on the Lee County Property Appraiser record or your closing documents.
Look at exposed drain pipes under sinks, in the garage or at a cleanout. Cast iron is heavy and dark gray or black, and a magnet sticks to it. PVC is white or cream plastic.
Ask for a camera inspection. A plumber feeds a camera down the cleanout and records the inside of the line, showing cracks, scale, sagging sections and where the leak is.
Buying an older home? Ask for a sewer camera inspection before closing. A standard home inspection usually doesn't look inside the drain line.
Services
What the Camera Shows: Stages of Cast Iron Failure in Fort Myers Homes
The plumber's camera video tells you how far the pipe has gone, and how much of your floor is likely to be affected.
What the camera shows What it means What it usually means for your floors
Heavy scale and rust buildup The pipe is narrowing and corroding, but may still be intact Slow drains and clogs; floors usually dry so far
Channeling along the bottom of the pipe The bottom has worn into a groove and is thin or open Wastewater is likely seeping into the soil under the slab
Cracks or holes Water is leaving the pipe at that spot Damp tile, baseboards and slab near the break
A belly or sag A section has dropped and holds water and waste Repeat clogs and backups; possible leaks at the joints
Collapsed or missing sections The line has failed Backups and spreading contamination; repair is urgent
Ask for the video and a written report. They show where the damage is, measured from the cleanout, which tells you which rooms will be opened.
Services
What a Leaking Cast Iron Drain Does to a Fort Myers Home
Because the pipe carries wastewater, the water under your floor is Category 3.
Material What usually happens
Tile and grout Tile may stay; wet grout and slab are cleaned, disinfected and dried. Cracked or loose tile is replaced
Luxury vinyl plank and laminate Removed; it traps contaminated water on the slab
Carpet and pad Removed
Baseboards and lower drywall Removed above the wet line, often with a flood cut about 2 feet up
Bathroom vanities and kitchen base cabinets Removed if swollen or contaminated
Concrete slab Cleaned, treated with antimicrobial and dried; slower to dry than walls
The plumbing repair often requires opening the floor anyway, so tile and slab work usually happen together.
Services
How Cast Iron Pipe Is Fixed in Fort Myers Homes: Lining, Spot Repair or Replacement
A plumber decides after the camera inspection.
Option How it works How much floor is opened Good to know
Hydro jetting High-pressure water clears scale and roots None Cleans the line but doesn't fix a crack; it can also show how thin the walls are
Spot repair One damaged section is cut out and replaced One area of slab, or a tunnel under it Works when the rest of the line is in good shape
Pipe lining A new pipe is formed inside the old cast iron Usually little or none Not every line qualifies; badly channeled or collapsed sections may need replacing first
Full replacement The old line is replaced with PVC Trenches through the slab, or a tunnel under the house The most disruptive option, but it ends the problem for that line
Services
Questions to Ask Your Plumber After the Camera Inspection
Where exactly is the damage, measured from the cleanout, and under which rooms?
Is it one section or the whole line?
Will lining work here, or does it need spot repair or replacement?
Which floors and walls will be opened, and how wide will the trench be?
Does the repair need a permit and an inspection before the slab is closed?
Who patches the slab, and who replaces the flooring afterward?
Can I have the video and a written report for my insurer?
Services
How a Cast Iron Job Runs in a Fort Myers Home, Start to Finish
1 Camera inspection
The plumber finds the damage and records it. Keep the video and report.
2 Containment
Plastic barriers keep contamination and dust out of clean rooms.
3 Removal
Contaminated flooring, baseboards, lower drywall and swollen cabinetry come out and are bagged.
4 Plumbing repair
The plumber trenches, tunnels or lines the pipe. The trench and access holes are planned with the cleanup crew so neither undoes the other's work. Larger drain repairs usually need a plumbing permit and an inspection before the slab is patched.
5 Cleaning and disinfection
The slab, studs and remaining surfaces are cleaned and treated with antimicrobial.
6 Drying
Dehumidifiers and air movers dry the slab and wall framing, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
7 Rebuild
New drywall, baseboards, flooring and cabinets go in once everything reads dry and clean.
Services
Living Through Cast Iron Repairs in Your Fort Myers Home
Plan the bathrooms. If the work is under the only working bathroom, plan where you'll stay or ask whether one bathroom can stay usable.
Expect dust and noise. Cutting a slab is loud and dusty, even with containment.
Keep kids and pets out of the work area and away from open trenches.
Move what you can out of the affected rooms before the trench is cut.
Keep a list of what was removed and when, alongside the plumber's report and the drying log.

Does Insurance Cover Cast Iron Pipe Damage in Florida?
This is general information, not advice about your policy. Cast iron claims are among the most disputed water claims in Florida. In general:
The pipe itself is often excluded as wear and tear or deterioration.
Resulting water damage to floors, walls and cabinets may be covered when the leak was sudden, and may be excluded when the insurer decides it was long-term seepage.
Tear-out coverage in some policies pays to open the floor or wall to reach the broken pipe.
Sewer or drain backup coverage may require a separate endorsement.
Keep the plumber's camera video, written report and photos, and report the date you found the damage truthfully. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Services
Check for a water damage limit before the floor is opened
Older homes are the ones most likely to carry a limited water damage endorsement, and cast iron claims are where it matters most, because reaching the pipe often means opening tile and slab. Some endorsements cap water damage and tear-out together at a fixed amount; others cap the water damage but say nothing about tear-out. Before demolition starts, ask your agent or adjuster which wording your policy has, and keep a copy of the endorsement in your claim file.
Services
Cast Iron in Fort Myers Condo Buildings
Older condo buildings often have cast iron drain stacks that serve several units. A failure in a shared stack is usually the association's responsibility; a branch line serving only one unit may be the owner's. Report repeat backups to the association in writing, with dates and photos. See condo water damage .
Services
Questions About Cast Iron Pipe Water Damage in Fort Myers
What year did Florida stop using cast iron pipes?
There was no single cutoff. Cast iron was common in homes built before about 1975, and some homes built in the 1970s and 1980s also have it. Check the year built and ask a plumber to confirm.
How long do cast iron pipes last in Florida?
They were expected to last for many decades, but many in Florida fail much earlier because of corrosion.
Why does my bathroom smell like sewer?
It can be a dry trap, a failed toilet wax ring, a vent problem or a cracked drain line under the floor. If the smell keeps coming back with slow drains or damp tile, have the drain camera-inspected.
Is water from a cast iron leak dangerous?
Yes. It is wastewater, classed as Category 3. Keep children, pets and anyone with health issues away, and don't clean it with household tools.
Can a cast iron leak damage the soil under my slab?
It can. Over time, leaking drain water can wash soil out from under the slab. If floors crack, settle or sound hollow over a wide area, mention it to the plumber, who may suggest having it checked further.
Do I have to tear up my floors?
Often part of the floor has to come up, both to repair the pipe and to remove contaminated flooring. Pipe lining can reduce how much floor is opened if the line qualifies.
Does pipe lining work on Florida cast iron?
Often, but not always. Lines with heavy channeling, missing sections or a deep sag may need those sections replaced before lining, or a full replacement instead.
Should I get a sewer camera inspection before buying an older home?
Yes, for a home built before about 1975. A standard home inspection usually doesn't look inside the drain line, and the camera video shows its condition before you buy.
Will insurance pay to replace my cast iron pipes?
Usually not for the pipe itself, which policies often treat as wear and tear. Some policies pay for tear-out to reach the pipe and for resulting damage.
Can I live in the house during cast iron repairs?
Often yes, if at least one bathroom works and the contaminated area is sealed off. Large trenching jobs through the kitchen or main bath may make staying elsewhere easier.
Who cleans up cast iron pipe leaks in Cape Coral and Fort Myers?
A plumber repairs the drain line; restoration removes contaminated materials and dries the slab and walls. Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for Cape Coral , Fort Myers, Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Estero and Bonita Springs .

Found Water Damage After Time Away From Fort Myers? Do This First
Shut off the main water if you find active water or don't know the source.

What Usually Fails While a Fort Myers Home Sits Empty
AC failure or power loss. If the AC stops from a breakdown or storm outage, indoor humidity climbs and mold can grow on walls, closets and furniture within days.
AC condensate overflow. The AC keeps running but the drain line clogs, and water spills into the closet, ceiling or floor for weeks.
Water heater leaks. Tanks rust through at the bottom and leak slowly, or fail all at once in a garage or closet. See water heater leak cleanup .
Supply line failures. Braided lines to toilets, sinks, washers and ice makers split without warning. See burst pipe water damage .
Roof and window leaks from summer downpours and tropical storms, often showing up as ceiling stains. See ceiling leak water damage .
Chewed lines. Rodents in quiet houses sometimes chew plastic dishwasher, ice maker or washer lines.
Leaks from the unit above in condos, where your neighbor may also be away.
Services
Room-by-Room Return Check for Your Fort Myers Home
Walk the house before you unpack, with a flashlight and your nose.
Where What to look for
Front door and first breath Musty or sour smell, damp air, fogged windows
AC closet or air handler Water in the pan, rust, wet floor or baseboards, thermostat and indoor humidity reading
Kitchen Under the sink, around the dishwasher and ice maker line, swollen cabinet bottoms
Bathrooms Around toilets and supply lines, under vanities, loose or stained tile, shower base
Laundry Washer hoses, the floor behind the machine, the wall below the valves
Water heater Rust or water at the base, a wet pan, damp garage or closet floor
Ceilings Stains under the attic AC, bathrooms above and along exterior walls
Closets and furniture Mold spots on shoes, leather, closet walls and the backs of furniture
Floors Lifting vinyl plank, hollow tile, dark grout lines, damp carpet edges
Turning the water back on. Open the main valve slowly and check under sinks and around the water heater before running appliances. If you have an electric water heater, let the tank fill completely before you turn its power back on; heating an empty tank can burn out the elements.
Services
Is That Musty Smell in Your Fort Myers Home Humidity or Water Damage?
A closed-up house in Southwest Florida can smell musty from humidity alone, but the smell can also come from a hidden leak or mold behind walls.
Check indoor humidity with an inexpensive hygrometer. Indoor relative humidity is generally best kept below about 60 percent; readings well above that mean the AC wasn't keeping up.
Look for visible mold on walls, ceilings, closet contents and the AC return grille.
Feel the bottoms of walls and baseboards near bathrooms, the kitchen and the AC closet for dampness or softness.
Watch the water meter. With every fixture off, a moving meter means a leak somewhere.
Smell the drains. A sewer smell after months away often means the water in the drain traps has dried up. Run water in every sink, tub, shower and floor drain, and flush each toilet, to refill them.
If you see mold on the air handler or vents, have the AC checked before running it hard, so it doesn't spread spores through the ducts.
Services
How Long-Running Leaks Change the Cleanup in a Fort Myers Home
Water category drifts. Clean water left for 24 to 48 hours or more can become Category 2, and long-standing water is often treated as more contaminated.
More material comes out. Drywall, baseboards, cabinet bases and vinyl plank that stayed wet for weeks usually can't be saved.
Slabs hold more water. Concrete under tile and plank soaks up water and takes longer to dry.
Mold is more likely. If mold has grown, bring in a qualified Florida mold remediation company to remove it.
Services
How Water Damage in a Vacant Fort Myers Home Is Dried
1 Find and stop the source
A plumber, HVAC technician or roofer fixes the cause.
2 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera show how far water spread under floors and into walls, often far beyond the visible stain.
3 Extract and remove
Standing water is extracted, and soaked carpet pad and materials that can't be saved are removed and photographed. See emergency water removal .
4 Dry the structure
Dehumidifiers and air movers dry the wet drywall and flooring in the seasonal home, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
5 Bring the whole house down
Humidity is brought down across the house so closets, furniture and dry rooms stop absorbing moisture.

Insurance When Nobody Was Home: What Fort Myers Owners Should Know
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
Vacancy and unoccupancy clauses. Many policies limit coverage for certain losses after a home is vacant or unoccupied for a set number of days. Read yours or ask your agent.
Sudden vs. gradual. A supply line that burst is treated differently from a slow leak that ran for months. Report the date you found it honestly.
Proof of care. Home watch reports, utility bills showing normal water use and smart thermostat or leak-sensor logs help show the home was checked and when the damage began.
Mold limits. Many Florida policies cap mold coverage.
Tell it plainly. Tell the adjuster when you left, how the house was checked and when you found the damage. Don't guess at the cause; let the inspection show it.
Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .

What a Good Home Watch Visit Covers in Lee County
Home watch can't stop a pipe from failing, but a thorough visit catches a leak in days instead of months. Ask for visits that include:
A walk through every room, with dated photos sent to you.
The AC: is it running, is the drain pan dry, and what do the thermostat and humidity read?
Ceilings under the attic AC and bathrooms, and along exterior walls.
Under every sink, around toilets, behind the washer and at the water heater.
Running water in each sink and tub and flushing each toilet so drain traps don't dry out.
A check of doors, windows and the roof line after every major storm, as soon as it's safe.
A written report you can keep for your insurer.

Questions About Water Damage in Vacant Fort Myers Homes
I came back to a wet floor. Can I just dry it with fans?
Only if it's a small, recent spill on a hard floor. If water sat for days or reached under flooring, cabinets or walls, it needs moisture mapping and commercial drying, or it will keep feeding mold.
Will insurance cover water damage if my house was empty?
It depends on your policy's vacancy or unoccupancy wording and whether the leak was sudden or gradual. Read the policy and document everything before cleanup.
The AC was off when I got back and there's mold. What now?
Don't run the AC hard until it's checked, keep windows closed and photograph the mold. Bring in a qualified Florida mold remediation company for removal. Drying and humidity control stop it from getting worse.
Why does my house smell like sewer after months away?
Usually the water in the drain traps has dried up and sewer gas is coming through. Run water in every sink, tub, shower and floor drain and flush each toilet. If the smell stays, have a plumber check the line.
How long does drying take after a long leak?
Clean-water drying often takes about 3 to 5 days, but long-running leaks usually need tear-out first and more time on concrete slabs.
Can home watch prevent this?
It can't stop a pipe from failing, but regular visits catch leaks early, and documented visits help with insurance questions.
What if a hurricane hits while I'm away?
Have someone check the house as soon as it's safe and again a few days later, confirm the AC restarted after the power came back, and report any damage to your insurer right away.
What's the first thing to check when I get back?
Smell the air, then check the AC closet, under the kitchen sink, around toilets and at the water heater. That is where most leaks in empty homes start.
Is there help for snowbirds returning to Fort Myers, Estero or Bonita Springs?
Yes. Help for homes found wet or musty after time away covers Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Estero , Bonita Springs , Fort Myers Beach and the rest of Lee County . Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7.

## What to Do After Water Damage in Fort Myers: Checklist
https://fortmyerswaterdamagerestoration.us/first-hour-checklist/

Emergency Service · Answered 24/7
What to Do in the First Hour After Water Damage in Fort Myers
Water on the floor, dripping through the ceiling or backing up from a drain? Don't panic, and don't start tearing things out yet. What you do in the next hour decides how much of your home has to be replaced later. This checklist walks Fort Myers and Lee County homeowners through each step, in order. If you need help at any point, call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7.
Call 239-356-3708
Answered 24/7 · Moisture readings taken · Written scope before rebuild
Read the intro ↓
Home
»
What to Do in the First Hour After Water Damage in Fort Myers
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
In the first hour after water damage: (1) make it safe by cutting power to wet areas, (2) stop the water at the fixture or main, (3) photograph everything, (4) move belongings out of the water, and (5) report the loss and start drying. Clean water can turn contaminated within 24 to 48 hours.
Guide
The First-Hour Checklist for Fort Myers Homes, Minute by Minute
Minutes 0 to 5: Make it safe
Turn off power at the breaker to any room where water touches outlets, cords, appliances or a light fixture. If the panel is wet or you'd have to stand in water to reach it, don't; call an electrician or your utility.
Get people and pets out from under any sagging or bulging ceiling.
Keep everyone away from sewage. Toilet, drain or floodwater is Category 3 and can make people sick.
Never use a household vacuum on water.
Minutes 5 to 10: Stop the water
Close the fixture valve under the sink or behind the toilet if that's the source.
Turn off the main shut-off if you can't find the source or the fixture valve won't close. In most Fort Myers slab homes it's where the line enters the house, often near the garage, or at the meter box near the street.
On a private well, common in Lehigh Acres, also turn off the well pump at its breaker.
For an AC leak, turn the system off at the thermostat.
For a water heater, close the cold-water valve on top and turn off its power or gas.
For a sewage backup, stop using all water in the house: no flushing, showers, laundry or dishwasher.
For rain or a roof leak, you can't stop it from inside. Catch the water and protect what's below.
Minutes 10 to 20: Photograph and record
Take wide photos of every wet room, then close-ups of the water line on walls, stains, the source and damaged belongings.
Record a short video walking through the house.
Write down the time you found the water and what you saw.
Keep damaged items until your insurer says you can throw them out, or photograph them first if they must go.
Minutes 20 to 40: Protect your home and belongings
Move rugs, electronics, papers and small furniture out of the water.
Put foil or plastic under furniture legs so wood and fabric don't wick water.
Hang wet rugs and drapes away from walls.
Open cabinet doors under sinks so air reaches the wet base.
Keep the AC running if it's safe and not the source; it pulls humidity down. Don't open windows on a humid Florida day; it usually adds moisture.
Minutes 40 to 60: Start drying and report it
Call for water removal and drying. Standing water and hidden moisture in walls, under tile and in the slab need commercial equipment and moisture readings.
Call a plumber, roofer or HVAC technician to fix the source if it isn't already fixed.
Report the loss to your insurer. Florida generally requires notice of a new property claim within one year of the date of loss, but reporting the same day is always better.
In a condo, tell building management and the unit above or below. See condo water damage .
Guide
What to Do First in a Fort Myers Home, by Type of Water Damage
What happened First move Next step

AC leaking through the ceiling or closet Turn the AC off at the thermostat AC leak water damage

Guide
Extra First-Hour Steps After a Storm or Flood in Lee County
Storm water brings risks a pipe leak doesn't. Add these to the checklist:
Smell gas? Leave. Get everyone out and call the gas company or 911 from outside.
Don't go back in until officials say it is safe, and never walk or drive through moving water.
Run generators outside only, well away from doors, windows and the garage.
Keep the power off if water reached outlets, the panel or appliances, until an electrician checks it.
Photograph the water line on inside and outside walls before anything is cleaned. It shows how high the water rose.
Follow any boil water notice from your utility before drinking or cooking with tap water.
Treat all floodwater as Category 3. Keep children and pets out of it, inside and in the yard.
Guide
What Not to Do After Water Damage in a Fort Myers Home
Don't walk into standing water with the power on.
Don't use a household vacuum or regular mop on large amounts of water or any sewage.
Don't turn on ceiling fans or lights in rooms with wet ceilings.
Don't tear out drywall or flooring before you photograph it.
Don't paint over stains or re-lay flooring until moisture readings confirm the area is dry.
Don't wait to see if it dries on its own. In Southwest Florida humidity, hidden water in walls and under tile rarely does before mold starts.
Don't sign anything you don't understand. Ask for a written scope before work beyond emergency water removal.
Guide
Why the First 48 Hours Matter So Much in Fort Myers
Time What happens
First hours Water spreads under baseboards, tile and vinyl plank; drywall wicks water upward
24 to 48 hours Clean water can become contaminated; mold can start in humid conditions
After 2 days Particle board cabinets and baseboards swell for good; flooring cups or lifts; odors set in
After a week More material has to be removed and drying takes longer
Fort Myers homes are mostly built on concrete slabs, and the air stays humid most of the year. Water spreads sideways under flooring and stays trapped, which is why fast extraction and structural drying matter more here than in drier climates.
Guide
Before It Happens: Set Up Your Fort Myers Home in 15 Minutes
The first hour goes faster when you've done this once on a calm day.
Find your shut-offs
The main water valve, usually where the line enters the house or near the garage. Tag it so anyone can find it.
The meter box near the street, and whether you need a meter key to turn it.
The valves under each sink, behind each toilet and behind the washer. Turn each one to make sure it moves.
The cold-water valve on top of the water heater.
The well pump breaker, if your home is on a well.
Your breaker panel. Make sure each circuit is labeled.
Put together a small water damage kit
A flashlight and a phone charger or power bank.
Buckets, old towels, a roll of plastic sheeting and squares of foil for furniture legs.
Rubber gloves and boots.
A meter key, if your main is at the street.
A list of numbers: your insurer and policy number, a plumber, your HVAC company, condo management and 239-356-3708 .
Guide
What to Have Ready When You Call for Help in Fort Myers
Your address and the best phone number to reach you.
What happened and when you found it.
Where the water came from, if you know.
Which rooms are wet and roughly how much.
Whether the water is clean, from an appliance, or sewage or floodwater.
Whether the power and water are off.
Your insurance company and policy number, if you plan to file a claim.
For condos: building management's contact information.
For gated communities: gate access instructions.
Guide
What Happens in the Next 1 to 5 Days in a Fort Myers Home
Day 1: water is extracted, moisture is mapped with meters and a thermal camera, materials that can't be saved are removed and drying equipment is set.
Days 2 to 4: moisture readings are taken daily and equipment is moved as areas dry.
Days 3 to 5 for most clean-water jobs: materials reach normal dry readings and equipment is removed. Slabs, hardwood and sewage jobs take longer.
After drying: repairs to drywall, baseboards, flooring and cabinets.
See the full process: what happens after you call .

Insurance Steps in the First Hour for Florida Homeowners
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
Photograph before cleanup and keep damaged items or photos of them.
Take reasonable steps to stop further damage. Most policies expect it, and drying is one of those steps.
Report the claim promptly.
Keep every receipt for emergency work, supplies and any hotel stay.
Know the assignment-of-benefits rule. For Florida policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, you can't sign your insurance benefits over to a contractor after a loss.

Guide
Questions About the First Hour After Water Damage in Fort Myers
What is the first thing to do when you have water damage?
Make it safe: cut power to wet areas at the breaker and keep people away from sagging ceilings and sewage. Then stop the water at the fixture or main shut-off.
Should I call my insurance company or a restoration company first?
Stop the water first. Then start drying and report the claim as soon as you can. Most policies expect you to take reasonable steps to prevent more damage, and waiting for an adjuster before drying usually makes the damage worse.
Should I turn off the electricity if there's water on the floor?
Yes, at the breaker for the affected rooms, but only if you can reach the panel without standing in water. If the panel is wet, stay away and call an electrician or the power company.
Where is the main water shut-off in a Florida house?
Usually where the main line enters the house, often near the garage or an outside wall, or at the meter box near the street, which may need a meter key. Find it before you need it.
Do I need a meter key?
Only if your house valve is missing, stuck or hard to reach and you have to shut the water off at the meter box. A meter key is inexpensive and worth keeping with your flashlight.
Can I use fans and a wet vac myself?
For a small clean-water spill caught right away, yes. If water reached under flooring, into walls, under cabinets or came from a toilet or drain, it needs commercial drying and moisture readings.
Can I use a regular vacuum to suck up water?
No. A household vacuum isn't built for water and can shock you or burn out. A wet/dry shop vac works for small amounts.
Should I stay home tonight or go to a hotel?
Most families can stay after a clean-water leak. Leave if sewage or floodwater is inside, a ceiling is sagging, the power can't be made safe, or the only bathroom or kitchen can't be used. If your home isn't livable after a covered loss, many policies include additional living expenses, so keep hotel and meal receipts and ask your insurer what applies.
What should I do first after a hurricane or flood?
Wait until officials say it's safe, keep the power off if water reached outlets or the panel, run any generator outside only, and photograph the water line before cleanup. Treat all floodwater as Category 3.
Who do I call for water damage at night in Fort Myers?
Call 239-356-3708 . It's answered 24/7, including nights and weekends, for Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Fort Myers Beach , Estero and Bonita Springs .

Please read first: the figures on this page are rough Fort Myers and Southwest Florida ranges, gathered from local price data and regional cost guides. They are a general idea only. They are not an exact estimate, a quote or our pricing. Every job is different, and the real price for your home depends on what got wet, what kind of water it was and how long drying takes. Call 239-356-3708 and ask. A written number comes after the moisture in your home is measured, and before any work beyond emergency water removal.
In the Fort Myers area, most water damage restoration jobs land roughly between $1,200 and $5,500. A small leak caught early can come in well under that, while sewage backups and storm flooding often run $7,000 to $20,000 or more. Repairs after drying are usually priced separately.

Key facts about water damage pricing
Water category is the biggest driver, because it decides how much has to be removed instead of dried.
Equipment is billed by the day, so every extra drying day adds to the bill.
Drying (mitigation) and rebuilding (restoration) usually come as two separate invoices.
Small jobs often cost more per square foot, because the trip, setup and monitoring visits carry minimums.
Your policy wording, not the contractor, decides how much insurance pays.

Water Damage Cost per Square Foot in Fort Myers
What is being priced Rough area range per sq ft
Emergency water extraction About $2 to $7
Structural drying and dehumidification About $3 to $6
Local all-in example: removal, drying, labor and materials About $10 to $11
Flood damage cleanup About $16 to $18
Clean water sits at the low end of each range, and sewage and floodwater sit at the high end, because more has to be removed and the work needs containment and protective gear. In Fort Myers humidity, clean water can turn into Category 2 faster than it would in a dry climate, which moves the price up.
Water category Typical sources in Fort Myers homes Effect on the price
Category 1, clean Supply line, water heater, AC condensate, rain before it touches the ground Lowest; often dried in place
Category 2, gray Washing machine, dishwasher, toilet overflow without waste, clean water left a day or two Higher; carpet pad and lower drywall often removed
Category 3, black Sewage backup, cracked cast iron drain, floodwater, storm surge Highest; porous materials removed and containment needed
More on contaminated water: sewage backup cleanup .
Guide
Damage Class: Why Two Fort Myers Leaks of the Same Size Are Priced Differently
The IICRC S500 standard also rates how much water the materials soaked up and how hard they are to dry. This is the class of water damage, and it changes how much equipment a job needs.
Class What it means Fort Myers example Effect on the price
Class 1 Little water absorbed, small area AC pan overflow onto tile, wiped up quickly Fewest machines, shortest drying
Class 2 A whole room wet; carpet and lower walls wicking water Toilet supply line soaking bedroom carpet and the bottom of the wall More air movers and more removal
Class 3 The most absorbent materials soaked, often from water coming down from above Attic air handler overflow through a hallway ceiling into the carpet below Ceiling drywall and insulation often removed; more equipment
Class 4 Dense materials holding water deep inside Water under tile and vinyl plank on the slab, hardwood, concrete block Specialty drying and extra days
Guide
What Goes on a Fort Myers Water Damage Estimate, Line by Line
Most water damage estimates in Florida are itemized. These are the lines you are likely to see, how each one is usually billed and what to check:
Line item How it is usually billed What to check
Emergency water extraction By square foot or by the hour Matches the wet area and the meter readings
LGR dehumidifier Per unit, per day Count and days match the drying log
Desiccant dehumidifier Per unit, per day Used for slabs and dense materials, not on every job
Air mover Per unit, per day Roughly one for every 10 to 16 feet of wet wall
Moisture monitoring Per visit or per day Readings recorded at every visit
Antimicrobial treatment By square foot Listed for gray and black water, or where it is needed
Carpet pad removal By square foot, plus disposal Square footage matches the wet area
Flood cut and drywall removal By square foot or linear foot Cut height matches the wet line on the meter
How many machines does one room need? Under IICRC S500 drying guidance, a common starting point is about one air mover for every 10 to 16 linear feet of wet wall, with dehumidifiers sized to the room's volume and how wet it is. A 12-by-14-foot bedroom with two wet walls often gets three or four air movers and one LGR dehumidifier. Because every machine is billed by the day, each extra drying day adds the day rate of every machine in the house.
Guide
Why Water Damage Can Run Higher in a Fort Myers Home
Humidity. Fort Myers air stays humid most of the year, so wet materials rarely dry on their own and drying leans hard on dehumidifiers. Wetter air can mean more equipment or more days.
Block walls with furring strips. Interior drywall on concrete block usually sits on wood strips. Water wicks into the gap behind it, so baseboards come off and the bottom of the wall is often opened to dry the cavity.
Slab floors with vinyl plank. Water runs under floating floors along the slab. Plank is often lifted, and concrete gives up water slowly.
Attic air handlers and AC closets. An overflow in the attic soaks insulation and ceiling drywall, which usually come out. See AC leak water damage .
Condo buildings. One leak can reach two or three units, each with its own owner and insurer, plus building rules for access, elevators and work hours.
Saltwater storm surge. Surge water is Category 3, and salt left in walls and outlets adds cleaning and electrical checks.
Older drain lines. Cast iron failing under a slab adds plumbing repair, trenching and Category 3 cleanup. See cast iron pipe water damage .
Empty seasonal homes. A leak that ran for weeks means more tear-out, more drying days and often mold. See water damage in vacant homes .
After a big storm. Demand across Lee County climbs fast, and crews and equipment are stretched.
Access. Gated communities, high-rise condos, island homes and attics all add labor time.
Guide
Typical Fort Myers Jobs and Where They Usually Land
These show where common Fort Myers jobs usually fall in the rough area ranges above. They are not an estimate or a quote for your home, and your real price depends on the job.
1 AC overflow from a ground-floor closet into the hallway carpet, clean water, caught the same day. Usually a small or one-room job, from about $500 to $3,500, and the carpet pad is often replaced.
2 Toilet supply line in a second-floor condo that reaches the ceiling of the unit below. Two units to dry, often with two owners and two insurers. Condo and high-rise jobs often run 20% to 40% more than the same damage in a house. See condo water damage .
3 Dishwasher leak found a week later under a full run of kitchen cabinets. Gray water by then, with swollen particle board bases. Drying alone often lands in the one-room range, and replacing cabinets at about $200 to $800 or more each usually costs more than the drying.
4 Cast iron drain failure under a 1970s slab home. Sewage cleanup in the bathroom and hallway often lands around $7,000 to $20,000 or more, before the plumbing repair, the trench through the slab and new flooring.
5 Supply line that ran for three weeks in an empty seasonal home. Several rooms, wet walls and often mold, which frequently puts drying in the $8,000 to $15,000 range, with mold removal and rebuilding on top.
6 Storm surge through a first floor. About $15,000 to $50,000 or more, and rising water is a flood claim, not a homeowners claim.
Minimum charges for the trip, setup and monitoring visits mean even a very small job has a starting price.
Guide
How Fort Myers Water Damage Estimates Are Priced
Most insurers and many restoration companies write water damage estimates in Xactimate, estimating software that prices each line item from a price list set by ZIP code. Those price lists are updated monthly, so an estimate for a Fort Myers address reflects local labor and material prices for that month.
Ask for the estimate line by line, not as one lump sum.
When two estimates differ, compare the scope first: square footage, number of machines, drying days and what is being removed. That is usually where most of the gap sits.
Ask for the moisture readings and photos behind each line, so you and your adjuster can see why it is there.
Guide
What a Fair Fort Myers Water Damage Estimate Should Include
The water category and class
Square footage of each affected room
Extraction, by square foot or by the hour
Each machine, with the number of days it runs
Monitoring visits and daily moisture readings
Antimicrobial treatment, if it is used
Materials removed (carpet, pad, drywall, baseboards, cabinets) and disposal
Photos of the damage before anything is torn out
What is not included, such as rebuilding, plumbing or mold work
Warning signs in an estimate
One lump-sum number with no line items.
Equipment left running with no daily moisture readings.
A request to sign over your insurance benefits. For Florida policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, post-loss assignment of benefits isn't allowed.
Pressure to sign the same day for anything beyond emergency water removal.
Tear-out that the moisture readings don't support.
How drying is measured: structural drying .

Guide
What Waiting Does to the Price in a Fort Myers Home
When drying starts What usually happens
Same day Clean water is often dried in place; drywall and carpet are frequently saved
Day 2 to 3 Water may be treated as Category 2; carpet pad, lower drywall and swollen baseboards usually come out
Day 7 and later Cabinets, flooring and more drywall are often lost; mold becomes likely; drying and repairs both climb
In Fort Myers heat and humidity, each step can come sooner.
Guide
Costs Fort Myers Homeowners Often Forget
Fixing the cause. The plumber, roofer or HVAC technician who repairs the leak bills separately.
Matching flooring. Tile and vinyl plank often run through the whole house. Under Florida Statute 626.9744, when replaced items don't match in quality, color or size, a homeowners insurer must make reasonable repairs or replacement in adjoining areas, unless the policy says otherwise. Some policies now limit matching, so check yours.
Contents. Packing out, cleaning and storing furniture and belongings is priced separately, per item, box or hour.
Somewhere to stay. A hotel and meals if the home isn't livable; many policies include additional living expense.
Permits. Rebuilding drywall, electrical or plumbing can need a permit from your building department.
Your deductible. It comes off the claim payment first.
Guide
How Insurance Changes What You Pay in Fort Myers
This is general information, not advice about your policy. Your policy wording decides your coverage.
Deductible first. Leaks and appliance failures usually fall under your all other perils (AOP) deductible. Hurricane damage usually has its own deductible, often a percentage of dwelling coverage.
Sudden vs gradual. A sudden burst or overflow is often covered for the resulting damage; a slow leak that ran for months is often excluded.
Water damage caps. Some Florida policies carry a limited water damage endorsement that caps plumbing-leak losses, often at $10,000 per loss. On a $14,000 loss, the amount above the cap, plus your deductible, may be yours to pay.
Citizens policies. Citizens Property Insurance Corporation, Florida's state-backed insurer, offers free emergency water removal through its own program for eligible non-weather water losses. Its published materials say that if you use your own mitigation contractor instead, emergency water mitigation is limited to $3,000, and permanent repairs outside its managed repair program can be capped at $10,000. Check your own policy before you hire.
Who pays whom. For Florida policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, you can't assign your benefits to a contractor after a loss. Your contract is with the restoration company, and insurance checks are often made out to you and sometimes your mortgage company too.
Flood is separate. Rising water and storm surge need a flood policy from the NFIP or a private insurer, not your homeowners policy.
Hotel and meals. Many policies include additional living expense when a covered loss makes your home unlivable. Keep every receipt.
Guide
Lee County's 50% Rule and Your Repair Total
If your home sits in a FEMA flood zone that starts with A or V, the repair total matters for more than the bill. Building departments in Lee County compare the price of repairing the building with its market value. At 50% or more, the building has to meet current flood rules, which can mean raising it.
Damage of any origin counts, not only floodwater.
Repairs from the same event are added together.
Work you do yourself still counts.
A clear, itemized scope shows the building department exactly what is being repaired. Ask the department that issues your permit before you plan the rebuild. More on the 50% rule: water damage restoration in Fort Myers.
Guide
How to Keep the Water Damage Bill Down in Fort Myers
Stop the water at the fixture or main shut-off right away.
Start drying the same day. Every day of delay adds tear-out and equipment days.
Move belongings off wet floors so contents don't add to the bill.
Photograph everything before tear-out; it can prevent a claim dispute later.
Ask for daily moisture readings, so equipment comes out as soon as the readings say dry.
Fix the cause properly: an AC float switch, new braided supply lines, a water heater pan.
Check your policy for water caps and insurer programs before you hire.
Guide
Is It Cheaper to Dry It Yourself in Fort Myers?
For a small clean-water spill on tile caught within minutes, yes. Towels, a wet vac and the AC running usually handle it. Renting a dehumidifier and air movers can work for a small area, but rental gear is only as good as the moisture readings behind it.
The catch in Fort Myers is hidden moisture. Without a moisture meter, water under vinyl plank, behind baseboards or inside cabinet bases is easy to miss, and in this humidity it turns into mold, swelling and a bigger bill later. Doing it yourself also leaves you without the readings and drying logs an insurer may ask for.
Guide
Questions About Water Damage Restoration Cost in Fort Myers
How much does water damage restoration cost in Fort Myers?
Most jobs in the Fort Myers area land roughly between $1,200 and $5,500. That is a rough idea, not an exact estimate or pricing. Every job is different, so call 239-356-3708 and ask about yours.
How much does it cost to dry out a house after a leak?
Rough Florida figures put structural drying at about $3 to $6 per square foot, with extraction on top when there is standing water. The real number depends on how far the water spread and how many days drying takes.
What is the price per square foot for water damage restoration?
As a rough area idea: extraction about $2 to $7 and drying about $3 to $6 per square foot, with local all-in examples around $10 to $11 per square foot and flood cleanup closer to $16 to $18. Clean water sits at the low end and sewage at the high end.
Are condo water damage jobs more expensive in Fort Myers?
Often, yes. South Florida cost guides put condo and high-rise losses about 20% to 40% higher than a house with the same damage, because water reaches more than one unit and building access, elevators and work hours add time.
Why can't I get an exact price over the phone?
The price depends on how far water spread inside walls and under flooring, and that only shows up with moisture meters and a thermal camera on site.
Does the restoration price include repairs?
Usually not. Water removal and drying are one invoice; drywall, flooring, cabinets and paint are another. Ask which parts are included before you sign.
Why did my estimate go up after the first day?
Moisture readings often show water spread farther than you could see, which adds square footage, removal or drying days. Ask for the moisture map and photos behind any change.
Is mold removal included in water damage restoration?
No. If mold has already grown, removal is separate work by a qualified Florida mold remediation company, with its own price.
Will I pay my deductible to the restoration company?
Often, yes. Insurance pays covered amounts above your deductible, so that part is usually yours, paid to the company directly or out of the claim payment.
What is the $3,000 water mitigation limit on some Florida policies?
Some policies, including Citizens policies for non-weather water losses, limit emergency water mitigation to $3,000 if you don't use the insurer's own water removal program. Check your declarations page or ask your agent before work starts.
Is it worth filing a claim for a small leak?
If the loss is close to your deductible, maybe not, since claims history can affect renewal. Fast drying still saves money either way by limiting tear-out.
Does the price differ in Cape Coral, Lehigh Acres or Estero?
The same drivers apply across Lee County: water category, square footage, materials and drying days. For a written number for your home in Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , Estero or Bonita Springs , call 239-356-3708 .

## Does Insurance Cover Water Damage in Fort Myers, Florida?
https://fortmyerswaterdamagerestoration.us/insurance/

Emergency Service · Answered 24/7
Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Water Damage in Fort Myers?
Often yes, when the water escaped suddenly: a burst supply line, a failed water heater or an AC pan overflowing from an attic air handler. Often no, when it came from a slow leak, rising floodwater without a flood policy, or a sewer backup without the right endorsement. This guide explains how Florida policies usually handle each case, what Lee County homeowners should check on their own policy and what Florida law requires of insurers.

Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Water Damage in Fort Myers?
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
General information only: this page is not legal or insurance advice. Your policy wording decides your coverage, so read your declarations page and endorsements and ask your agent or insurer.
Florida homeowners policies usually cover sudden and accidental water damage, like a burst pipe or an AC overflow, but often exclude long-term seepage, flood and sewer backup without an endorsement. Many also cap plumbing-leak damage through a limited water damage endorsement. Notice of a new claim is generally due within one year of the date of loss.
Fort Myers water damage
Usually covered by homeowners insurance?
Burst supply line, failed water heater, AC overflow Often, for the resulting damage
Slow leak that ran for weeks or months Often excluded as gradual
Rising water, storm surge, canal overflow No; needs a separate flood policy
Sewage or drain backup Only with a water backup endorsement
Roof leak after wind damage Often; a hurricane deductible may apply
Mold from a covered leak Often limited to a set amount
The broken pipe, AC unit or water heater itself Usually not
Key facts about water damage insurance in Florida
Sudden and accidental is the rule behind most decisions; gradual leaks are a common exclusion.
Flood needs a separate policy from the NFIP or a private flood insurer, and Citizens now requires flood coverage on its home policies that include wind.
Sewer and drain backup usually needs a water backup endorsement.
Condo owners split coverage with the association under Florida Statute 718.111(11).
New and reopened claims: generally one year from the date of loss; supplemental claims: generally 18 months.
Your insurer generally must acknowledge your claim within 7 days and pay or deny within 60 days.
