Wind tears off shingles or tiles and rain gets in Often Wind-created opening; a hurricane deductible may apply
An old, worn roof leaks in a summer downpour Often excluded Wear and tear
Slow drip under a sink, or a shower pan leaking for months Often excluded Gradual or repeated seepage
Storm surge or rising water from a canal or street Not under homeowners Needs a separate flood policy
Sewage backs up through a tub or floor drain Only with a water backup endorsement Commonly excluded otherwise
A cast iron drain under the slab corrodes and leaks Pipe usually excluded; resulting damage sometimes covered Wear and tear vs sudden failure
Mold after a covered leak Often limited or capped Mold limits are common
Related guides: AC leak water damage , burst pipe water damage and cast iron pipe water damage .
Guide
Sudden vs Gradual: The Rule Behind Most Fort Myers Water Claims
Most Florida water claims turn on one question: did the water escape suddenly, or did it leak over time?
Sudden and accidental: a supply line bursts, a water heater fails, an AC pan overflows. These are the losses policies are built to cover.
Gradual, continuous or repeated: a slow drip under a sink, a shower pan leaking into the slab for months, a cast iron drain seeping under the floor. Many policies exclude this.
In a humid Fort Myers home, a slow leak usually leaves its own evidence: a musty smell, swollen baseboards or a stain that spread over weeks. Adjusters look at exactly those signs. Report the date you discovered the damage truthfully and don't guess at how long it was leaking. The plumber's report, photos, moisture readings and water bills show what happened.
Guide
Flood vs Water Damage for Lee County Homes
Standard Florida homeowners policies don't cover flooding, meaning surface water that rises from outside: storm surge, an overflowing canal, a flooded street or heavy rain pooling against the house.
Flood insurance comes from the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) or a private flood insurer.
New NFIP policies usually have a 30-day waiting period, so buying one when a storm is already forecast is usually too late.
Wind-driven rain through a storm-damaged roof or window is usually a homeowners claim, while rising water is a flood claim. After hurricanes, adjusters often have to separate the two in the same house, so photograph the water line on the walls before cleanup.
In FEMA flood zones that start with A or V, lenders usually require flood insurance on a mortgaged home.
See flood and storm cleanup .
Guide
Citizens Policies in Lee County: Water Limits and the Flood Requirement
Citizens Property Insurance Corporation, Florida's state-backed insurer, covers many Lee County homes. Its policies have rules worth knowing before you hire anyone.
Free emergency water removal. Citizens offers free water removal and drying through its own program for eligible non-weather water losses, like a burst pipe or an appliance leak.
A $3,000 limit if you use your own company. Citizens' published materials say that if you choose your own mitigation contractor instead, emergency water mitigation is limited to $3,000, less any applicable deductible.
A $10,000 limit on repairs outside its program. For non-weather water losses, permanent repairs done outside its Managed Repair Contractor Network can be capped at $10,000, and that cap is reduced by what was paid for outside mitigation.
Flood insurance is becoming mandatory. Under Florida law, Citizens home policies that include wind coverage need a separate flood policy. The requirement has been phasing in by dwelling value, and from January 1, 2027 it applies to all of them, in every flood zone. Condo unit-owner policies, renters policies and policies without wind coverage are not included.
If Citizens insures your home, call Citizens or check your policy before any work beyond emergency water removal starts.
Guide
Sewer and Drain Backup Coverage for Fort Myers Homes
Water and sewage that back up through a toilet, tub or floor drain are often excluded from standard policies unless you added a water backup or sewer backup endorsement. That endorsement usually has its own limit, often far below the dwelling limit, so check the dollar amount on your declarations page. In older Fort Myers neighborhoods with cast iron drains, it is one of the most useful endorsements to carry. See sewage backup cleanup .
Guide
Condo Water Damage Insurance in Fort Myers: Association vs HO-6
Under Florida Statute 718.111(11), the condo association's policy generally covers the building as originally installed. Unit owners generally insure their own floor, wall and ceiling coverings, electrical fixtures, appliances, water heaters, cabinets, countertops and personal property, usually with an HO-6 policy.
If the leak started in another owner's unit, that owner's insurer may also be involved.
The association's master policy has its own deductible, and associations can pass some losses on to owners through assessments. Loss assessment coverage on an HO-6 policy can help with that.
Condo unit-owner policies are not part of the Citizens flood requirement.
See condo water damage .
Guide
Water Damage Limits and Endorsements on Fort Myers Policies
Many Florida homeowners policies now carry a limited water damage endorsement, sometimes called an LWD endorsement or a water damage limitation. It is most common on older homes, it is sometimes chosen for a lower premium, and it can be added at renewal without the homeowner noticing.
The cap. It limits what the policy pays for certain water losses, such as a plumbing leak or an appliance discharge, to a fixed amount per loss. A $10,000 limit per loss is common, even when the dwelling limit is far higher.
Tear-out. Some endorsements say the cap also covers tearing out and replacing walls or floors to reach the pipe; others don't mention tear-out. Florida appeals courts have read the exact wording of each endorsement to decide which applies.
Exclusion plus endorsement. It often sits alongside a water damage exclusion, so the endorsement may be the only coverage for that kind of loss.
Emergency measures limits. Some policies cap emergency water mitigation, like the Citizens $3,000 limit above.
Matching limits. Under Florida Statute 626.9744, when replaced items don't match in quality, color or size, a homeowners insurer must make reasonable repairs or replacement in adjoining areas, unless the policy says otherwise. Some newer policies limit matching, which matters for tile or vinyl plank that runs through the whole house.
Mold limits. Often a small fixed amount.
How to check your policy
Look at the declarations page and the endorsement list for words like "Limited Water Damage", "Water Damage Limitation", "Water Damage Exclusion" or "Matching".
Ask your agent: "Is water damage from a plumbing leak capped on my policy, and does the cap include tear-out?"
Read every renewal, because endorsements are sometimes added there.
When coverage is capped, keeping the scope to what the moisture readings support matters even more. Ask for the written scope before any work beyond emergency water removal, and send a copy to your adjuster.
Guide
Deductibles and Policy Terms Fort Myers Homeowners Should Know
All other perils (AOP) deductible. The usual deductible for leaks and appliance failures.
Hurricane deductible. Florida insurers must offer hurricane deductible options of $500, 2%, 5% or 10% of the dwelling limit, with some exceptions for higher-value homes, and the dollar amount must appear on your declarations page.
Once per calendar year. On a personal residential policy, the hurricane deductible applies on an annual basis to all hurricane losses in the same calendar year with the same insurer, not once per storm.
What it means in dollars. On a home insured for $400,000, a 2% hurricane deductible is $8,000 and a 5% deductible is $20,000.
Separate water deductibles. Some Florida policies carry their own deductible or limit for non-weather water losses.
Roof settlement and wind exclusions. Some Florida policies pay for roofs on a depreciated schedule, and some exclude wind entirely, which sends a wind-driven roof leak to a separate wind policy. Check both before storm season.
Guide
Florida Deadlines for a Fort Myers Water Damage Claim
Claim type General deadline
New claim Notice within 1 year of the date of loss
Reopened claim Within 1 year of the date of loss
Supplemental claim for more money on the same loss Within 18 months of the date of loss
These are outer limits. Most policies also require prompt notice, so report a water loss as soon as you can.
Guide
What Your Insurer Must Do for a Fort Myers Claim Under Florida Law
Florida Statute 627.70131 sets deadlines for residential property claims:
Step Florida deadline
Acknowledge your claim communication Within 7 calendar days
Begin investigating Within 7 days after receiving your proof-of-loss statement
Physical inspection, if one is needed Within 30 days after receiving your proof-of-loss statement
Send you a copy of any detailed loss estimate Within 7 days after the adjuster prepares it
Pay or deny all or part of the claim Within 60 days after notice, unless factors beyond the insurer's control prevent it
The insurer must explain in writing why it paid, denied or partly denied the claim, and explain the difference when it pays less than a detailed estimate.
The adjuster who inspects must identify themselves to you in writing.
Within 14 days after you first report a claim, your insurer must send you the Homeowner Claims Bill of Rights, a plain-language summary of these rights.
Keep a log of every call, email and adjuster visit, with dates and names. Questions can go to the Florida Department of Financial Services Insurance Consumer Helpline at 1-877-693-5236.
Guide
Assignment of Benefits Is Gone: Who Pays Whom in Fort Myers Now
An assignment of benefits (AOB) used to let homeowners sign insurance benefits over to a contractor, who then billed the insurer directly. For residential and commercial property policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, Florida law bars assigning post-loss benefits.
Your contract for the work is between you and the company you hire.
Your insurer pays under your policy, often with checks made out to you and sometimes your mortgage company too.
Mortgage companies often hold large checks and release the money in stages as repairs are done.
Be cautious with anyone who asks you to sign over your benefits.
Guide
How to Protect Your Fort Myers Water Damage Claim
Stop the water and make it safe.
Photograph and video everything before cleanup: the source, every wet room, the water line on the walls and damaged belongings.
Take reasonable steps to prevent more damage. Emergency water removal and structural drying count, and waiting for an adjuster before drying usually makes the damage worse.
Keep damaged materials or photos of them, and a list of damaged belongings with their age and what they were worth.
Keep moisture readings and drying logs. They show what was wet and when it was dry.
Keep the invoice from the plumber, roofer or HVAC technician that says what failed.
Report the claim promptly, and write down your claim number and the adjuster's name.
Be there for the adjuster's inspection and walk them through the moisture map.
Ask for written scopes before work beyond emergency water removal, and send copies to your adjuster.
Guide
Will Insurance Pay for a Hotel While Your Fort Myers Home Dries?
Many homeowners policies include additional living expense or loss of use coverage, which can pay for a hotel, meals and other extra living expenses if a covered loss makes your home unlivable. Sewage, a flooded kitchen or the only bathroom out of service are common reasons. Keep every receipt and ask your adjuster before booking a long stay.
Guide
Seasonal and Vacant Homes in Lee County
Many policies limit some coverage when a home sits vacant or unoccupied for a set number of consecutive days, and some expect the water to be shut off while you're away. Read that section of your policy before you leave for the season. Home watch reports, leak sensor logs and normal utility records help show when damage happened. See water damage in vacant homes .
Guide
Older Fort Myers Homes: Plumbing and Insurability
Many Florida insurers ask for a four-point inspection on older homes, covering the roof, electrical, plumbing and HVAC. Older plumbing, like polybutylene supply lines or cast iron drains, can make coverage harder to get or lead to exclusions. Replacing it can help with insurability and lowers the risk of the next leak. See cast iron pipe water damage and slab leak water damage .
Guide
If Your Fort Myers Water Damage Claim Is Denied or Underpaid
Read the letter. Find the exact policy language the insurer relied on.
Ask for the reports. Request the adjuster's report and any engineer or plumber reports.
Send what's missing. Photos, plumber reports, moisture logs, receipts and water bills.
Free mediation. The Florida Department of Financial Services runs a mediation program for many residential property claim disputes.
Appraisal. Many policies have an appraisal clause for disputes about the amount of the loss.
Public adjusters. They negotiate claims for a fee. Florida caps their fees at 10% of payments on claims from a declared emergency in the first year, and 20% on other claims.
Before a lawsuit. Florida requires written notice of intent to sue at least 10 business days before filing, and only after the insurer has made a coverage decision. The insurer must respond in writing within 10 business days.
Coverage disputes. Talk with a Florida property insurance attorney.
Guide
Questions About Water Damage Insurance in Fort Myers
Does homeowners insurance cover a burst pipe in Florida?
Usually yes for the water damage the burst causes, such as wet drywall, flooring and cabinets. Repairing the pipe itself may not be covered.
Does insurance cover AC leak water damage in Fort Myers?
Often for sudden overflows that damage ceilings, walls and floors. The AC repair itself usually isn't covered, and leaks that ran for weeks may be excluded.
Is a slab leak covered by homeowners insurance?
The resulting damage to floors, walls and cabinets often is, when the leak was sudden. The pipe repair may not be, though some policies pay to break out the slab to reach it.
Is mold from a water leak covered?
Sometimes, usually up to a mold limit, and usually only when the mold came from a covered water loss.
How long do I have to file a water damage claim in Florida?
Florida law generally requires notice of a new claim within one year of the date of loss, and supplemental claims within 18 months. Your policy may also require prompt notice.
Can a restoration company bill my insurance directly in Florida?
Not through an assignment of benefits on policies issued on or after January 1, 2023. Your contract is with the company you hire, and your insurer pays under your policy.
Do I have to use my insurer's water removal program?
Usually not, but some policies limit what they pay if you don't. Citizens, for example, limits emergency water mitigation to $3,000 for eligible non-weather losses when you use your own company instead of its free program. Check your policy before work starts.
Does my Citizens policy require flood insurance?
If your Citizens home policy includes wind coverage, yes, under a phased Florida requirement that reaches all of those policies on January 1, 2027. Condo unit-owner and renters policies are not included.
What is the $10,000 water damage limit on Florida policies?
It usually comes from a limited water damage endorsement that caps what the policy pays for certain water losses, often plumbing leaks, per loss. Whether the cap also covers tearing out walls or floors depends on the endorsement's wording.
Will my premium go up if I file a water damage claim?
It can. Insurers may look at claims history at renewal. Ask your agent before filing a small claim close to your deductible.
My insurer says the leak was gradual. What now?
Ask for the denial in writing with the policy language it relies on. Gather what shows when the leak started, such as the plumber's report, photos, moisture readings and water bills. You can request free mediation through the Florida Department of Financial Services and talk to a public adjuster or attorney.
Where can I get free help with a Florida insurance claim?
Call the Florida Department of Financial Services Insurance Consumer Helpline at 1-877-693-5236. It answers questions about claims and runs the state's mediation program for many residential disputes.

Burst Pipe Water Damage in Fort Myers, FL
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
When a pipe bursts, close the fixture valve or the main shut-off, cut power to wet rooms, open a low faucet to drain the pressure and photograph everything. A plumber repairs the pipe; the wet drywall, flooring and cabinets still need extraction, moisture mapping and drying, usually about 3 to 5 days for clean water.
Burst pipe in a Fort Myers home
What to know
First move Close the fixture valve or the main shut-off

Key facts about burst pipes in Fort Myers
Freezing is rare here. Most bursts come from aging supply lines, washer hoses, water heater connectors, pinhole leaks in copper and old polybutylene pipe.
Supply-line water is Category 1 (clean) when caught fast, but it can become Category 2 after a day or two.
Pressurized lines release far more water than drain leaks, so the wet area is usually much bigger than the puddle.
Insurance often covers the sudden resulting damage, while the pipe repair itself may not be covered.
Services
Pipe Burst in Your Fort Myers Home? Do This Now
Shut off the water. Use the valve under the sink or behind the toilet for a fixture line. If you can't find it, or the leak is in a wall or ceiling, turn off the main shut-off, usually where the line enters the house, often near the garage.
Main valve stuck? Shut the water at the meter box near the street. Some meters need a meter key.
On a private well, turn off the well pump at its breaker too.
Cut power at the breaker to rooms where water reaches outlets, cords or appliances.
Drain the pressure by opening a faucet at the lowest point of the house.
Turn off the water heater (breaker, or gas to pilot) if the water will be off for a while.
Move belongings out of the water and lift furniture onto blocks or foil.
Photograph the broken pipe or line, the water, wet walls and floors before cleanup.
Call a plumber to repair the pipe, and start water removal and drying the same day.
Every step in one list: the first-hour water damage checklist .
Services
Why Pipes Burst in Fort Myers Homes Without Freezing
Braided supply lines to toilets, sinks and faucets. The rubber inside ages and the line can split without warning.
Washing machine hoses, especially original rubber hoses. See appliance leak water damage .
Water heater connectors and valves in garages, closets and condo utility rooms. See water heater leak cleanup .
Ice maker and refrigerator lines, often thin plastic tubing behind the fridge.
Attic water lines. Many Florida slab homes, especially repiped ones, run water lines through the attic, where a split shows up as a ceiling leak. See ceiling leak water damage .
Pinhole leaks in older copper pipe, which can spray inside a wall for days.
Polybutylene pipe, a gray plastic used in many homes built from roughly 1978 to 1995 and known for sudden failures.
High water pressure, which strains every joint and line in the house.
Lines under the slab. A break below the floor is a slab leak.
On the few cold nights Lee County gets, the pipes most at risk are exposed outdoor lines, hose bibs and irrigation backflow assemblies, not the pipes inside the house.
Services
What Kind of Pipe Is in Your Fort Myers Home?
The type of pipe tells you a lot about how it is likely to fail and what to watch for.
Pipe type Where you see it in Lee County homes How it usually fails What to watch for
Galvanized steel Some of the oldest homes Rusts from the inside, then leaks at the threads Rusty water, low pressure
Copper Common from the 1960s into the 2000s, often under the slab Pinhole leaks, sometimes spraying inside a wall Green stains at fittings, damp drywall, warm floor spots
Polybutylene (gray plastic) Many homes built from about 1978 to 1995 Fittings and pipe crack without warning Gray pipe at the water heater or under sinks
CPVC (cream or tan plastic) Common in Florida homes and repipes, often run through the attic Gets brittle with age and attic heat; cracks at fittings Ceiling stains below attic lines, cracked fittings
PEX (red, blue or white flexible) Newer homes and most repipes Fitting or crimp-ring failures; rodent damage in attics Drips at fittings, ceiling stains
Braided supply lines Every toilet, sink, faucet and ice maker The rubber core ages and the line bursts at the crimp Bulges, rust on the braid, kinks

Signs of a Hidden Burst Pipe in a Fort Myers Home
The sound of running water when every fixture is off
A water meter that keeps moving with everything turned off
On a private well, a pump that keeps kicking on with no water running
A sudden jump in your water bill
Wet or bulging drywall, peeling paint or a damp baseboard
Warm spots on a tile floor (hot water line)
Low water pressure at one or more fixtures
A musty smell in one room, or a new ceiling stain below the attic

How Far Burst Pipe Water Spreads in a Fort Myers Slab Home
Supply lines are under pressure, and a split line can release several gallons a minute until someone shuts the valve. In a Fort Myers slab home, that water:
Spreads under tile, vinyl plank and baseboards across several rooms
Soaks the bottom of drywall, which wicks it upward inside the wall
Gets behind drywall on block walls, into the gap at the furring strips
Runs under kitchen and bathroom cabinets and swells particle board bases. See water damaged kitchen cabinets .
In a condo, travels through the ceiling into the unit below. See condo water damage .
The visible puddle is usually only part of the damage. Moisture meters and a thermal camera show the rest.
Services
Supply Line vs Drain Line Leaks in Fort Myers Homes
Feature Supply line (burst pipe) Drain line
What it carries Fresh, pressurized water Used water and waste
How it leaks Fast, often spraying, until the water is shut off Only when water is used; slower and often hidden
Water category Category 1 if caught fast Category 2 or 3
Typical damage Wide spread across floors and walls Localized, but contaminated
A leaking drain line under the slab is a different problem; see cast iron pipe water damage .

How Burst Pipe Damage Is Cleaned Up and Dried in Fort Myers
1 Plumbing repair
A plumber repairs or replaces the broken section. If the pipe is inside a wall, a section of drywall is opened.
2 Water extraction
Standing water and water held in carpet are removed.
3 Moisture mapping
Meters and a thermal camera find wet areas under flooring and inside walls.
4 Remove what can't be saved
Carpet pad, swollen baseboards and cabinet bases, and drywall that stayed wet too long.

Dehumidifiers and air movers run around the clock, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .

Drywall, baseboards, flooring and cabinets are replaced once everything reads dry.
Most burst pipe jobs involve clean water and dry in about 3 to 5 days if drying starts quickly.

Is Water From a Burst Pipe in Your Fort Myers Home Clean?
Water from a supply line is Category 1, clean water, when it is handled fast. But clean water that sits for 24 to 48 hours can become Category 2, especially once it soaks into carpet, drywall and cabinet bases. In Fort Myers humidity that happens quickly, so the sooner extraction and drying start, the more can be saved.

Does Insurance Cover a Burst Pipe in Fort Myers?
This is general information, not advice about your policy. Usually yes for the water damage a sudden burst causes: wet drywall, flooring, cabinets and belongings. Common limits:
The pipe itself may not be covered, especially if it failed from age or corrosion.
Tear-out to reach the pipe is covered under some policies.
Slow leaks that ran for weeks are often excluded as gradual.
Some Florida policies cap plumbing-leak damage through a limited water damage endorsement, often at $10,000 per loss.
Citizens policies limit emergency water mitigation to $3,000 for eligible non-weather losses if you use your own company instead of its free program.
Vacant homes can have limits after a set number of days unoccupied. See water damage in vacant homes .

How to Prevent the Next Burst Pipe in Your Fort Myers Home
Replace supply lines and hoses on a schedule. Many plumbers suggest replacing braided supply lines every 5 to 10 years, and many manufacturers recommend replacing washer hoses about every five years.
Check your water pressure. Florida's plumbing code calls for a pressure-reducing valve when static water pressure is above 80 psi. A simple gauge on an outdoor spigot reads it.
Know your main shut-off and make sure it turns easily.
Install leak sensors under sinks, behind toilets, at the water heater and washer, or an automatic shut-off valve on the main. Ask your insurer whether it offers a discount for one.
Replace polybutylene if your home still has it, and have old CPVC in the attic checked for brittle fittings.
Turn off the main water when you leave for more than a few days.

Questions About Burst Pipe Water Damage in Fort Myers
What do I do first when a pipe bursts?
Close the fixture valve or the main shut-off, cut power to wet rooms at the breaker, open a low faucet to drain the pressure and photograph everything. Then call a plumber and start drying the same day.
Why do pipes burst in Florida if it doesn't freeze?
Most bursts here come from aging supply lines and hoses, pinholed copper, brittle attic fittings, high water pressure or failing polybutylene, not freezing.
Can drywall be saved after a burst pipe?
Often yes, if the water was clean and drying starts within a day or two. Drywall that stayed wet longer, swelled or grew mold is usually cut out.
How long does it take to dry after a burst pipe?
Most clean-water burst pipe jobs dry in about 3 to 5 days with dehumidifiers and air movers. Wet concrete, hardwood and long leaks take longer.
Does homeowners insurance pay for the plumber?
Policies usually address the resulting water damage. Repairing the pipe itself may not be covered, though some policies pay to open walls or floors to reach it.
Should I turn off the water heater after shutting off the main?
Yes, if the water will be off for a while. Turn off its breaker, or set a gas heater to pilot or vacation.
My pipe burst while I was at work. Is it too late?
No, but act now. Shut off the water, photograph everything and start extraction and drying today. The hours since the break matter more than the amount of water you can see.
Can a burst pipe in the attic damage my ceiling?
Yes. A split attic line soaks insulation and ceiling drywall, which can sag or fall. Turn off power to that room and stay out from under a bulging ceiling.
Should I replace polybutylene pipe?
Most plumbers recommend it, because the pipe and its fittings can fail without warning. Many Florida insurers also ask about polybutylene and may decline or limit coverage for homes that still have it.

Key facts about manufactured home water damage
Homes built after June 15, 1976 are built to the federal HUD code and called manufactured homes; older ones are usually called mobile homes. Both share the same weak points.
Particle board decking swells and loses strength when wet and usually can't be dried back to sound condition.
A leak in the belly may never show inside, only as a sagging bottom board or a rising water bill.
Lee County has many manufactured-home communities, especially in North Fort Myers, parts of Fort Myers and around Bonita Springs and Estero.
Services
Water Leaking in Your Fort Myers Mobile Home? Do This First
Shut off the water. Most manufactured homes have a main valve where the supply line comes up under the home, and many also have a valve at the water heater.
Turn off the water heater at its breaker if it's leaking or the water is off.
Cut power at the breaker to rooms where water reaches outlets or appliances.
Stay off soft spots. Wet particle board can give way under weight.
Look underneath from outside with a flashlight: is the bottom board sagging, torn or dripping?
Photograph everything, inside and under the home, before cleanup.
All first steps in one list: the first-hour water damage checklist .
Services
Why Water Damage Is Different in a Fort Myers Manufactured Home
A slab house sends water across concrete. A manufactured home sits on a steel frame above the ground, and every layer under your feet can hold water.
Layer, from the top down What water does there
Floor covering (carpet, vinyl, plank) Hides the wet decking underneath
Floor decking (particle board, OSB or plywood) Soaks up water, swells and loses strength
Floor joists Stay wet when the decking and insulation around them are wet
Floor insulation Soaks up water like a sponge and holds it against the floor
Ducts and water lines Run through the floor or belly; a leak can flood the ducts
Belly wrap (bottom board) Holds the insulation in place, and holds water from any leak above it
That is why a leak can look small inside while the belly underneath is full of water.

Water heater leak Floor of the water heater closet, often soft; belly under it

Crossover duct under a double-wide Water or condensation in the duct between the two halves

Particle Board, OSB or Plywood Under Your Fort Myers Mobile Home Floor?
Decking Common in What water does to it Can it be dried?
Particle board Many older mobile and manufactured homes Swells, crumbles and loses strength, often for good Rarely, once it has swelled
OSB Many newer manufactured homes Edges swell; holds up better than particle board Sometimes, if caught early
Plywood Some homes and past repairs Handles water best of the three Often, if caught early

How Mobile Home Water Damage Is Dried and Repaired in Fort Myers
1 Stop the source
A plumber repairs the line, fixture or water heater; a roofer or HVAC technician fixes the roof or AC.
2 Remove standing water
Water inside is extracted. See emergency water removal .
3 Map the moisture inside and underneath
Meters and a thermal camera show how far water spread in the floor system and belly.
4 Open the belly
The bottom board is opened where it holds water, the water is drained and soaked insulation is removed.
5 Dry the floor system from above and below
Dehumidifiers and air movers dry the subfloor and belly wrap from above and below, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
6 Replace damaged decking
Particle board that swelled or softened is cut out and replaced.
7 Close it up
New insulation goes in, the bottom board is patched or replaced and sealed, and flooring goes back down. Wet ducts in the belly are checked and cleaned or replaced.
Services
Can a Soft Mobile Home Floor in Fort Myers Be Dried Instead of Replaced?
Sometimes. If clean water was caught within a day or two and the decking is still firm, it can often be dried in place. Particle board that has swelled, crumbled or turned soft has lost its strength and needs to be replaced; walking on it can make it worse. Plywood caught early is the most likely to be saved.
Services
After a Flood: Piers, Tie-Downs and Ducts in Lee County Manufactured Homes
Floodwater or a long leak under the home does more than soak the belly.
Piers and tie-downs. Water can wash out the soil under piers and loosen anchors. Have a qualified manufactured-home installer check them before the home is lived in again.
Ducts. Ducts in the belly that took floodwater are usually replaced, not cleaned.
Electrical. Wiring and junction boxes in the floor system that took floodwater should be checked by a qualified electrician before the power goes back on.
Everything in the belly. Floodwater is Category 3, so wet insulation and bottom board come out, and the framing is cleaned and dried.
Services
Insurance for Manufactured Homes in Fort Myers
This is general information, not advice about your policy. Manufactured homes are usually insured under policies written for them, and the coverage rules are similar to homeowners policies:
Sudden leaks, such as a burst supply line or a failed water heater, are often covered for the resulting damage.
Slow leaks that rotted the floor over months are often excluded as gradual damage or wear and tear.
Flood needs a separate flood policy. Under the NFIP, a manufactured home counts as a building when it is affixed to a permanent foundation.
Mold coverage is often capped.
Photograph the floor and the belly before anything is removed, keep the plumber's invoice and report the claim promptly. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .

How to Protect a Fort Myers Manufactured Home From Water Damage
Check the floor around the toilet, tub and water heater every few months for softness.

Questions About Mobile Home Water Damage in Fort Myers
Why is my mobile home floor soft?
Usually because water has soaked the particle board or OSB decking, most often around a toilet, tub, sink or water heater. Once it softens, it has lost strength and typically needs replacing.
How do I know if there's water in my mobile home's belly?
Look under the home for a sagging, bulging or dripping bottom board, and check for a musty smell from floor vents. A rising water bill with no visible leak is another sign.
Can water in the belly wrap cause mold?
Yes. Wet insulation trapped in the belly stays damp in Florida humidity, which can lead to mold and odors. Opening the belly and drying it quickly prevents that.
Can a water-damaged mobile home floor be repaired?
Particle board that has swelled or gone soft usually has to be cut out and replaced. Plywood caught early can often be dried in place.
Is standing water under my mobile home a problem?
Yes. Water under the home raises humidity in the belly and floor system and invites mold and rot. Find the source, whether a leaking line, an AC drain or poor drainage, and get the belly area dried.
Does insurance cover a rotted mobile home floor?
It depends. A sudden leak is often covered; rot from a slow leak over months is often excluded.
Is my mobile home covered by flood insurance?
Only if you have a flood policy. Under the NFIP, a manufactured home is covered as a building when it is affixed to a permanent foundation, so check how yours is installed and what your policy says.
Who repairs the bottom board and skirting?
The bottom board is opened and patched or replaced as part of the drying and repair. Skirting is taken off for access and put back afterward; check whether your community has rules for it.
How long does it take to fix water damage in a mobile home?
Drying usually takes several days once the belly is opened. Replacing decking, insulation and the bottom board adds time.
Is there mobile home water damage help in North Fort Myers and Pine Island?
Yes. Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for manufactured and mobile homes in North Fort Myers, Fort Myers, Pine Island, Lehigh Acres , Cape Coral , Estero and Bonita Springs .

Key facts about slab leaks in Lee County
Most Fort Myers, Cape Coral and Lehigh Acres homes are slab-on-grade, with supply lines running in or under the concrete.
Hot water line leaks are the ones people notice most, because they warm the floor.
Vinyl plank and laminate trap water against the slab and usually have to be lifted.
Insurance often depends on whether the leak was sudden and whether your policy has tear-out coverage.
Services
Think You Have a Slab Leak in Your Fort Myers Home? Do This First
Check the water meter. Turn off every faucet, appliance and the irrigation. If the meter still moves, water is escaping somewhere.
On a private well, common in parts of Lehigh Acres, listen for the pump kicking on when no water is running.
Shut off the main water if the floor is wet or the meter is spinning fast.
Turn off the water heater at its breaker, or set a gas heater to pilot, if you suspect the hot water line.
Photograph wet areas, warm spots, stained grout and damp baseboards.
Call a plumber for leak detection, then start drying the same day.
More first steps: the first-hour water damage checklist .
Services
Signs of a Slab Leak in a Fort Myers Home
A warm or hot spot on tile or vinyl floors, usually from a hot water line
The sound of running water when nothing is on
A water meter that moves, or a well pump that runs, with every fixture off
A sudden jump in your water bill, or an electric bill that climbs because the water heater never stops
Damp or swollen baseboards with no visible leak above
Dark or wet grout lines, loose or cracked tile, or vinyl plank that lifts
A musty smell or mold along the bottom of walls
Low water pressure
Water pooling near the foundation outside when it hasn't rained
Services
Why Slab Leaks Happen in Fort Myers and Lee County Homes
Slab-on-grade construction is the norm across Lee County. Supply lines run below or inside the concrete, so when one fails, the water has nowhere to go but sideways under your floors. Common causes:
Corrosion of older copper lines, including the thin-wall copper used under many older slabs, which can develop pinholes over time
Abrasion where a pipe rubs against concrete, gravel or another pipe as it expands and contracts with hot water
Ground movement and settling in sandy soil
High water pressure that stresses every joint
Damage or poor installation during original construction
Not every leak under the slab is a supply line. A cracked drain line carries wastewater instead; see cast iron pipe water damage . A leak you can see above the floor is a different job; see burst pipe water damage.
Services
How Fort Myers Plumbers Find a Slab Leak
Method What it tells the plumber
Pressure test Which line is leaking: hot, cold or the main
Acoustic listening Where the water hisses under the floor
Thermal imaging Where a hot water leak is warming the slab
Tracer gas Where a harmless gas pushed through the line comes up, for hard-to-find leaks
Ask for a written leak detection report showing which line failed and where. Your insurer will want it.
Services
Spot Repair, Reroute or Repipe: Slab Leak Repair Options in Fort Myers
Option What it means What happens to your floors When it usually fits
Spot repair Breaking out a small section of slab, fixing the pipe and patching the concrete A hole in the floor where the leak is; flooring there is replaced One leak in an otherwise sound line
Reroute Abandoning the leaking line and running a new one through the walls or attic Little or no slab work; small wall openings Leaks in hard-to-reach spots, or a line likely to leak again
Repipe Replacing the home's supply lines Wall and ceiling openings instead of slab work Repeat leaks or aging copper throughout the house
Slab leak repairs and water line replacements often need a permit from your city or Lee County. Which option fits is the plumber's call.

Concrete slab Soaks up water and releases it slowly; needs extended drying
Tile Often stays if still bonded; grout and slab are dried. Loose or cracked tiles are replaced

How Slab Leak Water Damage Is Dried in Fort Myers
1 Repair the line
The plumber repairs the line and confirms it holds pressure.
2 Extract surface water
Water is extracted from carpet and the floor surface. See emergency water removal .
3 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera map moisture across the slab and up the walls. The wet area is often much bigger than the warm spot.
4 Open what traps water
Vinyl plank or laminate is lifted, baseboards are pulled and drywall is opened where needed.
5 Dry the slab and walls
Dehumidifiers, air movers and sometimes specialty equipment for concrete run with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
6 Repair
Flooring, baseboards, drywall and cabinets go back once the slab and walls read dry.
Services
When Can New Flooring Go Down on a Fort Myers Slab?
Not when the surface feels dry. Concrete keeps releasing water for days or weeks, and Fort Myers humidity slows it down. Vinyl plank, laminate and wood laid on a slab that is still wet can cup, lift or grow mold underneath. Before new flooring goes down, flooring makers usually require a slab moisture test, such as in-slab relative humidity probes under ASTM F2170, and your installer should check the result against the flooring's limits.
Services
Is Slab Leak Water in a Fort Myers Home Clean?
A leaking supply line carries clean water, Category 1, when caught early. Water that has sat under flooring for days or weeks can become Category 2, and long-standing moisture under vinyl plank or carpet often brings mold. The longer a slab leak runs, the more material comes out.
Services
Does Insurance Cover a Slab Leak for Fort Myers Homeowners?
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
The resulting water damage to floors, walls and cabinets is often covered when the leak was sudden.
The pipe repair itself may not be covered.
Tear-out coverage, in some policies, pays to break out the slab or open walls to reach the leak.
Long-running leaks may be excluded as continuous or repeated seepage.
Some Florida policies cap plumbing-leak damage through a limited water damage endorsement, often at $10,000 per loss.
Keep the plumber's leak detection report, photos and your water bills, which can show when the leak started. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Services
Slab Leaks in Cape Coral, Fort Myers and Lehigh Acres
Cape Coral is mostly single-family slab homes, many built between 1970 and 1999. Fort Myers and Lehigh Acres have the same slab construction across older and newer neighborhoods, and parts of Lehigh Acres run on private wells, where a slab leak shows up as a pump that won't rest. Homes with original copper lines, a history of leaks or high water pressure are the most likely to see repeat slab leaks. See water damage restoration in Cape Coral and water damage help in Lehigh Acres .
Services
How to Lower the Risk of Another Slab Leak in Your Fort Myers Home
Have your water pressure checked. Florida's plumbing code calls for a pressure-reducing valve when static pressure is above 80 psi.
Watch your water bill, and check the meter if it jumps.
Install a leak-detecting shut-off valve that closes the main when it senses continuous flow.
Ask about rerouting or repiping if you've had more than one slab leak.
Services
Questions About Slab Leak Water Damage in Fort Myers
How do I know if I have a slab leak?
Turn off every fixture and check the water meter. If it moves, look for warm spots on the floor, damp baseboards or the sound of running water, and call a plumber for leak detection.
How do I check for a slab leak if my home is on a well?
Turn off every fixture and listen at the pressure tank. If the pump kicks on with no water running, water is escaping somewhere. Call a plumber to test the lines.
Is a slab leak an emergency?
Yes, if water is surfacing on the floor or the meter is spinning fast. Shut off the main water and start drying. A slow leak still needs prompt attention before it damages flooring and grows mold.
Can tile be saved after a slab leak?
Often, if it's still firmly bonded. The grout lines and slab are dried in place. Loose, hollow or cracked tile is replaced.
How long does it take to dry a slab after a leak?
Longer than a surface leak. Concrete releases water slowly, so slab drying often takes more than the 3 to 5 days typical for drywall and carpet.
Should I reroute or repair the leaking line?
That's the plumber's call. One leak in an otherwise sound line is often spot-repaired; repeat leaks or old copper often lead to rerouting or repiping.
Can a slab leak damage my foundation?
Most slab leaks that are found and fixed promptly don't. A leak that runs for a long time can wash out sandy soil under the slab in some cases, so if new cracks or settling appear, have the plumber and a structural engineer look.
Can a slab leak cause mold?
Yes. Moisture trapped under vinyl plank, carpet or baseboards for days or weeks can grow mold in Florida humidity. Drying should start as soon as the line is repaired.
Can I stay in my house while the slab is dried?
Usually yes for a clean-water leak, with equipment running in the affected rooms. Large tear-outs or kitchen damage may make some rooms unusable for a while.
Who dries slab leak water damage in Cape Coral or Lehigh Acres?
After the plumber repairs the line, call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, to dry the slab, walls and flooring in Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Lehigh Acres, Estero and Bonita Springs .

Flood and Storm Surge Cleanup in Fort Myers, FL
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
After a flood in Fort Myers, go back only when officials say it's safe, keep the power off until an electrician checks it and photograph the water line. Floodwater is Category 3: wet carpet, drywall below the flood cut and insulation are removed, then the structure is disinfected and dried. Flood policies cover rising water.

Key facts about flood cleanup in Lee County
Floodwater from surge, canals, rivers and streets carries sewage, chemicals, fuel and debris.
Drywall is usually cut about 2 or 4 feet up, or higher, based on moisture readings rather than the visible stain.
New NFIP flood policies usually have a 30-day waiting period.
Mold can start within 24 to 48 hours in Florida humidity, so muck-out and drying should start as soon as it's safe.
Services
Before You Go Back Into a Flooded Fort Myers Home
Wait for the all-clear from Lee County or your city before returning to a flooded area.
Keep the power off. If water reached outlets or the panel, have an electrician check it before the power goes back on.
Smell for gas. If you smell it, leave and call the gas company from outside.
Never run a generator indoors or in a garage. Carbon monoxide kills.
Wear rubber boots, gloves, long sleeves and an N95 mask.
Watch for hazards: sagging ceilings, broken glass, nails and wildlife that came in with the water.
Photograph and video everything before you move or throw anything away, including the water line on the walls.
More first steps: the first-hour water damage checklist .
Services
Why Floodwater Cleanup in Fort Myers Is Different From a Leak
A burst pipe leaks clean water. Floodwater from storm surge, overflowing canals, rivers and street flooding picks up sewage, chemicals, fuel and debris on the way in. It is Category 3, the most contaminated type of water, and that changes the job:
Porous materials it touched are removed, not dried in place.
Hard surfaces are cleaned and disinfected before drying.
Work is done in protective gear with the area contained.
Drying comes after removal, not instead of it.
If the water came up through your drains rather than in from outside, see sewage backup cleanup.
Services
Saltwater Storm Surge in Fort Myers Homes
Surge on Fort Myers Beach, Sanibel, Pine Island, Iona and the Cape Coral canals is saltwater, and salt keeps working after the water leaves.
Electrical. Electrical industry guidance says breakers, outlets, switches and GFCIs that sat in floodwater should generally be replaced, not dried and reused. Saltwater makes that even more important.
Appliances and equipment. Water heaters, washers, dryers, refrigerators and AC condensers that sat in surge are often replaced; have them checked before use.
Block, slab and framing. Salt residue is cleaned off during disinfection so it doesn't keep drawing moisture back into the wall.
Metal parts. Hinges, fasteners and metal studs that took saltwater can corrode over time and should be looked at during the rebuild.
Services
How Flood Cleanup Works in a Fort Myers Home, Step by Step
1 Water removal
Standing water is pumped and extracted. See emergency water removal .
2 Muck-out
Wet carpet, pad, furniture and debris are removed and bagged or set out for curbside debris pickup.
3 Flood cuts
Drywall is cut in a straight line above the highest wet reading, and wet insulation behind it is removed.
4 Remove swollen materials
Particle board cabinets and vanities, baseboards, door casings and wet trim usually come out.
5 Clean and disinfect
The slab, studs, block and remaining surfaces are cleaned and treated with antimicrobial.
6 Dry the structure
Dehumidifiers and air movers run until framing and slab read dry.
7 Rebuild
Insulation, drywall, trim, cabinets and flooring go back once everything reads dry.
Services
2-Foot vs 4-Foot Flood Cuts in Fort Myers Homes
Water height on the wall Typical cut
A few inches to about 1 foot About 2 feet, to get above the wicking line
1 to 3 feet About 4 feet, which also matches a half sheet of drywall
Higher Above the highest wet reading, often full-height walls
Water wicks up drywall well above the visible line, so the cut is set by moisture readings, not just the stain. On block walls, the drywall and furring strips behind it are checked too.

Item After floodwater contact

Mattresses, upholstered furniture, pillows Usually discard

Solid wood and metal furniture Clean, disinfect and dry; may be saved

Photograph everything before it goes to the curb and keep a list for your flood claim. For curbside pickup, keep debris in separate piles, usually vegetation, construction debris like drywall and carpet, appliances, electronics and household hazardous waste, and follow your city's or Lee County's instructions.

Where Flooding Hits Hardest in Lee County
Fort Myers Beach, Sanibel, Captiva and Pine Island: storm surge on the barrier islands. See Fort Myers Beach .
Iona, McGregor and homes along the Caloosahatchee River: surge and river flooding.
Cape Coral canal-front homes: surge pushed through the canal system. See Cape Coral .
Bonita Springs near the Imperial River: river flooding after heavy rain. See Bonita Springs .
Lehigh Acres and low-lying neighborhoods: street flooding during heavy summer storms. See Lehigh Acres .
Manufactured homes take water in the belly and floor system; see mobile home water damage . Businesses: see commercial water damage .
Services
Septic Systems and Wells After a Lee County Flood
Parts of Lehigh Acres, North Fort Myers and other areas run on septic tanks and private wells, and both need care after a flood.
Septic. Don't have the tank pumped while the ground is still saturated; an emptied tank can shift or float. Use as little water as you can until the drain field dries out.
Wells. Don't drink well water that floodwater reached until the well is disinfected and the water is tested. The Florida Department of Health in Lee County can advise on testing.
Drains backing up. If toilets and tubs gurgle or back up after the water goes down, the septic system or sewer line may be overloaded.
Services
Storm Water That Came In From Above in Fort Myers Homes
Hurricanes and summer storms also push water in through roofs, soffits, windows and sliding doors. That water often starts as clean rainwater, but it soaks attic insulation, ceilings and walls and needs the same fast drying. See ceiling leak water damage . After a storm, many homes have both rising water at floor level and roof leaks overhead, often handled under different policies.
Services
Flood Insurance Basics for Fort Myers Homeowners
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
Homeowners doesn't cover flood. Rising surface water, storm surge and overflowing canals are covered by a flood policy from the NFIP or a private insurer.
Waiting period. New NFIP policies usually have a 30-day waiting period, so coverage bought when a storm is forecast is usually too late.
Wind vs water. Rain driven in through a storm-damaged roof or window is usually a homeowners claim; rising water is a flood claim.
Proof of loss. NFIP policies generally ask for a signed proof of loss within 60 days of the flood, and FEMA sometimes extends that after large storms. Ask your adjuster for the date in writing.
Below elevated homes. Areas below the lowest elevated floor often have limited flood coverage for finishes and contents.
Citizens policyholders. Citizens home policies that include wind coverage now require a separate flood policy, reaching all of them on January 1, 2027.
Document before you muck out. Photos, video, the water line on the walls and a list of damaged items.
Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Services
Rebuilding After a Fort Myers Flood: Permits and the 50% Rule
The 50% rule. In FEMA flood zones that start with A or V, Lee County building departments compare the repair total with the building's market value. At 50% or more, the building has to meet current flood rules, which can mean raising it. More on the 50% rule: water damage restoration in Fort Myers.
ICC coverage. NFIP policies include ICC coverage that can pay up to $30,000 toward elevating, flood-proofing, relocating or demolishing a home the community declares substantially damaged. Request it within 60 days of the substantial damage notice.
Permits. Ask your city or Lee County which repairs need a permit before the rebuild starts.
Keep the paper trail. Moisture readings, drying logs, photos and repair invoices support both the permit review and the claim.
Services
Renting Out or Selling a Fort Myers Home That Has Flooded
Florida now requires owners to tell the next tenant or buyer about past flooding.
Landlords. Since October 1, 2025, a landlord signing a residential lease of one year or longer must give the tenant a separate flood disclosure form at or before signing (Florida Statutes 83.512). It asks whether the owner knows of past flooding and about past flood claims or flood-damage assistance. A tenant who doesn't receive it and suffers substantial flood loss may be able to end the lease and get prepaid rent back.
Sellers. Sellers of residential property must give buyers a flood disclosure before the contract is signed (Florida Statutes 689.302). Since October 1, 2025, it covers flood-damage assistance received from any source, not only federal programs.
Keep the records. Moisture readings, drying logs, photos and repair invoices from this cleanup are the clearest way to show later what flooded, what was replaced and when the structure was dry.
This is general information, not legal advice. Ask a real estate attorney or your property manager what applies to your lease or sale.
Services
Getting a Fort Myers Home Ready Before the Next Storm
Photograph every room now, so you have a record of the house before any damage.
Move valuables, papers and electronics up high when a storm is forecast.
Know where your main water, power and gas shut-offs are.
Check flood coverage well before hurricane season (June 1 to November 30).
Clear gutters and drains and secure loose items outside.
Have a plan for a seasonal home, including who checks it after a storm. See water damage in vacant homes .
Services
Questions About Flood Cleanup in Fort Myers
Is floodwater dangerous?
Yes. Floodwater is Category 3 water that can carry sewage, bacteria, chemicals and debris. Wear boots, gloves and a mask, and keep children and pets out of flooded areas.
How soon should I start flood cleanup?
As soon as officials say it's safe to return and the power is safe. Mold can start within 24 to 48 hours, so muck-out and drying should start right away.
Do I have to cut out drywall after a flood?
Usually yes. Drywall and insulation soaked by floodwater are removed above the wet line, typically with a 2-foot or 4-foot flood cut, so the wall cavity can be cleaned and dried.
Can outlets and breakers be reused after storm surge?
Generally no. Electrical parts that sat in floodwater, especially saltwater, are usually replaced. Have an electrician check the system before the power goes back on.
Does homeowners insurance cover storm surge?
No. Storm surge and rising water are flood damage, covered by a separate flood policy. Wind and wind-driven rain damage is usually a homeowners claim.
Will flood insurance help me raise my house?
It can. If the community declares your home substantially damaged, NFIP ICC coverage can pay up to $30,000 toward elevating or otherwise bringing it up to current flood rules. Ask your adjuster about it early.
Should I wait for the adjuster before cleaning up?
No. Photograph and video everything, keep small samples of carpet and drywall if you can, then start mucking out. Waiting lets mold grow, and policies expect you to prevent further damage.
Can I clean up flood damage myself?
You can remove wet belongings and carpet with proper protection. Removing drywall, disinfecting and drying the structure to measured readings is safer and more reliable with professional equipment.
How long does it take to dry a house after a flood?
After removal and disinfection, drying the slab and framing usually takes several days, often longer than a clean-water leak.
Can I stay in my house after a flood?
Only if the power, water and structure are safe. Many families stay elsewhere while wet materials are removed and the home is dried.
Who does flood cleanup on Fort Myers Beach, Sanibel or Pine Island?
Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for flood and storm surge cleanup on Fort Myers Beach, Sanibel, Pine Island and across Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Estero and Bonita Springs. See all service areas .

Key facts about water damage in Cape Coral
Cape Coral is mostly single-family slab homes, so water spreads sideways under flooring.
Many 1970s and 1980s homes, especially in the southeast and southwest Cape, still have original cast iron drain lines.
The city's canal system, widely cited at more than 400 miles, carries storm surge toward homes during hurricanes.
The City's Utilities Extension Project has brought city water, sewer and irrigation to nearly all of the Cape south of Pine Island Road and is working north, which can expose old drain problems.
Areas
Water Damage in Your Cape Coral Home Right Now? Do This First
Shut off the water at the fixture or the main shut-off near the meter.
In north Cape homes still on a private well, turn off the well pump at its breaker too.
Cut power at the breaker to wet rooms, and don't run the washer or showers if a drain is backing up.
If it's a toilet or drain backup, stop using all water in the house.
Photograph everything, including cracked tile or damp grout that could point to a slab or cast iron leak.
Start drying the same day. In Southwest Florida humidity, mold can start within 24 to 48 hours.
Every step in one list: the first-hour water damage checklist .
Areas
What Makes Water Damage Different in Cape Coral Homes
Slab homes, everywhere. When water escapes, it runs under tile, vinyl plank, baseboards and cabinets instead of draining away.
Two building eras. A large share of the Cape was built from the 1970s to the 1990s, and much of the rest after 2000. The older half is where cast iron drains, aging copper lines and original water heaters show up.
Canals and storm surge. During hurricanes, surge pushes water through the canal system toward homes, garages and lanais.
Seasonal and empty homes. Many Cape homes sit empty part of the year, so leaks can run for weeks.
Septic-to-sewer conversions. New sewer connections in north Cape neighborhoods can expose drain-line problems that went unnoticed for years.
Areas
Cape Coral's Water System and What It Means for Leaks
Cape Coral runs its water differently from most of Lee County, and that changes how leaks show up.
Drinking water. In served areas, city drinking water comes from brackish groundwater treated by reverse osmosis. A leak on this line moves your water meter.
Irrigation water. Served areas also have irrigation-only water lines carrying reclaimed water and canal water for lawns and landscaping. It is not drinking water, and a leak on the irrigation side won't show on your drinking-water meter.
Wells and septic. Parts of the north Cape still run on private wells and septic tanks until the Utilities Extension Project reaches them.
New connections. When the city lines arrive, your own plumber connects the house to them. That work can stress or expose old drain lines under the slab.

How Water Damage Restoration Works in a Cape Coral Home
1 Find the source
A plumber, leak detection company, roofer or HVAC technician fixes the cause. In older Cape homes that often starts with a camera inspection of the drain.
2 Extract standing water
See emergency water removal .

Meters and a thermal camera trace water across the slab and up the walls.

Soaked carpet pad, swollen baseboards, cabinet bases and vinyl plank that traps water on the slab.

Drywall, flooring, baseboards and cabinets go back once everything reads dry.

Areas
Older Cape Coral Homes: Cast Iron and Copper
If your home was built before about 1980, two pipe problems deserve attention:
Cast iron drains that corrode and crack under the slab, leaking wastewater under floors. Signs include slow drains, sewer smells and damp, cracked tile.
Older copper supply lines that develop pinholes, causing slab leaks and wet walls.
A plumber's camera inspection or leak detection tells you what you're dealing with; restoration then removes contaminated materials and dries the slab and walls.
Areas
Canal-Front Cape Coral Homes and Flooding
Surge and heavy rain can push canal water into garages, lanais and living areas. Floodwater is Category 3, so wet drywall, insulation, carpet and particle board usually come out before drying.
Insurance. Rising water is covered by a flood policy, not standard homeowners insurance. Citizens home policies with wind coverage now require a separate flood policy.
The 50% rule. In FEMA flood zones that start with A or V, the City of Cape Coral building department, not Lee County, compares the repair total with the building's market value. At 50% or more, the home has to meet current flood rules.
Paper trail. Photos, moisture readings and drying logs support both the permit review and the flood claim.

November to January Seasonal owners returning to leaks, musty houses and mold

Questions About Water Damage in Cape Coral
Is there 24-hour water damage help in Cape Coral?
Yes. Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for water damage anywhere in Cape Coral, including nights and weekends.
Do older Cape Coral homes have cast iron pipes?
Many homes built in the 1970s and 1980s still have original cast iron sewer lines. A plumber's camera inspection confirms it.
Why does water spread so far in Cape Coral homes?
Nearly all Cape homes sit on concrete slabs. Water runs under tile and vinyl plank and wicks up drywall, so the wet area is usually bigger than it looks.
My canal-front home flooded. Will homeowners insurance pay?
Rising water and storm surge are flood damage, covered by a separate flood policy. Wind-driven rain through a damaged roof is usually a homeowners claim.
We just connected to city sewer and now have a leak. Is it related?
It can be. Connection work can stress or expose old drain lines. Have a plumber inspect it and photograph the damage before cleanup.
My north Cape home is on a well. How do I shut the water off?
Turn off the well pump at its breaker and close the main valve near the pressure tank. That stops the pump from pushing more water into a broken line.
Is irrigation water safe if it gets inside my home?
No. Cape Coral's irrigation water is reclaimed or canal water, not drinking water, so treat water from a broken irrigation line that reaches the house as contaminated and clean and dry it properly.
Why does my Cape Coral home smell like sewer?
Check for slow drains or damp floors near bathrooms and the kitchen. In an older home, a sewer smell can mean a cracked cast iron drain. Call a plumber for a camera inspection.
How long does drying take in a Cape Coral slab home?
Most clean-water leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days. Wet concrete under tile or vinyl plank, cast iron leaks and floodwater usually take longer.
Do you also cover North Fort Myers and Pine Island?
Yes. Help is available across Lee County, including North Fort Myers , Pine Island, Fort Myers, Lehigh Acres , Estero and Bonita Springs . See all service areas .

Water Damage in Your Lehigh Acres Home Right Now? Do This First
Shut off the water. On a well, turn off the well pump at its breaker as well as the main valve.

Turn off the AC at the thermostat if it's leaking.

What Makes Water Damage Different in Lehigh Acres Homes
Block homes on slabs. Water runs under flooring and wicks up the drywall inside block walls, into the gap at the furring strips.
Private wells. A pump, a pressure tank and supply lines that can fail, often in the garage or a utility closet.
Hard well water. Well water in the area tends to be hard, so water heaters, valves and fittings scale up and can fail sooner.
Septic tanks. Heavy rain can saturate the drain field and push water back into the house.
Drainage during summer storms. Some streets and low lots flood deeply in heavy rain.
AC that rarely rests. Inland Lehigh Acres runs hot, and clogged condensate lines are a top cause of indoor water damage.
Areas
Wells, Septic and City Utilities in Lehigh Acres
Lehigh Acres is a mix: some homes are on central water and sewer from FGUA, and many still run on a private well and a septic tank. Each part of a well and septic setup leaks in its own way.
Equipment How it usually leaks First step
Pressure tank Rusts through at the bottom and leaks onto the garage or closet floor Turn off the pump breaker and close the tank valve
Well pump and lines A broken line keeps getting fed until the pump is off Turn off the pump breaker
Water softener Fittings, the bypass valve or an overflowing brine tank Put it in bypass and unplug it
Under-sink filter or reverse osmosis unit Cracked housings and push-fit tubing Close its feed valve
Septic system Backups through tubs and toilets when the tank or drain field is full or flooded Stop using water and call a septic company
Have a well service company or septic company fix the equipment, then have the garage, closet and nearby walls checked for moisture.

Storm and Street Flooding in Lehigh Acres
Heavy rain can leave some streets under deep water. When water from outside reaches a garage or living area, it's floodwater, Category 3, even if it looks clear.

Lehigh Acres Rental Homes: Landlords and Tenants
Tenants. Stop the water if you safely can, photograph everything and tell your landlord or property manager right away. Renters insurance usually covers your belongings, not the building.
Landlords and property managers. Florida law generally requires landlords to keep plumbing in reasonable working condition (Florida Statutes 83.51), and the building is usually your insurance claim. Fast drying protects the property and keeps the home livable.
Both. Agree on who calls for drying, and keep copies of photos and messages.

How Water Damage Restoration Works in a Lehigh Acres Home
1 Stop the source
A plumber, HVAC technician, well service company or septic company fixes the cause.
2 Extract standing water
See emergency water removal.
3 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera find water under flooring and inside block walls.
4 Remove what can't be dried
Soaked carpet pad, swollen baseboards and cabinet bases.
5 Dry the structure
Dehumidifiers and air movers dry the wet drywall and carpet in the concrete block home, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
6 Repair
Drywall, flooring and cabinets go back once everything reads dry.
Most clean-water leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days; floodwater and sewage take longer.

Questions About Water Damage in Lehigh Acres
Is there 24-hour water damage help in Lehigh Acres?
Yes. Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for water damage anywhere in Lehigh Acres.
My home is on a well. How do I shut the water off?
Turn off the well pump at its breaker and close the main valve near the pressure tank. That stops the pump from pushing more water into a broken line.
My well pressure tank is leaking into the garage. What do I do?
Turn off the pump at its breaker, close the valve near the tank and photograph the leak. Have a well service company repair the tank, and have the garage walls and floor checked for moisture.
My septic is backing up after heavy rain. What now?
Stop using water, keep people and pets away from the overflow and photograph it. Don't have the tank pumped while the ground is still flooded. Call a septic company, and treat anything the backup touched as sewage.
Street flooding got into my garage. Is that covered?
Water rising from outside is flood damage, covered by a flood policy rather than standard homeowners insurance. Photograph everything before cleanup.
Who do I call about flooded canals or street drainage?
Canal and stormwater drainage in Lehigh Acres is handled by the Lehigh Acres Municipal Services Improvement District (LAMSID).
My AC closet floor is wet. What should I do?
Turn the AC off at the thermostat, soak up standing water and check whether the drain pan is full. Then have the drain line cleared and the closet walls and floor checked for hidden moisture.
I rent my Lehigh Acres home. Who pays for water damage?
The landlord usually handles the building and its repairs, and renters insurance usually covers your belongings. Tell your landlord right away and photograph everything.
How long does drying take in a Lehigh Acres home?
Most clean-water leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days. Floodwater, sewage and wet concrete under flooring take longer.

Areas
Fort Myers
Fort Myers runs from the historic River District and older homes along McGregor Boulevard to Iona, Gateway, Whiskey Creek, San Carlos Park and newer communities off Daniels Parkway. Older homes may have cast iron drains and aging supply lines; condos and townhomes see leaks from units above; and neighborhoods along the Caloosahatchee River face surge and river flooding during storms. Most common: AC leak water damage , condo water damage and cast iron pipe water damage . Full guide: water damage restoration in Fort Myers .
Cape Coral
Mostly single-family slab homes, many built between 1970 and 1999, laced with canals. City water, sewer and a separate irrigation system serve most of the Cape, while parts of the north still run on wells and septic. Slab leaks, original cast iron drains in older Cape neighborhoods, canal surge and leaks in seasonal homes are the most common calls. Full guide: water damage restoration in Cape Coral .
Lehigh Acres
A large, younger community of concrete block homes, many built in the 2000s and later. Many homes use private wells and septic tanks, heavy summer rain can flood streets and low lots, and air conditioners run hard most of the year. Full guide: water damage help in Lehigh Acres .
North Fort Myers
North of the Caloosahatchee, North Fort Myers mixes riverfront homes, golf communities and many manufactured-home communities. Soft floors from water heater and supply line leaks, water trapped in the belly wrap, roof leaks and river flooding are the most common problems. Full guide: water damage restoration in North Fort Myers . See also mobile home water damage .
Fort Myers Beach
Fort Myers Beach on Estero Island sits right on the Gulf, and many homes and businesses there have been rebuilt, often elevated. Storm surge, condo and vacation rental leaks and sewage problems after storms are the main concerns. Full guide: water damage help on Fort Myers Beach .
Areas
Sanibel and Captiva
Many seasonal owners, condos and elevated homes. Hurricane surge is the biggest risk, followed by leaks that go unnoticed while owners are away. See water damage in vacant homes and flood and storm cleanup .
Areas
Pine Island and Matlacha
Pine Island, Bokeelia, St. James City and Matlacha are low-lying and surrounded by water, so surge is a real threat. Many manufactured homes and seasonal residents mean floor and belly-wrap damage and leaks found after time away.
Estero
Gated communities, condos, coach homes and seasonal residents. The most common water damage is a leak from the unit above, an AC closet overflow, or a home found wet and musty when the owner returns. Full guide: water damage restoration in Estero .
Bonita Springs
Condos along the coast and neighborhoods near the Imperial River. River and rain flooding, condo leaks and seasonal-home damage are the main concerns. Full guide: water damage restoration in Bonita Springs .

These communities carry Fort Myers addresses but sit in unincorporated Lee County. San Carlos Park has single-family homes from several decades; Gateway is a planned community with mostly newer homes; Iona, near the Gulf and the Caloosahatchee, has canal-front and older homes that face storm surge.

Emergency Water Heater Leak Cleanup in Fort Myers
Water pooling around the water heater, a puddle spreading across the garage, or a soaked, warm closet carpet? Close the cold-water valve and cut the power or gas first. A failing tank can release its full 40 or 50 gallons and keep refilling until the supply is shut off. Water heater leak cleanup means extracting the water and drying the walls and floors before it spreads.

Emergency Water Heater Leak Cleanup in Fort Myers
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
If your water heater is leaking, close the cold-water valve on top of the tank or the main, switch off the breaker for an electric heater or set gas to Off, and stay clear of hot water. After the plumber's repair, the slab, flooring and nearby walls still need moisture readings and drying.
Water heater leak in a Fort Myers home
What to know
First moves Cold-water valve closed, breaker or gas off, stay clear of hot water
Typical tank life Roughly 8 to 12 years; a tank leaking from the bottom is replaced, not repaired
Where heaters sit here Garages, interior closets, condo utility closets, sometimes the attic
Water category Category 1 from the supply; can become Category 2 on a dirty floor or over days
Who fixes what A plumber replaces or repairs the heater; drying covers the slab, walls and flooring
