Help 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7
Key facts about water heater leaks in Fort Myers
Most tank water heaters last roughly 8 to 12 years; once the tank rusts through at the bottom, it can't be repaired.
In Lee County homes, heaters usually sit in the garage, an interior closet, a condo utility closet or occasionally the attic.
Water from a heater closet spreads under baseboards, carpet and vinyl plank into nearby rooms.
The heater itself usually isn't covered by insurance; sudden resulting damage often is.
Services
Water Heater Leaking in Your Fort Myers Home? Do This First
Close the cold-water valve on the pipe going into the top of the heater. If it won't turn or the leak is heavy, shut off the main water to the house. On a well, turn off the pump too.
Cut the power or gas. For an electric heater, switch off its double breaker. For gas, turn the control to Off or Pilot. If you smell gas, leave and call the gas company from outside.
Stay away from hot water. Water near the tank can be scalding.
Keep clear of wet outlets and extension cords on the garage floor.
Move boxes, rugs and stored items out of the water.
Photograph the tank, its age label, the floor and the walls before cleanup.
Start drying the same day.
Every step in one list: the first-hour water damage checklist .
Services
Where Is Your Fort Myers Water Heater Leaking From?
Where the water is coming from What it usually means
Bottom of the tank Tank corrosion; usually means replacement
Top of the tank Loose or corroded supply connections or a failing fitting
T&P relief valve or its discharge pipe Pressure or temperature too high, or a worn valve
Drain valve near the bottom Worn or loose valve; sometimes a simple fix
Condensate line on a heat pump water heater A clogged or disconnected drain line, much like an AC
Water around the base with a dry tank Condensation, a nearby AC drain or another leak
A plumber confirms the cause. If the tank itself is leaking, plan on replacement rather than a patch.
Services
Tank, Tankless or Heat Pump: How Each Fort Myers Water Heater Leaks
Type How it usually leaks How much water
Standard tank Rusted bottom, fittings, relief valve, drain valve Up to the full tank, and more until the supply is shut off
Tankless Fittings, the heat exchanger or the relief valve Usually a steady drip or spray at the unit
Heat pump (hybrid) tank All of the tank leaks, plus its condensate drain line Tank leaks can be large; condensate leaks are slow but steady
Services
Where Water Heaters Sit in Lee County Homes, and Where the Water Goes
Garage: the most common spot in Lee County single-family homes. Water spreads across the slab, under the door into the house and into the bottom of garage drywall and stored boxes.
Interior closet: common in condos, townhomes and some houses. Water soaks the flooring outside the closet, the hallway and the walls on both sides.
Attic: less common but the worst case. A leaking attic heater soaks insulation and comes through the ceiling. See ceiling leak water damage .
Condo utility closet: a failed heater can leak into the unit below. See condo water damage .
Manufactured homes: the heater closet floor often goes soft. See mobile home water damage .
Services
What Florida's Plumbing Code Expects Around a Fort Myers Water Heater
Florida's plumbing code, based on the International Plumbing Code, sets a few rules that matter when a heater leaks:
A drain pan under the heater where a leak would damage the building, piped to an approved place to drain.
A relief valve discharge pipe that runs full size to a safe spot where you can see it, never capped or plugged.
Thermal expansion control, usually an expansion tank, when a check valve or backflow preventer makes the system closed.
A permit is often needed to replace a water heater, so ask your plumber to pull it.
A heater in a closet or attic with no pan is one of the most common reasons a small leak turns into a big repair.
Services
How Water Heater Leak Cleanup Works in a Fort Myers Home
1 Shut down and replace
The plumber replaces the heater or repairs the fitting.
2 Extract the water
Standing water is extracted from the slab, carpet and closet floor.
3 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera check under flooring and up the walls, including rooms next to the closet or garage.
4 Remove what can't be dried
Soaked carpet pad, swollen baseboards, particle board shelving and wet lower drywall if needed.
5 Dry the structure
Dehumidifiers and air movers dry the garage and the wet lower drywall, with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
6 Repair
Drywall, baseboards and flooring go back once everything reads dry.
Most clean-water heater leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days if drying starts quickly.
Services
Is Water Heater Water in a Fort Myers Home Clean?
Water straight from the supply line is Category 1, clean water. Water that sits on a garage floor, soaks through dirty carpet or runs for days can become Category 2, which means more cleaning and more removal.
Services
Slow Leak or Sudden Burst in a Fort Myers Water Heater
Feature Slow leak Sudden burst
What you notice Rust stains, damp baseboards, a musty smell, a small puddle that keeps coming back A flooded garage or closet, water running across the floor
Hidden damage Often more than it looks, under flooring and inside walls Spread across a large area quickly
Mold risk Higher, because water has been there longer Lower if drying starts the same day
Insurance Long-running leaks are often excluded Sudden damage is often covered
Services
Warning Signs Before a Fort Myers Water Heater Fails
Rust-colored hot water or rust at the tank's base
Rumbling or popping sounds as sediment builds up
Moisture or small puddles around the base
A tank older than about 10 years; the serial number on the label usually shows the year it was made
Corroded fittings on the pipes at the top
A relief valve that drips or a discharge pipe that's wet
On private wells in Lehigh Acres and parts of the north Cape, hard water builds sediment faster, so tanks there often need flushing more often. If you see these signs, have a plumber look at the heater before it fails, and make sure a drain pan is installed.
Services
How to Lower the Risk of a Water Heater Flood in Your Fort Myers Home
Install a drain pan under the heater, piped to a drain where possible.
Add a leak alarm or an automatic shut-off valve.
Flush the tank as the manufacturer recommends.
Know where the cold-water shut-off is and make sure it turns.
Keep the area around a heat pump water heater's condensate line clear, and check that it drains.
Plan replacement before the tank reaches the end of its life.
Seasonal homes: turn off the heater and the main water when you leave. See water damage in vacant homes .

Does Insurance Cover Water Heater Leak Damage in Fort Myers?
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
Resulting damage to floors, walls and belongings is often covered when the failure was sudden.
The water heater itself usually isn't covered, because tanks wear out.
Long-running leaks may be excluded as continuous seepage.
Some Florida policies cap non-weather water losses, often at $10,000 per loss, through a limited water damage endorsement.
Condos: damage reaching other units can involve the association and other owners' policies.
Keep photos, the heater's age label and the plumber's invoice. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Services
Questions About Water Heater Leaks in Fort Myers
What do I do first when my water heater is leaking?
Close the cold-water valve at the top of the heater, then cut its power at the breaker or set a gas heater to Off. If the leak is heavy or the valve won't turn, shut off the main water.
Is a leaking water heater an emergency?
Yes, if water is spreading or the tank is leaking from the bottom. A leaking tank can fail completely without warning.
Can a leaking water heater be repaired?
A leaking fitting, drain valve or relief valve can often be repaired. A tank leaking from the bottom because of corrosion usually needs replacement.
Can I still use hot water if the heater is leaking?
No. Shut off the supply and the power or gas until a plumber has checked it.
Does my water heater need a drain pan in Florida?
Florida's plumbing code calls for a pan where a leak would damage the building, such as in a closet, an attic or a condo. Ask your plumber to add one if yours doesn't have it.
Why is my heat pump water heater leaking?
Heat pump water heaters make condensate like an AC. A clogged or loose condensate line is a common cause; leaks from the tank or fittings are handled like any other tank.
My water heater leaked into the garage. Do I need to worry about the walls?
Yes. Water on a garage slab often wicks into the bottom of the drywall and can run under the door into the house. Have the walls and nearby rooms checked with a moisture meter.
How long does it take to dry after a water heater leak?
Most clean-water leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days. Leaks that soaked under vinyl plank, reached several rooms or ran for days take longer.
How long do water heaters last in Florida?
Most tank heaters last roughly 8 to 12 years. Have one that's 10 years or older checked for rust and leaks at the base.

When an appliance leaks, turn it off, close its water valve or the main, and photograph everything before cleanup. Appliance Leaking in Your Fort Myers Home? Do This First
Turn the appliance off. Unplug it only if you can reach the plug without standing in water; otherwise switch off its breaker.
Close its water valve. Washers have hot and cold valves on the wall box. Dishwashers usually shut off under the kitchen sink. Ice maker lines often have a small valve under the sink or behind the fridge.
Can't find the valve? Shut off the main water. On a well, switch off the pump too.
Water coming out of the pipe behind the washer? That's the laundry drain backing up. Stop the washer and don't run it again until the drain is cleared. If toilets or tubs are gurgling or backing up too, the main drain may be blocked. See sewage backup cleanup .
Soak up standing water and move rugs, boxes and belongings out of it.
Photograph the appliance, the failed hose or line, its model label and the floor.
In a condo, tell the unit below and building management right away.
Every step in one list: the first-hour water damage checklist .

Where Laundry Rooms Sit in Lee County Homes, and Where the Water Goes
Garage: common in Fort Myers, Cape Coral and Lehigh Acres single-family homes. Water spreads across the slab, wicks into the bottom of the garage drywall and runs under the door into the house.
Interior laundry room: water slips under baseboards into the hallway and nearby bedrooms, often under vinyl plank.
Condo laundry closet: with stacked units, an overflow can come through the ceiling below. See condo water damage .
Second-floor laundry: in two-story homes and townhomes, an overflow soaks the subfloor and the ceiling underneath. See ceiling leak water damage .
Manufactured homes: a washer leak soaks the particle board decking and the floor system below. See mobile home water damage .

Why Appliance Leaks Do More Damage Than They Look in Fort Myers
Water goes under things. It runs under toe kicks, beneath cabinet floors and under vinyl plank or laminate, where it's trapped against the slab.
Leaks are often slow. An ice maker line or dishwasher connection can drip for weeks before a soft cabinet floor, lifting plank or musty smell gives it away.
Particle board swells. Most cabinet bases are particle board, and once it swells it doesn't go back.
Florida humidity slows drying. Water trapped under cabinets and flooring dries slowly here on its own, which gives mold time to grow.

Is Appliance Water in a Fort Myers Home Clean?
Source Water category
Washer, dishwasher or ice maker supply line Category 1 if caught right away
Washer or dishwasher drain water Category 2 (gray water)
Clean water that sat on the floor for days Can degrade from Category 1 to Category 2
Backup from a sink or drain line Category 2, or Category 3 if it involves sewage
Gray water carries detergent, food and soil, so carpet pad and porous materials it soaks are usually removed, and surfaces are cleaned and treated before drying.

How Appliance Leak Cleanup Works in a Fort Myers Home
1 Stop the source
An appliance technician or plumber repairs or replaces the hose, line or appliance.
2 Extract standing water
Standing water comes off the floor, carpet and garage slab. See emergency water removal .
3 Pull the appliance and check behind it
The wall, floor and cabinets around and behind it are checked, including the toe kicks next to a dishwasher.
4 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera check under flooring, inside cabinet bases and up the walls.
5 Remove what can't be dried
Soaked carpet pad, swollen toe kicks, particle board cabinet floors and wet vinyl plank.
6 Clean and treat
Gray-water areas are cleaned and treated with antimicrobial.
7 Dry and repair
Dehumidifiers and air movers run with readings logged daily, then repairs follow. See structural drying .

Appliance Leaks in Fort Myers Condos
Under Florida Statute 718.111(11), the association's policy generally leaves appliances, water heaters, water filters, built-in cabinets, countertops and floor, wall and ceiling coverings inside a unit to the owner's HO-6 policy. If a washer hose or ice maker line in one unit damages another, who pays often depends on the cause and whether the appliance was kept up, and your declaration can change parts of the default. Report it to building management and your insurer the same day.

How to Prevent the Next Appliance Leak in Your Fort Myers Home
Replace rubber washer hoses with braided stainless hoses, and replace hoses about every five years.
Leave a few inches behind the washer so the hoses don't kink.
Turn off the washer valves when you leave town.
Use a washer drain pan in condos, second-floor laundry rooms and over finished floors.
Check the ice maker line whenever the fridge is moved; braided lines hold up better than thin plastic tubing.
Put leak alarms or an automatic shut-off valve under sinks, behind the fridge and next to the washer.
Don't run the washer or dishwasher while nobody is home.
Seasonal homes: close the washer valves and the main before you leave. See water damage in vacant homes .

This is general information, not advice about your policy.

The appliance or the failed hose itself usually isn't.

Questions About Appliance Leaks in Fort Myers
My washing machine overflowed. What should I do first?
Turn the washer off, close the hot and cold valves behind it and soak up the water. Photograph everything, then check the walls and floors in nearby rooms, the garage or the unit below.
Why is water coming out of the pipe behind my washer?
That pipe is the laundry drain, called a standpipe. When it overflows during the drain cycle, the line is usually clogged with lint or buildup. Stop the washer, and if other drains in the house are slow or backing up too, call a plumber before using more water.
Can a dishwasher leak damage the floor under the cabinets?
Yes. Dishwasher water runs under the cabinets and toe kicks and soaks particle board cabinet floors and the flooring beneath. Pull the toe kick and check with a moisture meter.
How do I know if my refrigerator is leaking under the floor?
Look for a puddle that keeps returning, lifting or soft vinyl plank, stained grout or a musty smell near the fridge. A cracked ice maker line can leak slowly for weeks.
Why is there water under my fridge when the ice maker line is fine?
A clogged defrost drain is a common cause: melt water from the freezer overflows the drain pan underneath. A cracked water filter housing or heavy condensation can also leave water there. Pull the fridge out and check behind and under it.
Can a water softener leak cause water damage?
Yes. In well homes in Lehigh Acres, north Cape Coral and North Fort Myers, softeners often sit in the garage or a utility room, and a brine tank overflow or loose fitting can soak the floor and the bottom of nearby drywall. Close its bypass valve and have it checked.
Is washing machine water dangerous?
Drain water from a washer is gray water, Category 2. It isn't sewage, but it carries detergent, soil and bacteria, so wet carpet pad and porous materials are usually removed and the area is cleaned before drying.
Can a refrigerator leak cause mold?
Yes. A slow ice maker or defrost drain leak can keep the floor and cabinets damp for weeks, which is enough for mold in Florida humidity. Pull the fridge out and check behind and under it.
Should I keep using the washer after it leaked?
No. Leave it off with the valves closed until the hose, drain or machine has been checked.
How long does it take to dry after an appliance leak?
Most appliance leaks dry in about 3 to 5 days. Leaks that soaked cabinets or ran under vinyl plank take longer.

Key facts about water damaged floors in Fort Myers
Most Lee County homes are on concrete slabs, so water spreads sideways under flooring instead of draining away.
Vinyl plank is waterproof on top but not at the seams; water gets under it and stays.
Laminate's fiberboard core swells at the edges and rarely recovers.

Can My Floor Be Saved After a Fort Myers Leak?
Flooring When it can often be saved When it usually comes up
Porcelain or ceramic tile Firmly bonded, clean water, dried quickly Loose, hollow or cracked tiles; sewage or floodwater soaked the grout
Terrazzo Usually; it's cement-based and dries with the slab Cracked or loose sections, or sewage soaked through
Luxury vinyl plank (LVP) Small surface spill caught right away; click planks lifted and reinstalled Water trapped under glued-down planks, or planks with damaged edges
Laminate Rarely, unless wiped up immediately Core swells at the edges and doesn't recover
Engineered wood Mild cupping from a short clean-water leak Delamination, heavy cupping or long exposure
Solid hardwood Mild cupping from clean water dried quickly Buckling, crowning after drying, or contaminated water
Carpet Clean water caught within a day or two Gray water, sewage or floodwater; left wet for days
Carpet pad Rarely Usually replaced, because it acts like a sponge
Services
Why Fort Myers Slab Floors Trap Water
Concrete is porous. When water gets under flooring, the slab soaks it up and releases it slowly. Vinyl plank, laminate and many underlayments act like a lid, so the slab can't breathe and stays wet for weeks. That's why lifting the flooring is often the fastest way to dry the house, even when the planks look fine. Under-slab leaks are a different problem, because the water comes from below.
Services
Signs of Water Under Your Floor in a Fort Myers Home
Vinyl plank or laminate lifting, peaking or separating at the seams
Dark or damp grout lines that don't dry
Tile that sounds hollow when tapped, or cracks that appear suddenly
Wood boards cupping, with the edges higher than the center
Swollen or stained baseboards
A musty smell near the floor
A floor that feels cool or damp in one area, or warm in one spot if a hot water line is leaking
Services
How Water-Damaged Floors Are Dried in Fort Myers Homes
1 Find and stop the source
A plumber, appliance technician or HVAC technician fixes the cause.
2 Extract surface water
See emergency water removal .
3 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera map moisture across the floor, the slab and the bottom of the walls.
4 Remove what traps water
Vinyl plank, laminate, carpet pad and swollen baseboards are lifted or removed. Click-together planks in good shape are numbered and set aside.
5 Dry the slab and walls
Dehumidifiers, air movers and sometimes floor-drying equipment run with readings logged daily. See structural drying .
6 Confirm the slab is dry
New flooring over a wet slab leads to mold, adhesive failure and warped planks, so the slab is tested before anything goes back down.
Tile and grout over a clean-water leak often dry in about 3 to 5 days. Bare concrete under removed flooring can take longer.
Services
Tile and Terrazzo Floors After a Fort Myers Leak
Tile itself doesn't absorb much water, but grout and the thinset or mortar underneath do. If tiles are firmly bonded and the water was clean, they can usually stay while the slab dries through the grout and edges. Hollow, loose or cracked tiles are replaced. Matching discontinued tile can be the hardest part of the repair, so keep spare tiles if you have them.
Many older Fort Myers homes have terrazzo, sometimes hidden under carpet or newer tile, or tile set in a thick mortar bed. Terrazzo is cement-based, so it usually handles clean water well and dries along with the slab. The bigger risk is the carpet, pad or floating floor laid over it.
Services
Is It Water or Heat? Tile Tenting in Fort Myers Homes
Tile that suddenly pops up into a tent shape, often in a sunny room or along a long run with no movement joints, is usually caused by expansion, not by water. A moisture meter on the grout tells the difference: dry grout points to tenting, wet grout points to a leak. Either way, keep off the raised tiles and have them checked.
Services
Vinyl Plank and Laminate After a Fort Myers Leak
Luxury vinyl plank is waterproof on top, but water still gets under it through the seams and edges, and the planks hold it against the slab. Usually the planks in the wet area are lifted, the slab is dried, and click-together planks are reinstalled if undamaged; glued-down or damaged planks are replaced. Laminate has a fiberboard core that swells and rarely survives.
Services
Wood Floors After a Fort Myers Leak
Wood absorbs water and cups. With quick drying, mild cupping can flatten out. Sanding too soon can cause crowning later, so wood floors should be dried and monitored before any refinishing decision. Wood is less common on Fort Myers slabs and reacts fastest to humidity.
Services
Carpet After a Fort Myers Leak
Carpet can often be saved from a clean-water leak if it's extracted and dried within a day or two. The pad usually isn't worth saving. Carpet soaked by gray water, sewage or floodwater is removed.
Services
Floors in Fort Myers and Lee County Condos
Under Florida Statute 718.111(11), floor coverings inside a unit are generally the owner's to insure with an HO-6 policy, not the association's. Many condo associations also have rules on sound-reducing underlayment under tile, vinyl plank or wood on upper floors, so check them before new flooring goes in. See condo water damage .
Services
Older Floors and Asbestos in Lee County Homes
Some older vinyl tile, sheet vinyl and the black adhesive under them contain asbestos. In an older home, have the old flooring tested before anyone breaks it, scrapes it or sands the adhesive. Left intact, it's far safer than torn up untested.
Services
Insurance and Continuous Flooring in Fort Myers
This is general information, not advice about your policy. When water damages part of a continuous floor, whether the insurer replaces only the wet area or more depends on your policy. Florida Statute 626.9744 says that when replaced items don't match in quality, color or size, an insurer settling on a repair or replacement basis must make reasonable repairs or replacement in adjoining areas. What counts as reasonable is often where floor claims get argued, so photograph the whole floor before anything is removed, keep a spare plank or tile and ask your adjuster how matching is handled.
Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida . General pricing information: water damage pricing guide .
Services
LVP vs Tile vs Wood in Fort Myers Slab Homes
Most newer Fort Myers and Cape Coral homes have porcelain tile or luxury vinyl plank on the slab, and many older homes have tile or terrazzo throughout. Tile and terrazzo handle a quick clean-water leak best, because the slab can dry through the grout. Vinyl plank is the floor that most often has to be lifted. Wood floors are less common on slabs here and react fastest to humidity.
Services
Questions About Water-Damaged Floors in Fort Myers
Can vinyl plank flooring be saved after water damage?
Sometimes. Click-together planks in good condition can often be lifted, set aside while the slab dries and reinstalled. Glued-down planks or planks with damaged edges are usually replaced.
How do I know if water is under my tile?
Look for dark grout lines that stay damp, tiles that sound hollow when tapped or swollen baseboards. A moisture meter on the grout and slab confirms it.
Can terrazzo floors get water damaged?
Terrazzo itself usually survives a clean-water leak, because it's cement-based like the slab under it. Cracks, loose sections or sewage soaking through are what lead to repairs, and carpet or vinyl plank laid over terrazzo often has to come up.
Should I pull up my flooring myself?
Photograph everything first, and check with your insurer if you plan to file a claim. Removing flooring yourself can also disturb older materials, such as asbestos in some old vinyl tile or adhesive.
Can I put new flooring down right after the leak is fixed?
Not until the slab reads dry. New flooring over a wet slab can trap moisture, grow mold and fail.
Why is my vinyl plank floor lifting?
Water under the planks, high humidity or a wet slab can push planks up at the seams. Find the water source first, then check the slab with a moisture meter.
Will my floor smell if water is still underneath?
Often, yes. A musty smell near the floor, especially by the baseboards, usually means moisture is trapped under the flooring or in the bottom of the walls.
Will insurance replace my whole floor if only one room got wet?
It depends on your policy and on whether the new flooring can reasonably match. Florida's matching law calls for reasonable repairs or replacement in adjoining areas when items don't match, but how far that goes is decided claim by claim. Keep a spare plank or tile and photograph the whole floor.
Who dries water-damaged floors in Fort Myers?

Why Water Hides Under Fort Myers Cabinets

How Water-Damaged Cabinets Are Dried in Fort Myers Homes
1 Stop the source
A plumber or appliance technician fixes the leak.
2 Empty and open
Cabinets are emptied and the toe kicks removed.
3 Map the moisture
Meters and a thermal camera check the cabinet floors, the wall behind and the flooring underneath.
4 Push dry air in
Small holes are drilled or the toe kick space is opened so dry air can reach under and behind the cabinets.
5 Remove what can't be dried
Swollen particle board panels, and wet drywall behind the cabinets if needed.
6 Dry and repair
Dehumidifiers and air movers run with readings logged daily, then damaged panels, toe kicks and drywall are replaced. See structural drying .
Done early, this often saves the cabinets and countertop. When a leak sat for weeks or cabinets are badly swollen, replacement is often the better choice.
Services
Does the Floor Run Under Your Fort Myers Cabinets?
How the flooring meets the cabinets changes the size of the repair. Tile laid before the cabinets went in usually runs under them, so it can stay while the cabinets are dried, but replacing that tile can mean pulling cabinets. Vinyl plank is normally installed up to the cabinets, not under them, so it can usually be lifted without touching the cabinets, though water can still be trapped under the cabinet bases.
Services
When Do Countertops Have to Come Off in Fort Myers Kitchens?
Replacing a whole run of base cabinets usually means removing the countertop. Granite and quartz can sometimes be removed and reinstalled, but there is a risk of cracking, and laminate countertops usually can't be reused. That's why drying cabinets in place and replacing only the damaged panels is worth trying first.
Services
Signs of Hidden Water Damage in Fort Myers Cabinets
Swollen or bubbling cabinet floor under the sink
Peeling or lifting edges on cabinet doors or sides
A musty smell when you open the cabinet
Stains or dark spots inside the cabinet or on the toe kick
Vinyl plank or tile near the cabinets lifting or staying damp
Swollen baseboards next to the cabinets
Services
Bathroom Vanities After a Fort Myers Leak
Vanities have the same weak point as kitchen cabinets: a particle board floor under the sink plumbing. Toilet supply leaks and overflows also run under vanities and into the wall behind them. Toilet overflows can be Category 2 or 3, so a vanity soaked by one is often replaced rather than dried. See sewage backup cleanup .
Services
Cabinets in Fort Myers and Lee County Condos
Florida Statute 718.111(11) generally leaves built-in cabinets and countertops, along with appliances, water heaters and water filters, to the unit owner's HO-6 policy rather than the association's. Your declaration can change parts of that default. A kitchen or bathroom leak can also reach the cabinets in the unit below, so tell building management right away. See condo water damage .
Services
How to Prevent Cabinet Water Damage in Your Fort Myers Home
Check under sinks once a month for drips and damp spots.
Replace old braided supply lines and corroded shut-off valves.
Check under-sink filter and reverse osmosis fittings when you change the filters.
Use a leak alarm or a waterproof cabinet mat under the kitchen sink.
Don't store paper goods directly on the cabinet floor, where a slow leak can hide.
Close the valves under the sinks when you leave home for an extended time. See water damage in vacant homes .
Services
Does Insurance Cover Water-Damaged Cabinets in Fort Myers?
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
Damage from a sudden leak, such as a burst supply line, is often covered.
Damage from a slow drip that ran for weeks is often excluded as continuous seepage.
Matching cabinets and countertops depends on your policy. Florida Statute 626.9744 calls for reasonable repairs or replacement in adjoining areas when replaced items don't match.
Some Florida policies cap non-weather water losses, often at $10,000 per loss, through a limited water damage endorsement.
Photograph everything and keep the failed part. Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida . General pricing information: water damage pricing guide .
Services
Questions About Water-Damaged Cabinets in Fort Myers
Can swollen particle board cabinets be fixed?
Not the swollen part. Particle board doesn't shrink back once it swells. The damaged panel, often just the cabinet floor, can be replaced, or the whole cabinet if it's widely damaged.
How do I know if there's water behind my kitchen cabinets?
Look for swollen toe kicks, a musty smell, peeling edges or damp flooring near the cabinets. A moisture meter or thermal camera confirms it.
Do kitchen cabinets have to be removed after water damage?
Not always. Many cabinets can be dried in place by removing the toe kicks and pushing dry air under and behind them. They're removed when badly swollen, contaminated or hiding mold.
Can I save my granite or quartz countertop if the cabinets are replaced?
Sometimes. Stone countertops can often be removed and reinstalled, but there's a risk of cracking, especially around sink and cooktop cutouts.
Can an under-sink water filter leak into the cabinet?
Yes. Filter housings and reverse osmosis units sit right on the cabinet floor, and a cracked housing or loose tube can drip for weeks. Close the filter's supply valve, dry the cabinet and check the floor panel.
Will new cabinet doors match the rest of my kitchen?
Not always. Older or discontinued styles and finishes are hard to match, which is one more reason to dry and save what you can. If you have a claim, ask your adjuster how matching is handled.
Is a musty smell under the sink a sign of mold?
It can be. A musty smell usually means moisture has been there for a while. Fix the leak, then have the cabinet and the wall behind it checked.
How long does it take to dry cabinets?
Usually about 3 to 5 days for a clean-water leak caught early, longer if water sat under the cabinets for a while.
Can I paint over water stains inside the cabinet?
Not until the cabinet and the wall behind it read dry and the leak is fixed. Painting over damp wood or particle board can trap moisture and hide mold.
Who handles cabinet water damage in Fort Myers?
Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for cabinet and kitchen water damage in Fort Myers, Cape Coral , Lehigh Acres , North Fort Myers , Estero and Bonita Springs .

Water Damage at Your Fort Myers Business Right Now? Do This First
Make it safe. Keep staff and customers away from wet areas, wet outlets and sagging ceilings.
Stop the water at the fixture, the riser or the building's main valve. If you lease, call the landlord or property manager.
Cut power to wet areas at the breaker, or have an electrician do it if the panel is wet.
Sprinklers went off? Call your fire sprinkler contractor and alarm monitoring company; the system has to be restored and checked.
Move inventory, records, computers and equipment off the floor.
Photograph and video everything, including damaged stock and equipment.
Notify your landlord, association and insurer.
Start drying the same day.

Keeping Your Fort Myers Business Open During Drying
Section off wet areas so the rest of the space can stay open where it's safe.
Schedule noisy work like demolition after hours when possible.
Place equipment and cords away from exits, walkways and customers.
Tell staff which areas are closed and why, and keep the closed areas marked.
Services
Restaurants and Food Service in Lee County
Florida's Division of Hotels and Restaurants, part of the Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR), inspects restaurants, and its inspectors treat a sewage backup in a food service area as an imminent health hazard that can bring an emergency closure order. Reopening follows cleanup and a callback inspection.
Stop service in any area contaminated water reached.
Throw out food, ice and single-use items that the water touched.
Clean and sanitize food-contact surfaces, equipment and floors before reopening.
Find the cause: grease trap and floor drain backups, ice machine and dishwasher leaks, walk-in cooler drains and roof leaks over kitchens are the usual ones.
Services
Asbestos Rules Before Tear-Out in Fort Myers Commercial Buildings
Federal asbestos rules, enforced in Florida by the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP), apply to commercial, institutional and public buildings and to apartment buildings with more than four units. Before wet drywall, ceiling tiles or flooring are cut out, the affected areas need an asbestos inspection by an asbestos consultant, no matter how new the building is. If regulated asbestos above set amounts will be disturbed, DEP has to be notified, normally at least 10 working days ahead; for unplanned emergency work, the notice can follow by the next working day. Raise this early, because it can affect how fast removal starts.
Services
Ceiling Tiles and Drop Ceilings in Fort Myers Offices and Stores
Wet acoustic tiles sag and stain and are usually replaced, but the bigger concern is what's above them: insulation, ductwork, wiring and the roof deck or floor above. A wet tile is a sign to find the source above it. See ceiling leak water damage .
Services
Fire Sprinkler Water Damage in Lee County Buildings
Water from sprinkler piping has usually sat in the lines for years, so it's often dark, oily and foul-smelling, and it's handled as contaminated water, not clean water. Wet ceiling tiles, insulation and carpet it reaches usually come out. The sprinkler contractor restores the system, and your alarm monitoring company and insurer need to know right away.
Services
Storm and Flood Damage to Fort Myers Commercial Property
Many Lee County businesses deal with both roof leaks and rising water after a hurricane. Wind-driven rain through a damaged roof is usually handled under the property policy; rising water and storm surge usually need flood coverage. See flood and storm cleanup .
Services
Landlords, Tenants and Property Managers in Lee County
Commercial leases usually say who's responsible for the building, the build-out and the contents. As a general rule, the landlord handles the structure and systems, and the tenant handles improvements, contents and inventory. In strip plazas, water from the unit next door or a shared roof adds another party. Everyone should document everything, notify each other quickly and agree on who calls for drying.
Services
Condo and HOA Buildings in Lee County
In a residential condo, Florida Statute 718.111(11) generally puts the building and common elements on the association's policy and the finishes inside each unit on the owner's. Property managers can call for common areas, risers and several units at once, and drying logs can be split by unit for each insurer. See condo water damage .
Services

Can work be scheduled so we can stay open?

How long does commercial drying take?
Clean-water drying usually takes about 3 to 5 days. Larger buildings, contaminated water and flooring removal take longer.
Is business interruption covered for water damage?
Only if your policy includes it and the loss is covered. Keep records of lost days and income in case it applies.
What should a restaurant do after a leak or sewage backup?
Stop service in affected areas, keep staff out of contaminated water, photograph everything and call. Food areas affected by contaminated water must be cleaned and sanitized, and a sewage backup can mean a state inspection before you reopen.
Do we need an asbestos inspection before wet drywall comes out?
In commercial buildings and apartment buildings with more than four units, Florida's asbestos rules call for one before materials are disturbed, whatever the building's age. Ask about it on the first call so it doesn't hold up drying.
What should we do if our fire sprinklers went off?
Keep people clear, have the sprinkler contractor shut down and restore the system, tell your alarm company and insurer, and start extraction. Sprinkler water is treated as contaminated, so soaked porous materials usually come out.

Yes. Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, and say when the next guests arrive so the work can be planned.

Yes. Property managers and associations can call for common areas, units and commercial spaces across Lee County .

Water Damage in North Fort Myers Right Now? Do This First
Shut off the water at the fixture or the main. In a manufactured home, check under the home near where the supply line comes in. On a well, switch off the pump at its breaker.

What Makes Water Damage Different in North Fort Myers?
Manufactured homes. Particle board or OSB decking, insulation in the floor system and a belly wrap underneath. Water soaks into the floor and gets trapped in the belly.
The Caloosahatchee and its creeks. North Fort Myers runs along the river's north bank. During hurricanes, surge and high water push up the river and into creeks such as Hancock Creek and Daughtrey's Creek, reaching low-lying streets.
Wells and septic. Larger-lot neighborhoods often have a private well, pressure tank, softener and septic system, each its own source of leaks and backups.
Older slab homes. Some neighborhoods have original plumbing, cast iron drains and aging water heaters. See cast iron pipe water damage .
Seasonal residents. Many homes sit empty part of the year. See water damage in vacant homes .

North Fort Myers ZIP Codes and Neighborhoods
Water damage help covers North Fort Myers ZIP codes 33903 and 33917, including Lochmoor Waterway Estates, Bayshore, Old Bridge Village, Pine Lakes, Lake Fairways, Herons Glen, Sabal Springs, Del Webb Oak Creek, Moody River Estates and Suncoast Estates, from riverfront streets near the Caloosahatchee to larger-lot neighborhoods farther from the river.
Areas
Who Supplies Your Water in North Fort Myers?
North Fort Myers doesn't have one water provider, and knowing yours tells you who to call about a leak at the meter or a backup in the sewer line.
Lee County Utilities serves many unincorporated neighborhoods.
FGUA (Florida Governmental Utility Authority) runs the former North Fort Myers Utility system, which provides sewer and, in some areas, water.
Private wells and septic are common on larger lots, such as in Suncoast Estates.
On a well, a pump that runs when no water is in use, or a pressure tank that keeps cycling, can point to a hidden leak. A septic tank that backs up after heavy rain needs pumping or drain field work before indoor cleanup is finished.
Areas
Manufactured-Home Communities in North Fort Myers: Who Fixes What?
In a land-lease community, where you own the home and rent the lot, Florida Statute 723.022 requires the park owner to keep the utility connections and systems it's responsible for in proper operating condition. Leaks in the home's own plumbing, water heater and floor are usually the homeowner's. Exactly where the line falls is set out in your prospectus and park rules, so check them, tell the community office about a leak at the connection and photograph both sides. Owners on their own land, as in Suncoast Estates, handle everything on the lot.
Areas
Manufactured Homes in North Fort Myers: Where Does the Water Go?
The floor decking, which swells and goes soft, often near the water heater, toilet, kitchen sink or washer.
The insulation in the floor system, which holds water against the decking and framing.
The belly wrap, the bottom board under the home, which can fill with water and sag.
Drying usually means opening the belly, removing wet insulation and replacing damaged decking, not just running fans inside.
Areas
Flooding Along the Caloosahatchee in North Fort Myers
When rising water reaches a home, it's floodwater, Category 3, even if it looks clear. Wet drywall, insulation, carpet and particle board usually come out before drying. In manufactured homes, floodwater fills the belly and soaks the floor system from below. Flood damage is handled by a flood policy, not standard homeowners insurance, and new flood policies usually have a 30-day waiting period. On a well, have the water tested before drinking it after a flood.
Areas
Seasonal and 55+ Communities in North Fort Myers
Before leaving for the summer, shut off the main water (or the well pump) and the water heater, set the AC to control humidity and arrange regular checks. After a storm, have someone look at the home as soon as it's safe. If your community office requires notice of contractor work, have your lot number ready when you call.

Permits and the 50% Rule in North Fort Myers
North Fort Myers is unincorporated, so permits for repairs, and the 50% rule for homes in a flood zone, go through Lee County's building department, not a city. Under that rule, if repairs reach half the building's market value, the home has to be brought up to current flood standards. Keep photos and invoices for every repair. Questions About Water Damage in North Fort Myers
Is there 24-hour water damage help in North Fort Myers?

Who fixes a leak at my lot's water connection in a land-lease community?
Usually the park owner, if the connection is one the park is responsible for under its prospectus; Florida's Mobile Home Act requires park owners to keep those connections working. Leaks inside the home are usually yours. Tell the office and photograph where the water is coming from.
Do you work in manufactured-home and 55+ communities?
Yes. Let your community office know about the work if they require it, and have your lot number ready when you call.
Is Caloosahatchee or creek flooding covered by homeowners insurance?
No. Rising water from the river, a creek or storm surge is flood damage, handled by a flood policy.
Is my North Fort Myers home on county water or a well?
Check your water bill: Lee County Utilities or FGUA means a public system. No water bill usually means a private well, and often a septic tank too.
Who handles permits for water damage repairs in North Fort Myers?
Lee County's building department, because North Fort Myers is unincorporated. It also decides whether the 50% rule applies to a home in a flood zone.

What Makes Water Damage Different on Fort Myers Beach?
Storm surge. Estero Island sits low between the Gulf and Estero Bay, so water can come from the beach side and the back bay. Porous materials surge touches usually have to go.
Elevated rebuilds. Many homes and businesses now sit above ground-level parking, storage or entry areas that are built to flood.
Vacation rentals. Leaks from AC drains, water heaters, toilets and washers can sit between bookings.
Condos. Mid-rise and high-rise buildings mean a leak can travel to several units below.
Salt air. Corrosion wears on fittings, water heaters and AC parts faster than it does inland.

Areas
Fort Myers Beach ZIP Code and Where the Town Ends
Fort Myers Beach is ZIP code 33931, covering Estero Island from the north end near the Matanzas Pass Bridge to the south end near Big Carlos Pass; 33932 is used for post office boxes. San Carlos Island, across Matanzas Pass, shares the Fort Myers Beach mailing address but isn't part of the Town, so permits and flood decisions there go through Lee County.
Areas
Who Supplies Water and Sewer on Fort Myers Beach?
Inside town limits, the Town of Fort Myers Beach runs the water lines and buys its treated water in bulk from Lee County Utilities. Lee County owns and runs the sewer system. That matters after a leak: a problem at the meter or in the street goes to the Town's utilities department, a backup in the public sewer goes to Lee County, and pipes inside your home are yours.
Areas
The 50% Rule on Fort Myers Beach
The Town of Fort Myers Beach decides when the 50% rule applies on Estero Island. If repairs reach half of the building's market value before the damage, the building has to be brought up to current floodplain standards, which often means elevation. The Town asks for a repair or improvement form listing the work on jobs of $2,500 or more. Keep detailed photos and invoices, and talk to the Town's building services staff before major work starts.
Areas
Ground-Level Enclosures Under Elevated Fort Myers Beach Homes
Many rebuilt island homes have ground-level enclosures for parking, storage and entry. These areas are built to flood, and NFIP flood coverage for an elevated, newer home in a high-risk zone is limited below the lowest elevated floor to a specific list of items, such as:
Foundation walls, anchorage and staircases attached to the building
Central air conditioners, water heaters and heat pumps, with the utility connections they need
As contents, clothes washers and dryers, and food freezers with the food in them
Finished walls, flooring and most belongings stored in the enclosure aren't on that list. Keep valuables and electronics out of these spaces, and read what your flood policy says about the area below the lowest elevated floor.
Areas
Condos on Fort Myers Beach
In island condos, a leak in one unit can reach several floors below. Florida Statute 718.111(11) generally puts the building and common elements on the association's policy and the finishes inside each unit on the owner's HO-6. Ask the association how the building's flood policy treats ground-level areas, and report every leak to management right away.
Areas
Vacation Rental Water Damage on Fort Myers Beach
Have your manager or cleaner check for water, smells and AC problems at every turnover.
Keep the AC on and set to control humidity between bookings.
Install leak alarms or automatic shut-off valves where practical.
Document everything before cleanup if you need to file a claim.
For rentals run as a business, see commercial water damage .
Areas
After a Storm: Getting Back to Fort Myers Beach
Follow official re-entry rules from the Town of Fort Myers Beach and Lee County.
Bring boots, gloves, N95 masks, a flashlight and a phone charger.
Don't turn the power on until an electrician says the panel and wiring are safe.
Photograph everything first, including the water line, before mucking out.
Keep receipts for supplies, hotels and emergency work.
Call early; demand across the island and the county is high after a major storm.

Questions About Water Damage on Fort Myers Beach
Is there 24-hour water damage help on Fort Myers Beach?
Yes. Call 239-356-3708 , answered 24/7, for water damage anywhere on Fort Myers Beach and San Carlos Island.
Does flood insurance cover the enclosure under my elevated home?
Only partly. For an elevated, newer home in a high-risk flood zone, NFIP coverage below the lowest elevated floor is limited to a list of items such as the foundation, attached stairs, central AC, water heaters, washers, dryers and food freezers. Finished walls, flooring and most stored belongings aren't covered there.
What is the 50% rule on Fort Myers Beach?
If repairs to a damaged building in a flood zone reach 50% or more of its market value, it usually has to meet current flood rules, often meaning elevation. The Town makes that decision and asks for a repair or improvement form on jobs of $2,500 or more.
Is San Carlos Island part of the Town of Fort Myers Beach?
No. San Carlos Island uses a Fort Myers Beach address, but it's in unincorporated Lee County, so permits and flood decisions go through Lee County, not the Town.
Who handles a sewer backup on Fort Myers Beach?
Lee County runs the public sewer, so a backup in the main line goes to Lee County Utilities. Drain lines inside your home are yours. Either way, sewage inside is Category 3 and needs cleanup.
My rental guests found water in the unit. What now?
Shut off the water, move guests if the unit isn't safe or usable, photograph everything and call. Let your manager and insurer know.
Can I go back to the island right after a hurricane?
Only after officials allow re-entry. Keep the power off until an electrician checks it, and wear protective gear around floodwater.
How do I protect my rental from leaks between guests?
Have the cleaner check under sinks, around the water heater and in the AC closet at each turnover, keep the AC running and consider leak alarms or an automatic shut-off valve.
Do you also cover Estero and Fort Myers?
Yes. See water damage restoration in Estero , Fort Myers and all service areas .

Estero ZIP Code and Communities
Estero is ZIP code 33928, between Fort Myers to the north and Bonita Springs to the south. Water damage help covers the whole village, including The Brooks, Pelican Sound, Grandezza, Wildcat Run, Copperleaf, Stoneybrook, Corkscrew Shores, West Bay Club, Bella Terra and the Villages at Country Creek, from Estero Bay and the Estero River east past I-75.
Areas
Who Supplies Water and Sewer in Estero?
Estero doesn't have one utility. Depending on the neighborhood, water and sewer come from Lee County Utilities or from Bonita Springs Utilities, a member-owned, not-for-profit cooperative that also serves Bonita Springs and unincorporated south Lee County. Some older neighborhoods near the Estero River are still on septic, and the Village has a septic-to-sewer program for them. Your bill tells you who to call about a leak at the meter or a backup in the public line.
Areas
Condo or HOA? Why It Matters for Estero Coach Homes and Villas
Coach homes and villas can look alike and still be set up differently. Some are legally condominiums, where Florida Statute 718.111(11) sets the default split: the association's policy generally covers the building and common elements, and your HO-6 covers your interior finishes, improvements and belongings. Others are homes in a homeowners' association, where that condo statute doesn't apply and your declaration decides who insures the roof and outside walls. Your documents or management can tell you which you have.
Areas
Condo Leaks in Estero: Who Pays?
The association's master policy usually covers the building structure and common elements.
Your HO-6 policy usually covers your interior finishes, improvements and belongings.
The cause and your condo documents decide the details, and negligence can shift responsibility.
Read your declaration, talk to your insurer and start drying while it's sorted out.
Areas
Coach Homes, Villas and Shared Walls in Estero
Coach homes and villas often share a roof, walls or floors with a neighbor. A leak in one home can show up in the other first. If water appears on a shared wall or ceiling, contact your neighbor and the association quickly, shut off your own water if the source is unclear and photograph both sides if you can.

Preventing Summer Damage in Estero Seasonal Homes
Shut off the main water and the water heater before you leave.
Set the AC to control humidity rather than turning it off.
Have the AC drain line cleared before summer.
Arrange regular checks by a home watch service, neighbor or property manager.
Install leak alarms or a smart shut-off valve that alerts your phone.
Leave interior doors open so air moves through the house.
Areas
Estero River Flooding
When rising water from the river or heavy rain reaches a home, it's floodwater, Category 3, even if it looks clear. Wet drywall, insulation, carpet and particle board usually come out before drying. Rising water needs a flood policy, not a standard homeowners policy, and new flood policies usually have a 30-day waiting period. When homes in a flood zone are rebuilt or substantially improved, the Village requires them to sit at least one foot above the base flood elevation.
Areas
Permits and the 50% Rule in Estero
The Village of Estero, not Lee County, issues building permits and makes 50% rule decisions inside the village. Substantial damage counts flood, wind, fire or other damage, so it can apply even when the repairs aren't flood-related. Expect to provide photos from before and after the damage and a market value, from an independent appraisal or the Lee County Property Appraiser.

## Water Damage Restoration Process Fort Myers | Step by Step
https://fortmyerswaterdamagerestoration.us/how-it-works/

Emergency Service · Answered 24/7
How Water Damage Restoration Works in Fort Myers
Water on the floor and no idea what happens next? Most people have never dealt with water damage before, and not knowing is half the stress. Here is exactly how water damage restoration works in Fort Myers, from the first call to the final dry reading, so there are no surprises.
Call 239-356-3708
Answered 24/7 · Moisture readings logged · Written scope before rebuild
Read the intro ↓
Home
»
How Water Damage Restoration Works in Fort Myers
Answered 24/7 · Call 239-356-3708
You call and describe the water, and get help making it safe while you wait. At the inspection, the wet area is measured and you get a written scope. Water is extracted, materials that can't be saved come out and the structure is dried with daily readings. You get the photos and logs, and you choose who does the repairs.
Stage What happens
The call A few quick questions and help shutting off the water
Inspection Source confirmed, water category set, moisture measured and mapped
Written scope What comes out, what equipment runs, the price and what isn't included
Extraction and removal Usually the first day
Drying About 3 to 5 days for clean water, with readings logged daily
Paperwork Photos, moisture map, drying logs and a list of removed materials
Repairs Your decision, with whoever you choose
Guide
Water Damage Restoration in Fort Myers, Step by Step
1 One short phone call You call
When you call 239-356-3708 , you'll be asked a few quick questions:
Your address and ZIP code
What happened and when you found it
Where the water came from: a supply line, appliance, AC, toilet, drain, roof or flooding
Which rooms are wet and roughly how big the wet area is
Whether the water and power are off
Whether you own or rent, and whether it's a condo or a gated community
Your insurance company, if you plan to file a claim
If the water is still running, you'll be walked through shutting it off. Timing is confirmed with you before anyone heads out.
2 While you wait
Shut off the water at the fixture or the main. On a private well, switch off the pump too.
Cut power at the breaker to wet rooms.
Photograph and video everything before you move or throw anything away.
Move belongings off wet floors.
Keep the AC running to help pull moisture out of the air, unless it's the source or the water is sewage or floodwater.
3 Usually at the first visit The inspection
The source is confirmed stopped, or you're told who needs to fix it: a plumber, roofer or HVAC technician.
The water category is identified: clean (Category 1), gray (Category 2) or contaminated, such as sewage or floodwater (Category 3). This decides what can be dried and what has to be removed.
Moisture is measured in floors, walls, cabinets and ceilings with moisture meters and a thermal camera.
The wet area is mapped; it's usually bigger than what you can see.
Findings are explained in plain language, and you can see the readings.
4 Usually at the first visit The written scope
Before work beyond emergency water removal, you get the scope in writing. It should explain:
What will be removed and why
What equipment will be used and for about how long
The price, based on square footage, water category, materials and drying days
What isn't included, such as plumbing repairs or rebuilding
If more water is found during drying, such as inside a wall, the scope is updated in writing with photos and readings. For general background on what moves the price, see the water damage pricing guide .
5 Usually the first day Water removal
Standing water is pulled out with truck-mounted or portable extractors. Extraction removes far more water than drying ever could, which shortens drying and limits damage.
6 Usually the first day Removing what can't be saved
Carpet pad soaked with water
Baseboards that have swelled
The lower part of drywall when it's soaked, contaminated or hiding water
Wet insulation inside walls or ceilings
Particle board cabinet bases and shelves that have swelled
Vinyl plank or laminate trapping water against the slab
Everything removed is photographed and listed for your records and your insurer.
7 About 3 to 5 days Drying
Dehumidifiers and air movers are set up to dry the structure. Moisture readings are taken and logged, and equipment is moved as areas dry. Most clean-water jobs take about 3 to 5 days; floodwater, sewage, concrete slabs and long-running leaks take longer. See structural drying .
During drying:
Equipment runs around the clock and makes noise.
Keep doors and windows closed unless told otherwise.
Keep the AC running.
Don't turn equipment off without asking.
8 Final readings and paperwork
When readings show materials are back to normal, drying is done. You receive:
Photos from before, during and after
The moisture map and drying logs
A list of materials removed
A final invoice that matches the written scope, or explains any changes
These are the records an insurance adjuster usually wants to see.
9 Repairs
After drying, drywall, baseboards, flooring and cabinets are rebuilt. Rebuilding is your decision, and you choose who does it.
Guide
Why Fort Myers Humidity Changes the Drying Plan
Outdoor air in Southwest Florida is humid for much of the year, so opening windows usually slows drying instead of helping it. That's why doors and windows stay closed, the AC keeps running and dehumidifiers do the heavy lifting. It's also why a leak left for a few days here can lead to mold faster than in drier climates.
Guide
What Changes for Fort Myers Condos, Rentals and Businesses
Condos: building management is told right away, and units above or below may need readings too. See condo water damage .
Rentals: the landlord or property manager is part of the plan from the first call.
Gated communities: gate access is arranged before anyone heads out.
Businesses: drying can often be sectioned around your hours. See commercial water damage .
Guide
What You Won't Be Asked to Do in Your Fort Myers Home
Sign over your insurance benefits. For Florida residential policies issued on or after January 1, 2023, post-loss assignment of benefits isn't allowed.
Pay for work you didn't agree to in writing.
Decide on the spot about rebuilding.
Guide
Mitigation, Restoration, Remediation: Words You'll Hear From Fort Myers Adjusters
You'll hear these words from adjusters and contractors, and they often appear as separate parts of an estimate or a claim.
Mitigation: the emergency work that stops the damage getting worse. Water removal, taking out what can't be saved, and drying.
Restoration: putting the home back. New drywall, baseboards, flooring, cabinets and paint once the structure is dry.
Remediation: removing a contaminant, usually mold or sewage, inside containment.
Moisture mapping: measuring and recording where the water went, wall by wall and room by room.
Dry standard: the reading that unaffected materials of the same kind show in your home. Drying is finished when the wet materials reach it.
Insurers often handle mitigation and repairs as separate parts of the claim, so ask for separate paperwork for each.
Guide
What the Water Category Means for Your Fort Myers Job
These categories come from the IICRC S500 standard for water damage restoration.
Category Examples What usually happens
Category 1: clean water Burst supply line, water heater, AC condensate caught early Most materials can be dried in place if drying starts quickly
Category 2: gray water Washer or dishwasher drain water, toilet overflow without waste Carpet pad and porous materials often removed; surfaces cleaned and treated
Category 3: contaminated water Sewage, floodwater, storm surge Porous materials removed; surfaces disinfected; protective gear used
A clean leak left for days can become Category 2, which is why starting the same day matters.
Guide
What the Drying Equipment Does in a Fort Myers Home
Air movers blow air across wet surfaces so moisture evaporates faster.
Dehumidifiers pull that moisture out of the air so it doesn't soak back into walls and floors.
Specialty equipment can push dry air into wall cavities, under cabinets and across concrete slabs.
Moisture meters and thermal cameras track progress, so drying ends when readings say it's dry, not when it looks dry.
Guide
How Long Each Stage Takes in Fort Myers
Stage Typical time
Call and questions One short phone call
Inspection and written scope Usually at the first visit
Extraction and removal Usually the first day
Drying About 3 to 5 days for clean water; longer for slabs, floodwater and sewage
Repairs Depends on materials and contractors
Guide
Insurance Paperwork for Fort Myers Water Damage Claims
This is general information, not advice about your policy.
You file the claim with your insurer and deal with your adjuster.
Photos, moisture readings and drying logs from the job support your claim.
You're responsible for your deductible and anything not covered.
Citizens policyholders: Citizens offers its own water removal program for non-weather losses, and its published materials say emergency water mitigation by your own company is limited to $3,000, so ask Citizens before work goes beyond the emergency.
Read how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Guide
Mold After Water Damage in Fort Myers Homes
If mold has already grown, it should be removed by a qualified Florida mold remediation company. Fast drying is the most reliable way to prevent mold in the first place.
Guide
Questions About the Water Damage Restoration Process in Fort Myers
Who will come to my home?
A water damage technician who works in your area. Details and timing are confirmed with you before anyone arrives.
Do I get the price before work starts?
Yes. You get a written scope before work beyond emergency water removal begins.
Do I have to use the same company for repairs?
No. Rebuilding is your decision, and you choose who does it.
Will you deal with my insurance company?
You file and manage your claim. The photos, moisture readings and drying logs from the job are there to support it.
Do I need to be home during drying?
Someone needs to give access for setup and readings. You don't have to be there all day while the equipment runs.
Why does the drying equipment have to run overnight?
Wet materials keep releasing moisture around the clock, and turning equipment off lets the air and the walls take it back up, especially in Fort Myers humidity. Steady drying is what gets the job done in days instead of weeks.
What changes if the water is sewage or floodwater?
More comes out and more cleaning happens. Porous materials the water touched are removed, surfaces are disinfected, protective gear is used, and affected rooms may be closed off until the work is done. See sewage backup cleanup .
What if more damage is found during drying?
The scope is updated in writing and explained, with photos and readings showing what was found.

Before You Call: If Water Is Still Coming Into Your Fort Myers Home
Turn off power at the breaker to wet rooms, if you can reach the panel without standing in water.
Shut off the water at the fixture or the main. On a private well, also turn off the pump.
Photograph everything before you move anything.
The full list: first-hour water damage checklist .

Your address, ZIP code and the best number to reach you
What happened and when you found it
Where the water came from, if you know
Which rooms are wet and roughly how big the area is
Whether the water is clean, from an appliance, or from a toilet, drain or flood
Whether the water and power are off
Condo or gated community: building management contact and gate instructions
Your insurance company, if you plan to file a claim

Calling About a Lee County Home You're Not At
Many calls come from seasonal owners up north, landlords, property managers and family members. If you're not at the home:
Name the person who can open the door: a home watch service, neighbor, property manager or building management.
Have the gate code, lockbox details or front desk contact ready.
Ask whoever is there to shut off the water and send you photos before anything is moved.
Give the best number to reach you for approvals, since you'll get the written scope before work beyond emergency water removal.

Questions About Contacting Fort Myers Water Damage Restoration Pros
Can I get a price over the phone?
Not an exact one. The price depends on how far water spread inside walls and under flooring, which has to be measured on site. For a rough idea, see the water damage pricing guide .
Do you cover my city?
Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Lehigh Acres, North Fort Myers, Fort Myers Beach, Estero and Bonita Springs are covered. If you're nearby and not sure, call and ask.
Should I call my insurer first?
Stop the water and make it safe first, then report the loss to your insurer as soon as you can. See how insurance handles water damage in Florida .
Can I call for a home I'm not at right now?
Yes. Owners, landlords, property managers and family members call for homes all the time. Have someone ready to open the door and the gate or building access details on hand.
I rent my home. Should I call you or my landlord?
Tell your landlord or property manager right away, because Florida law generally makes the landlord responsible for keeping the plumbing in working order and repairs are usually theirs to arrange. Your renters policy covers your belongings.

Water Damage Restoration in Fort Myers
ZIP codes 33901, 33905, 33907, 33908, 33912, 33913, 33916, 33919, 33966 and 33967. Slab homes, AC closet leaks and older cast iron drains are the most common calls. Many homes with a Fort Myers address, including Iona, McGregor, Gateway and San Carlos Park, are in unincorporated Lee County, so Lee County handles their permits. See water damage restoration in Fort Myers .
Water Damage Restoration in Cape Coral
ZIP codes 33904, 33909, 33914, 33990, 33991 and 33993. Canal homes, slab leaks and separate irrigation lines that don't show on your water meter, plus private wells and septic in parts of the north Cape. The City of Cape Coral handles permits and the 50% rule. See water damage restoration in Cape Coral .
Water Damage Restoration in Lehigh Acres
ZIP codes 33936, 33971, 33972, 33973, 33974 and 33976. Many homes run on a private well and septic, so pressure tanks, softeners and septic backups join AC closet and water heater leaks; FGUA provides central water and sewer in some areas. See water damage restoration in Lehigh Acres .
Water Damage Restoration in North Fort Myers
ZIP codes 33903 and 33917. Manufactured-home and 55+ communities, Caloosahatchee and creek flooding, and wells and septic on larger lots such as Suncoast Estates. North Fort Myers is unincorporated, so Lee County handles permits. See water damage restoration in North Fort Myers .
Water Damage Restoration on Fort Myers Beach
ZIP code 33931. Storm surge, enclosures under elevated homes, and condo and vacation rental leaks on Estero Island. The Town of Fort Myers Beach handles permits on the island; San Carlos Island, across Matanzas Pass, is Lee County. See water damage restoration on Fort Myers Beach .
Water Damage Restoration in Estero
ZIP code 33928. Condo and coach home leaks, AC closet overflows, seasonal homes and Estero River flooding in gated communities across the village. The Village of Estero handles permits and the 50% rule. See water damage restoration in Estero .
Water Damage Restoration in Bonita Springs
ZIP codes 34134 and 34135. Imperial River flooding, coastal condos near Bonita Beach and gated communities with seasonal owners. The City of Bonita Springs handles permits, and Bonita Springs Utilities supplies water and sewer. See water damage restoration in Bonita Springs .

How the Guides on This Site Are Written for Lee County Homeowners
The pages on this site are written to help Lee County homeowners make decisions during a stressful situation, whether or not they ever call.
Practical first. Every page starts with what to do right now, then explains why.
Checked against primary sources where rules apply, including Florida Statutes 718.111(11) for condos, 627.70131 and 627.70132 for property claims, 626.9744 for matching, 723.022 for mobile home parks, FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program for flood coverage, and EPA guidance on drying within 24 to 48 hours to limit mold.
Local details checked locally, such as which utility serves an area and which city, town, village or county decides permits and the 50% rule.
Insurance information is general, not advice about your policy.
No invented ratings, testimonials or customer quotes, and no promises about results or timing.
Prices appear only in one place. The pricing guide gives rough Fort Myers and Southwest Florida ranges for a general idea, not quotes; every job is different, so call and ask.
Kept current. If you spot something out of date, call 239-356-3708 and tell us.

Do you fix the leak itself?
